60	#     radius of a remote wipe is larger, not smaller.
61	#   * SQL through a script FILE (`python app.py` that drops a table) was
62	#     never matched and still is not; inline programs are matched by text.
63	#   * `cd "$(mktemp -d)" && rm -rf out` (substitution as the cd target) and
64	#     `rm -rf "$T"` where T came from anything but a plain `$(mktemp -d)`
65	#     or a temp path stay blocked — bind the path first, then rm.
66	#   * The hook never consults its own $PWD: a project checked out under
67	#     /tmp still has `rm -rf src` blocked.
68	#   * Rebinding builtins void the once-bound-variable proof only in command
69	#     position (`read T`, `while read T`, `IFS= read -r T`, `command read`,
70	#     `eval "read T"`); `exec read`, `env … read`, `sudo read`, `nice read`
71	#     are NOT counted — `read` is a builtin, so those forms fail or run in a
72	#     child and cannot rebind the caller's variable. `notes-guard.sh read`
73	#     and `echo read` are arguments, never rebinds.
74	#
75	# Registered in settings.hooks.json as PreToolUse matcher: "Bash"
76	# Part of Loa Harness Engineering (cycle-011, issue #297)
77	# Source: Trail of Bits claude-code-config safety patterns
78	# =============================================================================
79	# perf pass-2 (2026-07-05, skill-loop): fork/exec reduction. The boolean
80	# `echo | grep -qE` pattern dispatches (15 spawns on every benign Bash call)
81	# are replaced by bash [[ =~ ]] via the _match/_match_ci helpers below, which
82	# preserve grep's PER-LINE match model byte-for-byte (see helper comments).
83	# `\b` was translated to explicit POSIX boundary classes because bash =~
84	# compiles with the SYSTEM regex library — glibc supports \b, BSD libc does
85	# NOT, and this hook commits to macOS/BSD (header above). Each translated
86	# pattern carries an equivalence note. Deliberately NOT converted (grep
87	# retained): P10 DELETE-FROM segment extraction (grep -oiE multi-match with
88	# original-case output is not provably reproducible in bash — no match-offset
89	# primitive), the FR-SZ inner write-intent tests (their `X\b[^|;&]*` shapes
90	# make consuming \b-translation non-isomorphic; they only run when the
91	# command already mentions a protected path), and all `grep -oE | head -1`
92	# matched-substring extractions (block path only — the hook exits 2 right
93	# after). Also: stdin now streams straight into the Path-A jq (no cat spawn),
94	# audit timestamps use printf %(...)T (no date spawn), cwd uses $PWD.
95	# =============================================================================
96	# perf pass-8 (2026-07-05, skill-loop): provably-complete literal pre-filters
97	# on the pattern dispatch. After pass 2 the ~95% benign path still paid 13
98	# sequential ERE evaluations (~0.4 ms) plus the one unconditional P10 grep
99	# spawn (~3 ms). Each pattern group is now guarded by a cheap bash substring
100	# test on literal(s) PROVABLY NECESSARY for the group to match: each guard
101	# literal appears in the group's regex as a mandatory concatenation element —
102	# outside every alternation branch, optional (?) group and starred group — so
103	# any MATCHING LINE must contain it verbatim, hence the whole $command must
104	# contain it. Absence from the whole string therefore proves no line can
105	# match, and the group is skipped — outcome-identical by construction.
106	# Where a guard uses an alternation's literals (P6 drop|clear, FR-SZ
107	# .run/|grimoires/loa/skills), the guard tests ALL branch literals and any
108	# hit evaluates the group. Guards only ever SKIP, never accept: when the
109	# literal is present the group evaluates exactly as before, in the original
110	# order (first match still wins, block messages byte-identical).
111	# Case-insensitive groups (P8/P9/P10) guard on the same C-locale ASCII fold
112	# (${command,,}) that _match_ci applies per line and grep -i applies under
113	# the LC_ALL=C pin — folding is per-character and leaves \n untouched, so
114	# the folded whole string is exactly the folded lines joined by \n, and a
115	# literal absent from the folded whole is absent from every folded line.
116	# Per-group necessity proofs sit next to each guard. The P10 DELETE-FROM
117	# grep — the last unconditional spawn on the benign path — now runs only
118	# when the folded command contains both "delete" and "from" (both mandatory
119	# in its -i pattern). The log-redactor stays block-path-only (verified: it
120	# is exec'd only inside emit_block and the FR-SZ bypass audit branch).
121	# =============================================================================
122	
123	# =============================================================================
124	# FR-6 heredoc consumer classifier (cycle-129 D-6.1; knob
125	# destructive_command_guard.heredoc_classifier, default true; false = the
126	# pre-cycle scan, i.e. only the #1245 quoted-cat scrub below).
127	# Defined BEFORE the bash-version guard and the stdin read so another script
128	# can source this file with BDB_LIB_ONLY=1 and call
129	#   _bdb_heredoc_consumer_class <command text>   → prints interpreter|nonexec|none
130	#   heredoc_nonexec <command text>               → exit 0 iff nonexec
131	# Bash 3.2 compatible (no ${x,,}, no mapfile, no associative arrays) and safe
132	# under a caller's `set -u`.
133	#
134	# Grammar (literal command text; no alias or function expansion; CRLF folded
135	# to LF). The command is walked line by line; a line holding an unquoted
136	# `<<` / `<<-` (not `<<<`) is a heredoc header, the body runs to the first
137	# line equal to the delimiter (leading tabs stripped for `<<-`). FULL SCAN
138	# (the whole command as today) on: any other control character, a header the
139	# tokenizer cannot read (open quote, trailing backslash, comment), more than
140	# one heredoc on a header, a delimiter that is not a plain word ('W', "W",
141	# \W or W with W in [A-Za-z0-9_.+:@%-]; `$X` is a variable delimiter), or a
142	# missing terminator. Per heredoc the class is:
143	#   interpreter — body scanned exactly as today: the header holds `$(`, a
144	#     backtick, `<(` or `>(`, a paren or brace group or a shell keyword; it
145	#     continues on the next line (`|`, `&&`, `||` last) or an earlier line
146	#     opened a substitution, group, quote or pipe; a member of the heredoc's
147	#     pipeline is a shell, interpreter, wrapper that runs its argument or SQL
148	#     runner (_bdb_hd_is_interp, _bdb_hd_is_runner); an allowlisted form
149	#     carries an unknown or exec-shaped flag (-c, -e, -x clusters, --exec,
150	#     --eval, --command, in-place); a write target is executable content
151	#     (_bdb_hd_exec_dest: script extension, .claude/hooks, .claude/settings*
152	#     .json, .git/hooks, .git/config, rc/profile files, /etc, a bin dir or a
153	#     directory on PATH, or any non-literal path); the first body line is a
154	#     shebang; the body holds `<<` (nested); a target's basename appears
155	#     elsewhere in the command outside the safe readers (_bdb_hd_same_line_exec:
156	#     `bash x`, `./x`, `source x`, `. x`, `chmod +x x`, `exec x`, cp/mv …).
157	#   nonexec — every pipeline member is an exact allowlisted form
158	#     (_bdb_hd_member): cat, tee, printf, echo with plain-file or stdout sinks;
159	#     gh pr|issue comment -F -; gh pr create --body-file -; git commit -F -;
160	#     br create|update reading `-`; jq/yq without in-place; grep; sed -n with
161	#     a print-only script; sort; wc. The body is then scanned PER SEGMENT
162	#     (_bdb_hd_scan_body): each line split on ; && || | &, wrapper prefixes
163	#     stripped (sudo command exec env nice time nohup builtin stdbuf ionice,
164	#     a leading backslash, quote, paren or brace, assignments, an absolute
165	#     path); a segment whose command word is a fence verb (rm git find dd
166	#     mkfs* shred truncate kubectl terraform aws gcloud psql mysql DROP
167	#     DELETE TRUNCATE) is kept on its own line for the normal rules, other
168	#     segments are dropped. The body falls back to a full scan when it holds
169	#     `$(`, a backtick, `<(` or `>(` under an unquoted delimiter, or a segment
170	#     word is an interpreter or wrapper, or a variable (`$x -rf /`; such a
171	#     segment is ALSO scanned as rm, git and kubectl with the same arguments).
172	#     Special case (the #1245 scrub): a standalone quoted-delimiter `cat`
173	#     whose header is exactly `cat <<'W' [> path]` drops the whole body.
174	#   none — the consumer is on neither list: full scan.
175	# Documented gap: a body written to a plain file by one command and executed
176	# by a LATER command is outside a per-command fence (the Write tool shares it).
177	# =============================================================================
178	_bdb_hd_op_re='^[0-9]*(<<<|<<-|&>>|<<|>>|>[|]|&&|[|][|]|[|]&|&>|<>|>&[0-9-]*|<&[0-9-]*|;;|;|&|[|]|<|>|[(]|[)])$'
179	_bdb_hd_re_dw='^[A-Za-z0-9_.+:@%-]+$'
180	_bdb_hd_re_dsq="^'([A-Za-z0-9_.+:@%-]+)'\$"
181	_bdb_hd_re_ddq='^"([A-Za-z0-9_.+:@%-]+)"$'
182	_bdb_hd_re_dbs='^\\([A-Za-z0-9_.+:@%-]+)$'
183	_bdb_hd_re_psq="^'([^']*)'\$"
184	_bdb_hd_re_pdq="^\"([^\"\$\`\\\\]*)\"\$"
185	_bdb_hd_re_pbare="^[^'\"\$\`\\\\]+\$"
186	_bdb_hd_re_ctl=$'[\x01-\x08\x0b-\x1f\x7f]'
187	_bdb_hd_re_exflag='^-[A-Za-z]*[cex][A-Za-z]*$'
188	_bdb_hd_re_exlong='^--(exec|eval|command|in-?place)'
189	_bdb_hd_re_ext='\.(sh|bash|zsh|ksh|csh|fish|py|pyw|rb|pl|pm|js|mjs|cjs|ts|mts|cts|ps1|psm1|php|lua|tcl|command|bat|cmd)$'
190	_bdb_hd_re_sys='(^|/)(\.claude/hooks(/|$)|\.claude/settings[^/]*\.json$|\.git/hooks(/|$)|\.git/config$|\.gitconfig$|\.ssh/rc$|\.config/(fish|zsh|bash|git)/|s?bin/[^/]+$)'
191	_bdb_hd_re_rc='(^|/)\.(bashrc|bash_profile|bash_login|bash_logout|profile|zshrc|zshenv|zprofile|zlogin|zlogout|kshrc|mkshrc|cshrc|tcshrc|login|logout|envrc)$'
192	_bdb_hd_re_sedp='^(([0-9]+|[$]|/[^/]*/)(,([0-9]+|[$]|/[^/]*/))?)?p$'
193	_bdb_hd_re_assign='^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*='
194	_bdb_hd_re_varw='^[$]([{]|[A-Za-z_])'
195	_bdb_hd_re_knob='^[[:space:]]+heredoc_classifier:[[:space:]]*["'"'"']?([A-Za-z]+)["'"'"']?[[:space:]]*(#.*)?$'
196	
197	# Shells, interpreters and wrappers that run their argument or stdin.
198	_bdb_hd_is_interp() {
199	  case "$1" in
200	    bash|sh|zsh|dash|ksh|mksh|ash|fish|csh|tcsh|busybox|python|python[0-9]*|pypy*|node|nodejs|deno|bun|ruby|irb|perl|php|lua|luajit|tclsh|wish|expect|pwsh|powershell|osascript|Rscript) return 0 ;;
201	    eval|source|.|exec|command|builtin|time|awk|gawk|mawk|nawk|make|gmake|m4|ed|ex|vi|vim|nvim|gdb) return 0 ;;
202	    sudo|doas|su|runuser|env|xargs|parallel|timeout|nohup|nice|ionice|setsid|stdbuf|chroot|unshare|nsenter|ssh|docker|podman|kubectl|find|watch|script) return 0 ;;
203	  esac
204	  return 1
205	}
206	# The SQL runners of the FR-1.4/5/6 precondition (same list).
207	_bdb_hd_is_runner() {
208	  case "$1" in
209	    psql|pgcli|mysql|mariadb|mysqlsh|sqlite3|sqlcmd|sqlplus|isql|usql|litecli|duckdb|clickhouse|clickhouse-client|cockroach|bq|wrangler|prisma|supabase|drizzle-kit|knex|sequelize|typeorm|flyway|liquibase|dbmate|goose|sqitch|rails|manage.py|artisan|alembic|dbt|atlas|mongosh|sqlx) return 0 ;;
210	  esac
211	  return 1
212	}
213	# Command words the fence's own rules match.
214	_bdb_hd_is_destructive() {
215	  case "$1" in
216	    rm|git|find|dd|shred|truncate|kubectl|terraform|aws|gcloud|psql|mysql|mkfs|mkfs.*) return 0 ;;
217	    [Dd][Rr][Oo][Pp]|[Dd][Ee][Ll][Ee][Tt][Ee]|[Tt][Rr][Uu][Nn][Cc][Aa][Tt][Ee]) return 0 ;;
218	  esac
219	  return 1
220	}
221	# Readers that may name a heredoc's target elsewhere on the line.
222	_bdb_hd_is_safe_reader() {
223	  case "$1" in
224	    cat|ls|wc|head|tail|grep|egrep|fgrep|rg|diff|cmp|stat|file|test|'['|echo|printf|sort|uniq|jq|yq|git|gh|br|mkdir|touch|realpath|readlink|basename|dirname|du|md5sum|sha1sum|sha256sum|shasum|b2sum|cksum) return 0 ;;
225	  esac
226	  return 1
227	}
228	
229	# _bdb_hd_tokenize <line> → _bdb_hd_tok[] (words keep their quotes; operators
230	# are separate tokens, an fd number joins its redirect). Returns 1 when the
231	# line cannot be read: open quote, trailing backslash, unquoted comment.
232	_bdb_hd_tokenize() {
233	  local s="${1:-}" n i=0 ch tok="" q="" have=0 op cand
234	  n=${#s}
235	  _bdb_hd_tok=()
236	  while (( i < n )); do
237	    ch="${s:i:1}"
238	    if [[ -n "$q" ]]; then
239	      tok="$tok$ch"
240	      if [[ "$q" == "'" ]]; then
241	        [[ "$ch" == "'" ]] && q=""
242	      elif [[ "$ch" == '\' ]]; then
243	        (( i + 1 < n )) || return 1
244	        i=$((i + 1)); tok="$tok${s:i:1}"
245	      elif [[ "$ch" == '"' ]]; then
246	        q=""
247	      fi
248	      i=$((i + 1)); continue
249	    fi
250	    case "$ch" in
251	      "'"|'"') q="$ch"; tok="$tok$ch"; have=1; i=$((i + 1)) ;;
252	      '\')
253	        (( i + 1 < n )) || return 1
254	        tok="$tok$ch${s:i+1:1}"; have=1; i=$((i + 2)) ;;
255	      ' '|$'\t')
256	        if (( have )); then _bdb_hd_tok[${#_bdb_hd_tok[@]}]="$tok"; tok=""; have=0; fi
257	        i=$((i + 1)) ;;
258	      '#')
259	        (( have )) || return 1
260	        tok="$tok$ch"; i=$((i + 1)) ;;
261	      ';'|'&'|'|'|'<'|'>'|'('|')')
262	        op=""
263	        for cand in '<<<' '<<-' '&>>' '<<' '>>' '>|' '&&' '||' '|&' '&>' '<>' '>&' '<&' ';;' ';' '&' '|' '<' '>' '(' ')'; do
264	          if [[ "${s:i:${#cand}}" == "$cand" ]]; then op="$cand"; break; fi
265	        done
266	        i=$((i + ${#op}))
267	        if [[ "$op" == '>&' || "$op" == '<&' ]]; then
268	          while (( i < n )) && [[ "${s:i:1}" == [0-9-] ]]; do op="$op${s:i:1}"; i=$((i + 1)); done
269	        fi
270	        if (( have )); then
271	          if [[ "$tok" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] && [[ "$op" == '<'* || "$op" == '>'* ]]; then
272	            op="$tok$op"
273	          else
274	            _bdb_hd_tok[${#_bdb_hd_tok[@]}]="$tok"
275	          fi
276	          tok=""; have=0
277	        fi
278	        _bdb_hd_tok[${#_bdb_hd_tok[@]}]="$op" ;;
279	      *) tok="$tok$ch"; have=1; i=$((i + 1)) ;;
280	    esac
281	  done
282	  [[ -z "$q" ]] || return 1
283	  (( have )) && _bdb_hd_tok[${#_bdb_hd_tok[@]}]="$tok"
284	  return 0
285	}
286	
287	# _bdb_hd_unq_path <word> → _hd_up; returns 1 for a non-literal path (an
288	# expansion, an escape, mixed quoting) or an empty one.
289	_bdb_hd_unq_path() {
290	  _hd_up=""
291	  if [[ "${1:-}" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_psq ]] || [[ "${1:-}" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_pdq ]]; then
292	    _hd_up="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
293	  elif [[ "${1:-}" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_pbare ]]; then
294	    _hd_up="$1"
295	  else
296	    return 1
297	  fi
298	  [[ -n "$_hd_up" ]]
299	}
300	
301	# _bdb_hd_exec_dest <unquoted path> → 0 when a write there is executable
302	# content (or cannot be judged).
303	_bdb_hd_exec_dest() {
304	  local p="${1:-}" d e b old_ifs
305	  case "$p" in
306	    *'*'*|*'?'*|*'['*|*'{'*|'~'|'~'[!/]*|'') return 0 ;;
307	  esac
308	  [[ "$p" == '~/'* ]] && p="${HOME:-}/${p#'~/'}"
309	  b="${p##*/}"
310	  [[ "$b" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_ext ]] && return 0
311	  [[ "$p" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_sys || "$p" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_rc ]] && return 0
312	  [[ "$p" == /etc/* ]] && return 0
313	  if [[ "$p" == /* ]]; then d="${p%/*}"; [[ -n "$d" ]] || d="/"
314	  elif [[ "$p" == */* ]]; then d="${PWD:-.}/${p%/*}"
315	  else d="${PWD:-.}"
316	  fi
317	  old_ifs="$IFS"; IFS=':'
318	  for e in ${PATH:-}; do
319	    [[ -z "$e" || "$e" == "." ]] && e="${PWD:-.}"
320	    [[ "$e" != "/" ]] && e="${e%/}"
321	    if [[ "$d" == "$e" ]]; then IFS="$old_ifs"; return 0; fi
322	  done
323	  IFS="$old_ifs"
324	  return 1
325	}
326	
327	# _bdb_hd_member <tokens…> → _hd_mcls (interpreter|nonexec|none) for one
328	# pipeline member; write targets are appended to _hd_dests.
329	_bdb_hd_member() {
330	  local -a toks argv
331	  local t nxt i n stdout_files=0 a0 base fd stdin=0 ops=0 want="" has_n=0 script=""
332	  toks=("$@"); n=${#toks[@]}; argv=()
333	  _hd_mcls=none
334	  for ((i = 0; i < n; i++)); do
335	    t="${toks[i]}"
336	    if [[ "$t" =~ $_bdb_hd_op_re ]]; then
337	      case "$t" in
338	        *'<<<') return ;;
339	        *'<<'|*'<<-') i=$((i + 1)); continue ;;
340	        *'>&'[0-9]*|*'>&-'|*'<&'*) continue ;;
341	        *'>'|*'>>'|*'>|'|*'>&'|'&>'|'&>>')
342	          nxt="${toks[i+1]:-}"; i=$((i + 1))
343	          if [[ -z "$nxt" || "$nxt" =~ $_bdb_hd_op_re ]]; then _hd_mcls=interpreter; return; fi
344	          _bdb_hd_unq_path "$nxt" || { _hd_mcls=interpreter; return; }
345	          case "$_hd_up" in /dev/null|/dev/stdout|/dev/stderr) continue ;; esac
346	          _hd_dests[${#_hd_dests[@]}]="$_hd_up"
347	          fd="${t%%[>&]*}"
348	          [[ -z "$fd" || "$fd" == 1 || "$t" == '&>'* || "$t" == '>&' ]] && stdout_files=$((stdout_files + 1))
349	          continue ;;
350	        *) return ;;
351	      esac
352	    fi
353	    argv[${#argv[@]}]="$t"
354	  done
355	  (( ${#argv[@]} > 0 )) || return
356	  a0="${argv[0]}"
357	  base="${a0#\\}"; base="${base##*/}"
358	  if _bdb_hd_is_interp "$base" || _bdb_hd_is_runner "$base"; then _hd_mcls=interpreter; return; fi
359	  [[ "$a0" =~ ^[a-z][a-z0-9]*$ ]] || return
360	  (( stdout_files <= 1 )) || return
361	  for ((i = 1; i < ${#argv[@]}; i++)); do
362	    t="${argv[i]}"
363	    if [[ "$t" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_exflag || "$t" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_exlong ]]; then _hd_mcls=interpreter; return; fi
364	  done
365	  case "$a0" in
366	    cat)
367	      for ((i = 1; i < ${#argv[@]}; i++)); do [[ "${argv[i]}" == "-" ]] || { _hd_mcls=interpreter; return; }; done ;;
368	    tee)
369	      for ((i = 1; i < ${#argv[@]}; i++)); do
370	        t="${argv[i]}"
371	        case "$t" in
372	          -a|--append|-p) ;;
373	          -*) _hd_mcls=interpreter; return ;;
374	          *) _bdb_hd_unq_path "$t" || { _hd_mcls=interpreter; return; }
375	             _hd_dests[${#_hd_dests[@]}]="$_hd_up" ;;
376	        esac
377	      done ;;
378	    echo|printf)
379	      for ((i = 1; i < ${#argv[@]}; i++)); do
380	        case "${argv[i]}" in -n|-E) ;; -*) _hd_mcls=interpreter; return ;; esac
381	      done ;;
382	    gh)
383	      case "${argv[1]:-} ${argv[2]:-}" in
384	        "pr comment"|"issue comment") want=" -F --body-file -R --repo |" ;;
385	        "pr create") want=" -F --body-file --title -t --base -B --head -H --repo -R --label -l --reviewer -r --assignee -a --milestone -m --project -p --template -T | --draft -d --fill --fill-first --fill-verbose --no-maintainer-edit --dry-run " ;;
386	        *) return ;;
387	      esac
388	      for ((i = 3; i < ${#argv[@]}; i++)); do
389	        t="${argv[i]}"
390	        case "$t" in
391	          --body-file=-) stdin=1 ;;
392	          --*=*) [[ "${want%%|*}" == *" ${t%%=*} "* ]] || { _hd_mcls=interpreter; return; } ;;
393	          -*)
394	            if [[ "${want%%|*}" == *" $t "* ]]; then
395	              i=$((i + 1))
396	              [[ ( "$t" == "-F" || "$t" == "--body-file" ) && "${argv[i]:-}" == "-" ]] && stdin=1
397	            elif [[ "${want#*|}" != *" $t "* ]]; then
398	              _hd_mcls=interpreter; return
399	            fi ;;
400	          *) ops=$((ops + 1)); [[ "${argv[2]}" == comment && $ops -le 1 ]] || { _hd_mcls=interpreter; return; } ;;
401	        esac
402	      done
403	      (( stdin )) || { _hd_mcls=interpreter; return; } ;;
404	    git)
405	      [[ "${argv[1]:-}" == commit ]] || return
406	      for ((i = 2; i < ${#argv[@]}; i++)); do
407	        t="${argv[i]}"
408	        case "$t" in
409	          -F|--file) i=$((i + 1)); [[ "${argv[i]:-}" == "-" ]] || { _hd_mcls=interpreter; return; }; stdin=1 ;;
410	          --file=-|-F-) stdin=1 ;;
411	          -q|--quiet|-s|--signoff|-a|--all|--allow-empty|--allow-empty-message|-v|--verbose|--no-edit|--amend) ;;
412	          *) _hd_mcls=interpreter; return ;;
413	        esac
414	      done
415	      (( stdin )) || { _hd_mcls=interpreter; return; } ;;
416	    br)
417	      case "${argv[1]:-}" in create|update) ;; *) return ;; esac
418	      for ((i = 2; i < ${#argv[@]}; i++)); do
419	        t="${argv[i]}"
420	        case "$t" in
421	          -d|--description|--body) [[ "${argv[i+1]:-}" == "-" ]] && stdin=1 ;;
422	          -f|--file) [[ "${argv[1]}" == create && "${argv[i+1]:-}" == "-" ]] && stdin=1 ;;
423	          --description=-|--body=-) stdin=1 ;;
424	        esac
425	      done
426	      (( stdin )) || { _hd_mcls=interpreter; return; } ;;
427	    jq|yq)
428	      for ((i = 1; i < ${#argv[@]}; i++)); do
429	        # In-place flags: --inplace/--in-place, -i, -i=…, and any short-flag cluster holding an i
430	        # (corpus D114/D115: `-i` alone did not match `-[A-Za-z]*i*`, which needs a letter before the i).
431	        case "${argv[i]}" in --inplace|--in-place|-i*|-[A-Za-z]*i*) _hd_mcls=interpreter; return ;; esac
432	      done ;;
433	    grep|egrep|fgrep) ;;
434	    sed)
435	      for ((i = 1; i < ${#argv[@]}; i++)); do
436	        t="${argv[i]}"
437	        case "$t" in
438	          -n|--quiet|--silent) has_n=1 ;;
439	          -E|-r|--regexp-extended|-s|--separate|-u|--unbuffered|-z|--null-data) ;;
440	          -*) _hd_mcls=interpreter; return ;;
441	          *) if [[ -z "$script" ]]; then
442	               script="$t"; [[ "$script" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_psq || "$script" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_pdq ]] && script="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
443	               [[ "$script" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_sedp ]] || { _hd_mcls=interpreter; return; }
444	             fi ;;
445	        esac
446	      done
447	      (( has_n )) && [[ -n "$script" ]] || { _hd_mcls=interpreter; return; } ;;
448	    sort)
449	      for ((i = 1; i < ${#argv[@]}; i++)); do
450	        t="${argv[i]}"
451	        case "$t" in
452	          -o) i=$((i + 1)); _bdb_hd_unq_path "${argv[i]:-}" || { _hd_mcls=interpreter; return; }; _hd_dests[${#_hd_dests[@]}]="$_hd_up" ;;
453	          -k|-t) i=$((i + 1)) ;;
454	          -k*|-t*) ;;
455	          --*) _hd_mcls=interpreter; return ;;
456	          -*) [[ "$t" =~ ^-[bdfghiMnRrsuVz]+$ ]] || { _hd_mcls=interpreter; return; } ;;
457	        esac
458	      done ;;
459	    wc)
460	      for ((i = 1; i < ${#argv[@]}; i++)); do
461	        case "${argv[i]}" in -*) [[ "${argv[i]}" =~ ^-[lwmL]+$ ]] || { _hd_mcls=interpreter; return; } ;; esac
462	      done ;;
463	    *) return ;;
464	  esac
465	  _hd_mcls=nonexec
466	}
467	
468	# _bdb_hd_ctx_bad <line> → 0 when a line before (or the header itself) leaves
469	# the next text inside a substitution, group, quote, compound command or
470	# pipeline: a later heredoc there is interpreter-class.
471	_bdb_hd_ctx_bad() {
472	  local l="${1:-}" k last
473	  case "$l" in *'$('*|*'`'*|*'<('*|*'>('*) return 0 ;; esac
474	  _bdb_hd_tokenize "$l" || return 0
475	  for ((k = 0; k < ${#_bdb_hd_tok[@]}; k++)); do
476	    case "${_bdb_hd_tok[k]}" in
477	      '('|')'|'{'|'}'|do|done|then|else|elif|if|fi|while|until|for|case|esac|select|function|coproc) return 0 ;;
478	    esac
479	  done

file.content:
#     radius of a remote wipe is larger, not smaller.
#   * SQL through a script FILE (`python app.py` that drops a table) was
#     never matched and still is not; inline programs are matched by text.
#   * `cd "$(mktemp -d)" && rm -rf out` (substitution as the cd target) and
#     `rm -rf "$T"` where T came from anything but a plain `$(mktemp -d)`
#     or a temp path stay blocked — bind the path first, then rm.
#   * The hook never consults its own $PWD: a project checked out under
#     /tmp still has `rm -rf src` blocked.
#   * Rebinding builtins void the once-bound-variable proof only in command
#     position (`read T`, `while read T`, `IFS= read -r T`, `command read`,
#     `eval "read T"`); `exec read`, `env … read`, `sudo read`, `nice read`
#     are NOT counted — `read` is a builtin, so those forms fail or run in a
#     child and cannot rebind the caller's variable. `notes-guard.sh read`
#     and `echo read` are arguments, never rebinds.
#
# Registered in settings.hooks.json as PreToolUse matcher: "Bash"
# Part of Loa Harness Engineering (cycle-011, issue #297)
# Source: Trail of Bits claude-code-config safety patterns
# =============================================================================
# perf pass-2 (2026-07-05, skill-loop): fork/exec reduction. The boolean
# `echo | grep -qE` pattern dispatches (15 spawns on every benign Bash call)
# are replaced by bash [[ =~ ]] via the _match/_match_ci helpers below, which
# preserve grep's PER-LINE match model byte-for-byte (see helper comments).
# `\b` was translated to explicit POSIX boundary classes because bash =~
# compiles with the SYSTEM regex library — glibc supports \b, BSD libc does
# NOT, and this hook commits to macOS/BSD (header above). Each translated
# pattern carries an equivalence note. Deliberately NOT converted (grep
# retained): P10 DELETE-FROM segment extraction (grep -oiE multi-match with
# original-case output is not provably reproducible in bash — no match-offset
# primitive), the FR-SZ inner write-intent tests (their `X\b[^|;&]*` shapes
# make consuming \b-translation non-isomorphic; they only run when the
# command already mentions a protected path), and all `grep -oE | head -1`
# matched-substring extractions (block path only — the hook exits 2 right
# after). Also: stdin now streams straight into the Path-A jq (no cat spawn),
# audit timestamps use printf %(...)T (no date spawn), cwd uses $PWD.
# =============================================================================
# perf pass-8 (2026-07-05, skill-loop): provably-complete literal pre-filters
# on the pattern dispatch. After pass 2 the ~95% benign path still paid 13
# sequential ERE evaluations (~0.4 ms) plus the one unconditional P10 grep
# spawn (~3 ms). Each pattern group is now guarded by a cheap bash substring
# test on literal(s) PROVABLY NECESSARY for the group to match: each guard
# literal appears in the group's regex as a mandatory concatenation element —
# outside every alternation branch, optional (?) group and starred group — so
# any MATCHING LINE must contain it verbatim, hence the whole $command must
# contain it. Absence from the whole string therefore proves no line can
# match, and the group is skipped — outcome-identical by construction.
# Where a guard uses an alternation's literals (P6 drop|clear, FR-SZ
# .run/|grimoires/loa/skills), the guard tests ALL branch literals and any
# hit evaluates the group. Guards only ever SKIP, never accept: when the
# literal is present the group evaluates exactly as before, in the original
# order (first match still wins, block messages byte-identical).
# Case-insensitive groups (P8/P9/P10) guard on the same C-locale ASCII fold
# (${command,,}) that _match_ci applies per line and grep -i applies under
# the LC_ALL=C pin — folding is per-character and leaves \n untouched, so
# the folded whole string is exactly the folded lines joined by \n, and a
# literal absent from the folded whole is absent from every folded line.
# Per-group necessity proofs sit next to each guard. The P10 DELETE-FROM
# grep — the last unconditional spawn on the benign path — now runs only
# when the folded command contains both "delete" and "from" (both mandatory
# in its -i pattern). The log-redactor stays block-path-only (verified: it
# is exec'd only inside emit_block and the FR-SZ bypass audit branch).
# =============================================================================

# =============================================================================
# FR-6 heredoc consumer classifier (cycle-129 D-6.1; knob
# destructive_command_guard.heredoc_classifier, default true; false = the
# pre-cycle scan, i.e. only the #1245 quoted-cat scrub below).
# Defined BEFORE the bash-version guard and the stdin read so another script
# can source this file with BDB_LIB_ONLY=1 and call
#   _bdb_heredoc_consumer_class <command text>   → prints interpreter|nonexec|none
#   heredoc_nonexec <command text>               → exit 0 iff nonexec
# Bash 3.2 compatible (no ${x,,}, no mapfile, no associative arrays) and safe
# under a caller's `set -u`.
#
# Grammar (literal command text; no alias or function expansion; CRLF folded
# to LF). The command is walked line by line; a line holding an unquoted
# `<<` / `<<-` (not `<<<`) is a heredoc header, the body runs to the first
# line equal to the delimiter (leading tabs stripped for `<<-`). FULL SCAN
# (the whole command as today) on: any other control character, a header the
# tokenizer cannot read (open quote, trailing backslash, comment), more than
# one heredoc on a header, a delimiter that is not a plain word ('W', "W",
# \W or W with W in [A-Za-z0-9_.+:@%-]; `$X` is a variable delimiter), or a
# missing terminator. Per heredoc the class is:
#   interpreter — body scanned exactly as today: the header holds `$(`, a
#     backtick, `<(` or `>(`, a paren or brace group or a shell keyword; it
#     continues on the next line (`|`, `&&`, `||` last) or an earlier line
#     opened a substitution, group, quote or pipe; a member of the heredoc's
#     pipeline is a shell, interpreter, wrapper that runs its argument or SQL
#     runner (_bdb_hd_is_interp, _bdb_hd_is_runner); an allowlisted form
#     carries an unknown or exec-shaped flag (-c, -e, -x clusters, --exec,
#     --eval, --command, in-place); a write target is executable content
#     (_bdb_hd_exec_dest: script extension, .claude/hooks, .claude/settings*
#     .json, .git/hooks, .git/config, rc/profile files, /etc, a bin dir or a
#     directory on PATH, or any non-literal path); the first body line is a
#     shebang; the body holds `<<` (nested); a target's basename appears
#     elsewhere in the command outside the safe readers (_bdb_hd_same_line_exec:
#     `bash x`, `./x`, `source x`, `. x`, `chmod +x x`, `exec x`, cp/mv …).
#   nonexec — every pipeline member is an exact allowlisted form
#     (_bdb_hd_member): cat, tee, printf, echo with plain-file or stdout sinks;
#     gh pr|issue comment -F -; gh pr create --body-file -; git commit -F -;
#     br create|update reading `-`; jq/yq without in-place; grep; sed -n with
#     a print-only script; sort; wc. The body is then scanned PER SEGMENT
#     (_bdb_hd_scan_body): each line split on ; && || | &, wrapper prefixes
#     stripped (sudo command exec env nice time nohup builtin stdbuf ionice,
#     a leading backslash, quote, paren or brace, assignments, an absolute
#     path); a segment whose command word is a fence verb (rm git find dd
#     mkfs* shred truncate kubectl terraform aws gcloud psql mysql DROP
#     DELETE TRUNCATE) is kept on its own line for the normal rules, other
#     segments are dropped. The body falls back to a full scan when it holds
#     `$(`, a backtick, `<(` or `>(` under an unquoted delimiter, or a segment
#     word is an interpreter or wrapper, or a variable (`$x -rf /`; such a
#     segment is ALSO scanned as rm, git and kubectl with the same arguments).
#     Special case (the #1245 scrub): a standalone quoted-delimiter `cat`
#     whose header is exactly `cat <<'W' [> path]` drops the whole body.
#   none — the consumer is on neither list: full scan.
# Documented gap: a body written to a plain file by one command and executed
# by a LATER command is outside a per-command fence (the Write tool shares it).
# =============================================================================
_bdb_hd_op_re='^[0-9]*(<<<|<<-|&>>|<<|>>|>[|]|&&|[|][|]|[|]&|&>|<>|>&[0-9-]*|<&[0-9-]*|;;|;|&|[|]|<|>|[(]|[)])$'
_bdb_hd_re_dw='^[A-Za-z0-9_.+:@%-]+$'
_bdb_hd_re_dsq="^'([A-Za-z0-9_.+:@%-]+)'\$"
_bdb_hd_re_ddq='^"([A-Za-z0-9_.+:@%-]+)"$'
_bdb_hd_re_dbs='^\\([A-Za-z0-9_.+:@%-]+)$'
_bdb_hd_re_psq="^'([^']*)'\$"
_bdb_hd_re_pdq="^\"([^\"\$\`\\\\]*)\"\$"
_bdb_hd_re_pbare="^[^'\"\$\`\\\\]+\$"
_bdb_hd_re_ctl=$'[\x01-\x08\x0b-\x1f\x7f]'
_bdb_hd_re_exflag='^-[A-Za-z]*[cex][A-Za-z]*$'
_bdb_hd_re_exlong='^--(exec|eval|command|in-?place)'
_bdb_hd_re_ext='\.(sh|bash|zsh|ksh|csh|fish|py|pyw|rb|pl|pm|js|mjs|cjs|ts|mts|cts|ps1|psm1|php|lua|tcl|command|bat|cmd)$'
_bdb_hd_re_sys='(^|/)(\.claude/hooks(/|$)|\.claude/settings[^/]*\.json$|\.git/hooks(/|$)|\.git/config$|\.gitconfig$|\.ssh/rc$|\.config/(fish|zsh|bash|git)/|s?bin/[^/]+$)'
_bdb_hd_re_rc='(^|/)\.(bashrc|bash_profile|bash_login|bash_logout|profile|zshrc|zshenv|zprofile|zlogin|zlogout|kshrc|mkshrc|cshrc|tcshrc|login|logout|envrc)$'
_bdb_hd_re_sedp='^(([0-9]+|[$]|/[^/]*/)(,([0-9]+|[$]|/[^/]*/))?)?p$'
_bdb_hd_re_assign='^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*='
_bdb_hd_re_varw='^[$]([{]|[A-Za-z_])'
_bdb_hd_re_knob='^[[:space:]]+heredoc_classifier:[[:space:]]*["'"'"']?([A-Za-z]+)["'"'"']?[[:space:]]*(#.*)?$'

# Shells, interpreters and wrappers that run their argument or stdin.
_bdb_hd_is_interp() {
  case "$1" in
    bash|sh|zsh|dash|ksh|mksh|ash|fish|csh|tcsh|busybox|python|python[0-9]*|pypy*|node|nodejs|deno|bun|ruby|irb|perl|php|lua|luajit|tclsh|wish|expect|pwsh|powershell|osascript|Rscript) return 0 ;;
    eval|source|.|exec|command|builtin|time|awk|gawk|mawk|nawk|make|gmake|m4|ed|ex|vi|vim|nvim|gdb) return 0 ;;
    sudo|doas|su|runuser|env|xargs|parallel|timeout|nohup|nice|ionice|setsid|stdbuf|chroot|unshare|nsenter|ssh|docker|podman|kubectl|find|watch|script) return 0 ;;
  esac
  return 1
}
# The SQL runners of the FR-1.4/5/6 precondition (same list).
_bdb_hd_is_runner() {
  case "$1" in
    psql|pgcli|mysql|mariadb|mysqlsh|sqlite3|sqlcmd|sqlplus|isql|usql|litecli|duckdb|clickhouse|clickhouse-client|cockroach|bq|wrangler|prisma|supabase|drizzle-kit|knex|sequelize|typeorm|flyway|liquibase|dbmate|goose|sqitch|rails|manage.py|artisan|alembic|dbt|atlas|mongosh|sqlx) return 0 ;;
  esac
  return 1
}
# Command words the fence's own rules match.
_bdb_hd_is_destructive() {
  case "$1" in
    rm|git|find|dd|shred|truncate|kubectl|terraform|aws|gcloud|psql|mysql|mkfs|mkfs.*) return 0 ;;
    [Dd][Rr][Oo][Pp]|[Dd][Ee][Ll][Ee][Tt][Ee]|[Tt][Rr][Uu][Nn][Cc][Aa][Tt][Ee]) return 0 ;;
  esac
  return 1
}
# Readers that may name a heredoc's target elsewhere on the line.
_bdb_hd_is_safe_reader() {
  case "$1" in
    cat|ls|wc|head|tail|grep|egrep|fgrep|rg|diff|cmp|stat|file|test|'['|echo|printf|sort|uniq|jq|yq|git|gh|br|mkdir|touch|realpath|readlink|basename|dirname|du|md5sum|sha1sum|sha256sum|shasum|b2sum|cksum) return 0 ;;
  esac
  return 1
}

# _bdb_hd_tokenize <line> → _bdb_hd_tok[] (words keep their quotes; operators
# are separate tokens, an fd number joins its redirect). Returns 1 when the
# line cannot be read: open quote, trailing backslash, unquoted comment.
_bdb_hd_tokenize() {
  local s="${1:-}" n i=0 ch tok="" q="" have=0 op cand
  n=${#s}
  _bdb_hd_tok=()
  while (( i < n )); do
    ch="${s:i:1}"
    if [[ -n "$q" ]]; then
      tok="$tok$ch"
      if [[ "$q" == "'" ]]; then
        [[ "$ch" == "'" ]] && q=""
      elif [[ "$ch" == '\' ]]; then
        (( i + 1 < n )) || return 1
        i=$((i + 1)); tok="$tok${s:i:1}"
      elif [[ "$ch" == '"' ]]; then
        q=""
      fi
      i=$((i + 1)); continue
    fi
    case "$ch" in
      "'"|'"') q="$ch"; tok="$tok$ch"; have=1; i=$((i + 1)) ;;
      '\')
        (( i + 1 < n )) || return 1
        tok="$tok$ch${s:i+1:1}"; have=1; i=$((i + 2)) ;;
      ' '|$'\t')
        if (( have )); then _bdb_hd_tok[${#_bdb_hd_tok[@]}]="$tok"; tok=""; have=0; fi
        i=$((i + 1)) ;;
      '#')
        (( have )) || return 1
        tok="$tok$ch"; i=$((i + 1)) ;;
      ';'|'&'|'|'|'<'|'>'|'('|')')
        op=""
        for cand in '<<<' '<<-' '&>>' '<<' '>>' '>|' '&&' '||' '|&' '&>' '<>' '>&' '<&' ';;' ';' '&' '|' '<' '>' '(' ')'; do
          if [[ "${s:i:${#cand}}" == "$cand" ]]; then op="$cand"; break; fi
        done
        i=$((i + ${#op}))
        if [[ "$op" == '>&' || "$op" == '<&' ]]; then
          while (( i < n )) && [[ "${s:i:1}" == [0-9-] ]]; do op="$op${s:i:1}"; i=$((i + 1)); done
        fi
        if (( have )); then
          if [[ "$tok" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] && [[ "$op" == '<'* || "$op" == '>'* ]]; then
            op="$tok$op"
          else
            _bdb_hd_tok[${#_bdb_hd_tok[@]}]="$tok"
          fi
          tok=""; have=0
        fi
        _bdb_hd_tok[${#_bdb_hd_tok[@]}]="$op" ;;
      *) tok="$tok$ch"; have=1; i=$((i + 1)) ;;
    esac
  done
  [[ -z "$q" ]] || return 1
  (( have )) && _bdb_hd_tok[${#_bdb_hd_tok[@]}]="$tok"
  return 0
}

# _bdb_hd_unq_path <word> → _hd_up; returns 1 for a non-literal path (an
# expansion, an escape, mixed quoting) or an empty one.
_bdb_hd_unq_path() {
  _hd_up=""
  if [[ "${1:-}" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_psq ]] || [[ "${1:-}" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_pdq ]]; then
    _hd_up="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
  elif [[ "${1:-}" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_pbare ]]; then
    _hd_up="$1"
  else
    return 1
  fi
  [[ -n "$_hd_up" ]]
}

# _bdb_hd_exec_dest <unquoted path> → 0 when a write there is executable
# content (or cannot be judged).
_bdb_hd_exec_dest() {
  local p="${1:-}" d e b old_ifs
  case "$p" in
    *'*'*|*'?'*|*'['*|*'{'*|'~'|'~'[!/]*|'') return 0 ;;
  esac
  [[ "$p" == '~/'* ]] && p="${HOME:-}/${p#'~/'}"
  b="${p##*/}"
  [[ "$b" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_ext ]] && return 0
  [[ "$p" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_sys || "$p" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_rc ]] && return 0
  [[ "$p" == /etc/* ]] && return 0
  if [[ "$p" == /* ]]; then d="${p%/*}"; [[ -n "$d" ]] || d="/"
  elif [[ "$p" == */* ]]; then d="${PWD:-.}/${p%/*}"
  else d="${PWD:-.}"
  fi
  old_ifs="$IFS"; IFS=':'
  for e in ${PATH:-}; do
    [[ -z "$e" || "$e" == "." ]] && e="${PWD:-.}"
    [[ "$e" != "/" ]] && e="${e%/}"
    if [[ "$d" == "$e" ]]; then IFS="$old_ifs"; return 0; fi
  done
  IFS="$old_ifs"
  return 1
}

# _bdb_hd_member <tokens…> → _hd_mcls (interpreter|nonexec|none) for one
# pipeline member; write targets are appended to _hd_dests.
_bdb_hd_member() {
  local -a toks argv
  local t nxt i n stdout_files=0 a0 base fd stdin=0 ops=0 want="" has_n=0 script=""
  toks=("$@"); n=${#toks[@]}; argv=()
  _hd_mcls=none
  for ((i = 0; i < n; i++)); do
    t="${toks[i]}"
    if [[ "$t" =~ $_bdb_hd_op_re ]]; then
      case "$t" in
        *'<<<') return ;;
        *'<<'|*'<<-') i=$((i + 1)); continue ;;
        *'>&'[0-9]*|*'>&-'|*'<&'*) continue ;;
        *'>'|*'>>'|*'>|'|*'>&'|'&>'|'&>>')
          nxt="${toks[i+1]:-}"; i=$((i + 1))
          if [[ -z "$nxt" || "$nxt" =~ $_bdb_hd_op_re ]]; then _hd_mcls=interpreter; return; fi
          _bdb_hd_unq_path "$nxt" || { _hd_mcls=interpreter; return; }
          case "$_hd_up" in /dev/null|/dev/stdout|/dev/stderr) continue ;; esac
          _hd_dests[${#_hd_dests[@]}]="$_hd_up"
          fd="${t%%[>&]*}"
          [[ -z "$fd" || "$fd" == 1 || "$t" == '&>'* || "$t" == '>&' ]] && stdout_files=$((stdout_files + 1))
          continue ;;
        *) return ;;
      esac
    fi
    argv[${#argv[@]}]="$t"
  done
  (( ${#argv[@]} > 0 )) || return
  a0="${argv[0]}"
  base="${a0#\\}"; base="${base##*/}"
  if _bdb_hd_is_interp "$base" || _bdb_hd_is_runner "$base"; then _hd_mcls=interpreter; return; fi
  [[ "$a0" =~ ^[a-z][a-z0-9]*$ ]] || return
  (( stdout_files <= 1 )) || return
  for ((i = 1; i < ${#argv[@]}; i++)); do
    t="${argv[i]}"
    if [[ "$t" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_exflag || "$t" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_exlong ]]; then _hd_mcls=interpreter; return; fi
  done
  case "$a0" in
    cat)
      for ((i = 1; i < ${#argv[@]}; i++)); do [[ "${argv[i]}" == "-" ]] || { _hd_mcls=interpreter; return; }; done ;;
    tee)
      for ((i = 1; i < ${#argv[@]}; i++)); do
        t="${argv[i]}"
        case "$t" in
          -a|--append|-p) ;;
          -*) _hd_mcls=interpreter; return ;;
          *) _bdb_hd_unq_path "$t" || { _hd_mcls=interpreter; return; }
             _hd_dests[${#_hd_dests[@]}]="$_hd_up" ;;
        esac
      done ;;
    echo|printf)
      for ((i = 1; i < ${#argv[@]}; i++)); do
        case "${argv[i]}" in -n|-E) ;; -*) _hd_mcls=interpreter; return ;; esac
      done ;;
    gh)
      case "${argv[1]:-} ${argv[2]:-}" in
        "pr comment"|"issue comment") want=" -F --body-file -R --repo |" ;;
        "pr create") want=" -F --body-file --title -t --base -B --head -H --repo -R --label -l --reviewer -r --assignee -a --milestone -m --project -p --template -T | --draft -d --fill --fill-first --fill-verbose --no-maintainer-edit --dry-run " ;;
        *) return ;;
      esac
      for ((i = 3; i < ${#argv[@]}; i++)); do
        t="${argv[i]}"
        case "$t" in
          --body-file=-) stdin=1 ;;
          --*=*) [[ "${want%%|*}" == *" ${t%%=*} "* ]] || { _hd_mcls=interpreter; return; } ;;
          -*)
            if [[ "${want%%|*}" == *" $t "* ]]; then
              i=$((i + 1))
              [[ ( "$t" == "-F" || "$t" == "--body-file" ) && "${argv[i]:-}" == "-" ]] && stdin=1
            elif [[ "${want#*|}" != *" $t "* ]]; then
              _hd_mcls=interpreter; return
            fi ;;
          *) ops=$((ops + 1)); [[ "${argv[2]}" == comment && $ops -le 1 ]] || { _hd_mcls=interpreter; return; } ;;
        esac
      done
      (( stdin )) || { _hd_mcls=interpreter; return; } ;;
    git)
      [[ "${argv[1]:-}" == commit ]] || return
      for ((i = 2; i < ${#argv[@]}; i++)); do
        t="${argv[i]}"
        case "$t" in
          -F|--file) i=$((i + 1)); [[ "${argv[i]:-}" == "-" ]] || { _hd_mcls=interpreter; return; }; stdin=1 ;;
          --file=-|-F-) stdin=1 ;;
          -q|--quiet|-s|--signoff|-a|--all|--allow-empty|--allow-empty-message|-v|--verbose|--no-edit|--amend) ;;
          *) _hd_mcls=interpreter; return ;;
        esac
      done
      (( stdin )) || { _hd_mcls=interpreter; return; } ;;
    br)
      case "${argv[1]:-}" in create|update) ;; *) return ;; esac
      for ((i = 2; i < ${#argv[@]}; i++)); do
        t="${argv[i]}"
        case "$t" in
          -d|--description|--body) [[ "${argv[i+1]:-}" == "-" ]] && stdin=1 ;;
          -f|--file) [[ "${argv[1]}" == create && "${argv[i+1]:-}" == "-" ]] && stdin=1 ;;
          --description=-|--body=-) stdin=1 ;;
        esac
      done
      (( stdin )) || { _hd_mcls=interpreter; return; } ;;
    jq|yq)
      for ((i = 1; i < ${#argv[@]}; i++)); do
        # In-place flags: --inplace/--in-place, -i, -i=…, and any short-flag cluster holding an i
        # (corpus D114/D115: `-i` alone did not match `-[A-Za-z]*i*`, which needs a letter before the i).
        case "${argv[i]}" in --inplace|--in-place|-i*|-[A-Za-z]*i*) _hd_mcls=interpreter; return ;; esac
      done ;;
    grep|egrep|fgrep) ;;
    sed)
      for ((i = 1; i < ${#argv[@]}; i++)); do
        t="${argv[i]}"
        case "$t" in
          -n|--quiet|--silent) has_n=1 ;;
          -E|-r|--regexp-extended|-s|--separate|-u|--unbuffered|-z|--null-data) ;;
          -*) _hd_mcls=interpreter; return ;;
          *) if [[ -z "$script" ]]; then
               script="$t"; [[ "$script" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_psq || "$script" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_pdq ]] && script="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
               [[ "$script" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_sedp ]] || { _hd_mcls=interpreter; return; }
             fi ;;
        esac
      done
      (( has_n )) && [[ -n "$script" ]] || { _hd_mcls=interpreter; return; } ;;
    sort)
      for ((i = 1; i < ${#argv[@]}; i++)); do
        t="${argv[i]}"
        case "$t" in
          -o) i=$((i + 1)); _bdb_hd_unq_path "${argv[i]:-}" || { _hd_mcls=interpreter; return; }; _hd_dests[${#_hd_dests[@]}]="$_hd_up" ;;
          -k|-t) i=$((i + 1)) ;;
          -k*|-t*) ;;
          --*) _hd_mcls=interpreter; return ;;
          -*) [[ "$t" =~ ^-[bdfghiMnRrsuVz]+$ ]] || { _hd_mcls=interpreter; return; } ;;
        esac
      done ;;
    wc)
      for ((i = 1; i < ${#argv[@]}; i++)); do
        case "${argv[i]}" in -*) [[ "${argv[i]}" =~ ^-[lwmL]+$ ]] || { _hd_mcls=interpreter; return; } ;; esac
      done ;;
    *) return ;;
  esac
  _hd_mcls=nonexec
}

# _bdb_hd_ctx_bad <line> → 0 when a line before (or the header itself) leaves
# the next text inside a substitution, group, quote, compound command or
# pipeline: a later heredoc there is interpreter-class.
_bdb_hd_ctx_bad() {
  local l="${1:-}" k last
  case "$l" in *'$('*|*'`'*|*'<('*|*'>('*) return 0 ;; esac
  _bdb_hd_tokenize "$l" || return 0
  for ((k = 0; k < ${#_bdb_hd_tok[@]}; k++)); do
    case "${_bdb_hd_tok[k]}" in
      '('|')'|'{'|'}'|do|done|then|else|elif|if|fi|while|until|for|case|esac|select|function|coproc) return 0 ;;
    esac
  done

# _bdb_hd_header <line> — parse one header line. Sets _hd_ops (heredoc count,
# -1 = unreadable), _hd_delim, _hd_quoted, _hd_tabs, _hd_cls, _hd_dests[],
# _hd_pipe (pipeline id of the heredoc on this line).
_bdb_hd_header() {
  local line="${1:-}" k nt t opi=-1 w seg=0 pipe=0
  local -a tpipe mtoks
  _hd_ops=0 _hd_delim="" _hd_quoted=0 _hd_tabs=0 _hd_cls=none _hd_pipe=-1
  _hd_dests=()
  if ! _bdb_hd_tokenize "$line"; then _hd_ops=-1; return; fi
  nt=${#_bdb_hd_tok[@]}
  tpipe=()
  for ((k = 0; k < nt; k++)); do
    t="${_bdb_hd_tok[k]}"
    case "$t" in
      ';'|';;'|'&'|'&&'|'||'|'('|')') pipe=$((pipe + 1)); tpipe[k]=-1; continue ;;
      '|'|'|&') tpipe[k]=-1; continue ;;
    esac
    tpipe[k]=$pipe
    if [[ "$t" =~ ^[0-9]*'<<'-?$ ]]; then _hd_ops=$((_hd_ops + 1)); opi=$k; fi
  done
  (( _hd_ops == 1 )) || return
  w="${_bdb_hd_tok[opi+1]:-}"
  [[ "${_bdb_hd_tok[opi]}" == *'<<-' ]] && _hd_tabs=1
  if [[ "$w" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_dsq || "$w" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_ddq || "$w" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_dbs ]]; then
    _hd_delim="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"; _hd_quoted=1
  elif [[ "$w" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_dw ]]; then
    _hd_delim="$w"
  else
    _hd_ops=-1; return        # variable-expanded, mixed or missing delimiter
  fi
  _hd_pipe="${tpipe[opi]}"
  if _bdb_hd_ctx_bad "$line"; then _hd_cls=interpreter; return; fi
  _bdb_hd_tokenize "$line"    # _bdb_hd_ctx_bad reused the token buffer
  # Classify every member of the heredoc's pipeline; the most executing wins.
  local cls=nonexec
  k=0
  while (( k < nt )); do
    if [[ "${tpipe[k]}" != "$_hd_pipe" ]]; then k=$((k + 1)); continue; fi
    mtoks=()
    while (( k < nt )) && [[ "${tpipe[k]}" == "$_hd_pipe" ]]; do mtoks[${#mtoks[@]}]="${_bdb_hd_tok[k]}"; k=$((k + 1)); done
    _bdb_hd_member "${mtoks[@]}"
    case "$_hd_mcls" in
      interpreter) cls=interpreter ;;
      none) [[ "$cls" == interpreter ]] || cls=none ;;
    esac
    k=$((k + 1))
  done
  _hd_cls="$cls"

# _bdb_hd_segword <segment> → _hd_w (command word after wrapper stripping,
# quotes and an absolute path removed) and _hd_rest (the text after it).
_bdb_hd_segword() {
  local s="${1:-}" w guard=0
  _hd_w="" _hd_rest=""
  while (( guard < 64 )); do
    guard=$((guard + 1))
    s="${s#"${s%%[![:space:]]*}"}"
    [[ -n "$s" ]] || return
    case "${s:0:1}" in
      '('|'{'|'!'|'\'|'"'|"'") s="${s:1}"; continue ;;
    esac
    w="${s%%[[:space:]]*}"
    s="${s:${#w}}"
    if [[ "$w" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_assign ]]; then continue; fi
    case "$w" in
      sudo|doas|command|exec|env|nice|time|nohup|builtin|stdbuf|ionice)
        while :; do
          s="${s#"${s%%[![:space:]]*}"}"
          case "$s" in
            -S|-S[[:space:]]*|--split-string*) _hd_w="sh"; _hd_rest="$s"; return ;;
            -[ugnCphUrtTDc]|-[ugnCphUrtTDc][[:space:]]*)
              s="${s:2}"; s="${s#"${s%%[![:space:]]*}"}"; w="${s%%[[:space:]]*}"; s="${s:${#w}}" ;;
            -*) w="${s%%[[:space:]]*}"; s="${s:${#w}}" ;;

        done

# _bdb_hd_scan_body <first> <last> <quoted> — per-segment scan of
# _bdb_hd_L[first..last]. Sets _hd_kept (fence-verb segments, one per line),
# _hd_synth (variable-command segments rewritten as rm/git/kubectl) and
# _hd_full (1 = the body needs the full scan).
_bdb_hd_scan_body() {
  local k l t seg
  _hd_kept="" _hd_synth="" _hd_full=0
  for ((k = $1; k <= $2; k++)); do
    l="${_bdb_hd_L[k]}"
    [[ "$l" == *'<<'* ]] && _hd_full=1
    if (( ! $3 )); then
      case "$l" in *'$('*|*'`'*|*'<('*|*'>('*) _hd_full=1 ;; esac
    fi
    t="${l//'&&'/$'\n'}"; t="${t//'||'/$'\n'}"; t="${t//'|'/$'\n'}"; t="${t//';'/$'\n'}"; t="${t//'&'/$'\n'}"
    while :; do
      seg="${t%%$'\n'*}"
      _bdb_hd_segword "$seg"
      if [[ -n "$_hd_w" ]]; then
        if [[ "$_hd_w" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_varw ]]; then
          _hd_full=1
          _hd_synth="${_hd_synth}rm${_hd_rest}"$'\n'"git${_hd_rest}"$'\n'"kubectl${_hd_rest}"$'\n'
        elif _bdb_hd_is_destructive "$_hd_w"; then
          _hd_kept="${_hd_kept}${_hd_w}${_hd_rest}"$'\n'
        elif _bdb_hd_is_interp "$_hd_w" || _bdb_hd_is_runner "$_hd_w"; then
          _hd_full=1
        fi
      fi
      [[ "$t" == *$'\n'* ]] || break
      t="${t#*$'\n'}"
    done
  done
}

_bdb_hd_same_line_exec() {

      if (( j < nt )) && ! [[ "$t" =~ ^(';'|';;'|'&'|'&&'|'||'|'('|')'|'|'|'|&')$ ]]; then continue; fi

        seg_has=0 cw=""
        for ((c = start; c < j; c++)); do
          u="${_bdb_hd_tok[c]}"; u="${u//[\"\']/}"; u="${u##*/}"
          [[ "$u" == "$b" ]] && seg_has=1

          cw="$_hd_w"
          if ! _bdb_hd_is_safe_reader "$cw" || [[ "$cw" == "$b" ]]; then return 0; fi
        fi

while [[ -n "$rest" ]]; do
    line="${rest%%$'\n'*}"
    if [[ "$rest" == *$'\n'* ]]; then rest="${rest#*$'\n'}"; else rest=""; fi
    if [[ "$strip_tabs" == "-" ]]; then
      while [[ "$line" == $'\t'* ]]; do line="${line#$'\t'}"; done
    fi
    if [[ "$line" == "$delim" ]]; then
      if [[ -z "$rest" ]]; then printf '%s' "$header"; else printf '%s' "$text"; fi
      return
    fi
  done
  # No closing delimiter: leave the entire command visible.
  printf '%s' "$text"
}

# #1245: two COMPLETE data-only programs, not arbitrary interpreter exemptions.
# Loop: single-quoted items, one printf with a fixed format and the same lower-
# case variable. Python: single-quoted -c source, double-quoted string literals
# without escapes, a list optionally assigned and printed. No imports, calls
# other than that print, interpolation, other consumers or trailing shell text.
# Single shell quotes keep $()/backticks in these literals inert. Any mismatch
# retains raw input, including double-quoted arguments where expansions execute.
_bdb_scrub_literal_program() {
  local text="$1" loop_re python_re source name list_re program_re
  loop_re="^[[:space:]]*for[[:blank:]]+([a-z][a-z0-9_]*)[[:blank:]]+in[[:blank:]]+'[^']*'([[:blank:]]+'[^']*')*[[:blank:]]*;[[:space:]]*do[[:space:]]+printf[[:blank:]]+'%s"
  loop_re+='\\n'
  loop_re+="'[[:blank:]]+"
  loop_re+='"[$]([a-z][a-z0-9_]*)"[[:blank:]]*;[[:space:]]*done[[:space:]]*$'
  if [[ "$text" =~ $loop_re ]] && [[ "${BASH_REMATCH[1]}" == "${BASH_REMATCH[3]}" ]]; then
    printf '%s' ': literal loop data'
    return
  fi
  python_re="^[[:blank:]]*python3?[[:blank:]]+-c[[:blank:]]+'([^']*)'[[:blank:]]*$"
  if [[ "$text" =~ $python_re ]]; then
    source="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
    list_re='\[[[:space:]]*("[^"\\]*"[[:space:]]*(,[[:space:]]*"[^"\\]*"[[:space:]]*)*,?[[:space:]]*)?\]'
    program_re="^[[:space:]]*${list_re}[[:space:]]*$"
    if [[ "$source" =~ ^[[:space:]]*([a-z][a-z0-9_]*)[[:space:]]*= ]]; then
      name="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
      program_re="^[[:space:]]*${name}[[:space:]]*=[[:space:]]*${list_re}([[:space:]]*;[[:space:]]*print\([[:space:]]*${name}[[:space:]]*\))?[[:space:]]*$"
    fi
    if [[ "$source" =~ $program_re ]]; then
      printf '%s' ': literal Python data'
      return
    fi
  fi
  printf '%s' "$text"
}

# Heredoc scrub, then quoted-value carriers, then echo/printf (sed).
# The echo scrub must run last: it can otherwise consume a closing quote in
# metadata containing "; echo ..." and make a later live write look quoted.
# (bash loops, each guarded by a cheap literal test so the benign path pays
# nothing beyond the substring check).
_cmd_match="$command"
if [[ "$_cmd_match" == *"for "* || "$_cmd_match" == *"python"* ]]; then
  _cmd_match=$(_bdb_scrub_literal_program "$_cmd_match")
fi
# cycle-129 FR-6: with destructive_command_guard.heredoc_classifier on (the
# default) the fail-closed consumer classifier above replaces the #1245 scrub,
# which survives unchanged as its special case and as the knob-off path.
if [[ "$_cmd_match" == *"<<"* ]]; then
  if _bdb_heredoc_knob_on; then
    _cmd_match=$(_bdb_heredoc_scrub "$_cmd_match")
  else
    _cmd_match=$(_bdb_scrub_cat_heredoc "$_cmd_match")
  fi
fi
[[ "$_cmd_match" == *"git"* ]] && _cmd_match=$(_bdb_scrub "$_bdb_re_git" "$_cmd_match")
if [[ "$_cmd_match" == *"br "* || "$_cmd_match" == *"bd "* ]]; then
  _cmd_match=$(_bdb_scrub "$_bdb_re_brbd" "$_cmd_match")
fi
[[ "$_cmd_match" == *"gh "* ]] && _cmd_match=$(_bdb_scrub "$_bdb_re_gh" "$_cmd_match")
if [[ "$_cmd_match" == *grep* || "$_cmd_match" == *"rg "* || "$_cmd_match" == *"ag "* || "$_cmd_match" == *"ack "* ]]; then
  _cmd_match=$(_bdb_scrub "$_bdb_re_grep" "$_cmd_match")   # cycle-125 D-1.7
fi
_cmd_match=$(printf '%s' "$_cmd_match" | sed -E -e "$_bdb_sed_echo" 2>/dev/null) || _cmd_match="$command"
# Fail-safe: an empty scrub on a non-empty command → fall back to RAW (stricter
# matching), never to an empty scrub that would silence every pattern.
[[ -z "$_cmd_match" ]] && _cmd_match="$command"

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# perf pass-2 line-model helpers.
#
# `echo "$cmd" | grep -qE PAT` tests PAT against each LINE; bash [[ =~ ]]
# tests the WHOLE string, where a `[[:space:]]` would match the newline
# itself, negated classes like [^-] would cross line boundaries, and ^/$
# anchor only at string edges. To keep byte-identical semantics we split
# $command into grep's line model ONCE (trailing \n is a terminator, not an
# extra empty line; a final fragment without \n is still a line) and test
# per line. Invalid-regex behavior also matches the old `grep -qE …
# 2>/dev/null`: [[ =~ ]] returns non-zero silently.
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# quote-blindness fix: derive the line model from the scrub-copy _cmd_match so
# every pattern that goes through _match/_match_ci (P2-P9, P11, P12, FR-2 gate)
# sees inert carrier values redacted, with ZERO change to their own regexes.
_cmd_lines=()
if [[ "$_cmd_match" == *$'\n'* ]]; then
  mapfile -t _cmd_lines <<<"${_cmd_match%$'\n'}"
else
  _cmd_lines=("$_cmd_match")
fi

# _match <ere> — exit 0 iff any line matches; ≡ echo "$command" | grep -qE <ere>
_match() {
  local _l
  for _l in "${_cmd_lines[@]}"; do
    [[ "$_l" =~ $1 ]] && return 0
  done
  return 1

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# =============================================================================
     3	# profile-lib.sh — `loa.profile` resolution (cycle-129 SDD D-9.1, §5.3;
     4	# DEC-0143, DEC-0152, DEC-0166).
     5	#
     6	# Sourced API (bash 3.2 safe; sets no shell options; every function returns 0
     7	# unless stated):
     8	#   loa_profile                     → lean | standard | full
     9	#   loa_profile_source              → explicit | default | invalid
    10	#   loa_knob <yq-path> <fallback>   → the effective value of one config key:
    11	#        the key set explicitly in the config (an explicit `false` counts —
    12	#        never `// default`, which reads false as absent), else the selected
    13	#        profile's value when the key is a profile key, else <fallback>.
    14	#        Returns 2 (printing the fallback) on a malformed path.
    15	#   loa_profile_overrides           → `key=value` lines, one per explicit
    16	#        profile key whose value differs from the selected profile's value
    17	#   loa_effective_json              → the resolved document (below)
    18	#
    19	# CLI: profile-lib.sh profile | source | knob <path> <fallback> | overrides | json
    20	#
    21	# Inputs (each has a test seam):
    22	#   config    LOA_PROFILE_CONFIG_FILE, else LOA_STATUS_CONFIG_FILE (honoured
    23	#             only under bats, like loa-status.sh), else <root>/.loa.config.yaml
    24	#   profiles  LOA_PROFILES_FILE, else <root>/.claude/data/profiles.yaml
    25	#   floor     LOA_PROFILE_FLOOR_FILE, else <root>/.claude/data/floor.yaml
    26	#   root      LOA_PROFILE_ROOT, else three directories above this file
    27	#
    28	# Cache: <root>/.run/effective-config.json (LOA_PROFILE_CACHE_FILE overrides),
    29	# keyed on the paths and the mtime+size of the config, profiles.yaml and
    30	# floor.yaml: any edit to one of them rebuilds it on the next call, so it is
    31	# built once per session in practice. When the config is a seam (not the
    32	# repository's own file) and no cache seam is set, nothing is cached — a test
    33	# config never overwrites the repository's cache. The warm path is one stat
    34	# and one jq. The write is atomic (temp file + mv in the same directory).
    35	#
    36	# Safety: a profile key that names a floor key (floor.yaml `floor_keys`, `*`
    37	# matches one or more characters; an ancestor of a floor key also counts) is
    38	# ignored with a WARN — no profile can reach the floor. Key paths are checked
    39	# against ^[A-Za-z0-9_]+(\.[A-Za-z0-9_]+)*$ before they reach a yq expression.
    40	# Overrides and the requested profile name are control-stripped and cut.
    41	# =============================================================================
    42	
    43	_LOA_PL_SELF="${BASH_SOURCE[0]}"
    44	_LOA_PL_SELF_DIR="${_LOA_PL_SELF%/*}"
    45	[[ "$_LOA_PL_SELF_DIR" == "$_LOA_PL_SELF" ]] && _LOA_PL_SELF_DIR="."
    46	_LOA_PL_SELF_DIR="$(cd "$_LOA_PL_SELF_DIR" 2>/dev/null && pwd -P)"
    47	_LOA_PL_JSON=""
    48	_LOA_PL_ID=""
    49	
    50	_loa_pl_paths() {
    51	  local root="${LOA_PROFILE_ROOT:-}"
    52	  if [[ -z "$root" ]]; then
    53	    root="$(cd "$_LOA_PL_SELF_DIR/../../.." 2>/dev/null && pwd -P)"
    54	  fi
    55	  _LOA_PL_ROOT="$root"
    56	  local default_cfg="$root/.loa.config.yaml" status_cfg=""
    57	  # LOA_STATUS_CONFIG_FILE is loa-status.sh's bats-gated seam; honour it the same way.
    58	  if [[ -n "${BATS_TEST_FILENAME:-}${BATS_VERSION:-}" ]]; then
    59	    status_cfg="${LOA_STATUS_CONFIG_FILE:-}"
    60	  fi
    61	  _LOA_PL_CFG="${LOA_PROFILE_CONFIG_FILE:-${status_cfg:-$default_cfg}}"
    62	  _LOA_PL_PROF="${LOA_PROFILES_FILE:-$root/.claude/data/profiles.yaml}"
    63	  _LOA_PL_FLOOR="${LOA_PROFILE_FLOOR_FILE:-$root/.claude/data/floor.yaml}"
    64	  if [[ -n "${LOA_PROFILE_CACHE_FILE:-}" ]]; then
    65	    _LOA_PL_CACHE="$LOA_PROFILE_CACHE_FILE"
    66	  elif [[ "$_LOA_PL_CFG" == "$default_cfg" ]]; then
    67	    _LOA_PL_CACHE="$root/.run/effective-config.json"
    68	  else
    69	    _LOA_PL_CACHE=""
    70	  fi
    71	}
    72	
    73	# The cache key: the three paths plus one stat line per existing file. An
    74	# empty stat output for an existing file (no usable stat) disables caching.
    75	_loa_pl_id() {
    76	  local st
    77	  st=$(stat -Lc '%n|%y|%s' -- "$_LOA_PL_CFG" "$_LOA_PL_PROF" "$_LOA_PL_FLOOR" 2>/dev/null) ||
    78	    st=$(stat -Lf '%N|%Fm|%z' -- "$_LOA_PL_CFG" "$_LOA_PL_PROF" "$_LOA_PL_FLOOR" 2>/dev/null) || true
    79	  if [[ -z "$st" ]] && [[ -e "$_LOA_PL_CFG" || -e "$_LOA_PL_PROF" ]]; then
    80	    _LOA_PL_CUR_ID=""
    81	    return 0
    82	  fi
    83	  _LOA_PL_CUR_ID="v1|$_LOA_PL_CFG|$_LOA_PL_PROF|$_LOA_PL_FLOOR|${st//$'\n'/;}"
    84	}
    85	
    86	_loa_pl_warn() { printf '[profile-lib] WARN: %s\n' "$*" >&2; }
    87	
    88	# Builds the resolved document from the three inputs into _LOA_PL_JSON.
    89	_loa_pl_build() {
    90	  local cfg='{}' prof='{}' floor='[]' out
    91	  if ! command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || ! command -v yq >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    92	    _LOA_PL_JSON=""
    93	    return 1
    94	  fi
    95	  if [[ -f "$_LOA_PL_CFG" ]]; then
    96	    if ! cfg=$(yq -o=json '.' "$_LOA_PL_CFG" 2>/dev/null); then
    97	      _loa_pl_warn "$_LOA_PL_CFG does not parse; profile defaults apply"
    98	      cfg='{}'
    99	    fi
   100	  fi
   101	  if [[ -f "$_LOA_PL_PROF" ]]; then
   102	    if ! prof=$(yq -o=json '.' "$_LOA_PL_PROF" 2>/dev/null); then
   103	      _loa_pl_warn "$_LOA_PL_PROF does not parse; no profile defaults apply"
   104	      prof='{}'
   105	    fi
   106	  else
   107	    _loa_pl_warn "$_LOA_PL_PROF is missing; no profile defaults apply"
   108	  fi
   109	  if [[ -f "$_LOA_PL_FLOOR" ]]; then
   110	    floor=$(yq -o=json '.floor_keys // []' "$_LOA_PL_FLOOR" 2>/dev/null) || floor='[]'
   111	  fi
   112	  [[ -n "$cfg" ]] || cfg='{}'
   113	  [[ -n "$prof" ]] || prof='{}'
   114	  [[ -n "$floor" ]] || floor='[]'
   115	  out=$(printf '%s\n%s\n%s\n' "$cfg" "$prof" "$floor" | jq -cs --arg id "$_LOA_PL_CUR_ID" '
   116	    def render: if type == "string" then . elif type == "object" or type == "array" then tojson else tostring end;
   117	    def clean($n): render | gsub("[[:cntrl:]]"; "?") | .[0:$n];
   118	    def globre: "^" + (split("*") | map(gsub("\\."; "\\.")) | join(".+")) + "$";
   119	    (.[0] | if type == "object" then . else {} end) as $cfg |
   120	    (.[1] | if type == "object" then . else {} end) as $pf |
   121	    (.[2] | if type == "array" then map(select(type == "string")) else [] end) as $floor |
   122	    ($pf.profiles | if type == "object" then . else {} end) as $profiles |
   123	    ([$profiles[] | objects | keys[]] | unique) as $all |
   124	    def forbidden($k): any($floor[]; . as $f | ($k | test($f | globre)) or (($f | split("*")[0]) | startswith($k + ".")));
   125	    ($all | map(select(forbidden(.)))) as $bad |
   126	    ($all - $bad) as $keys |
   127	    (try ($cfg.loa.profile) catch null) as $req |
   128	    (if $req == null then {name: "standard", source: "default"}
   129	     elif ($req | type) == "string" and ($profiles[$req]? | type) == "object" then {name: $req, source: "explicit"}
   130	     else {name: "standard", source: "invalid"} end) as $sel |
   131	    ($profiles[$sel.name]? // {} | if type == "object" then . else {} end) as $pv |
   132	    (reduce $keys[] as $k ({};
   133	        (try ($cfg | getpath($k | split("."))) catch null) as $e |
   134	        (if ($pv | has($k)) then $pv[$k] else null end) as $p |
   135	        if $e != null then .[$k] = {value: $e, source: "explicit", profile_value: $p}
   136	        elif ($pv | has($k)) then .[$k] = {value: $p, source: "profile", profile_value: $p}
   137	        else . end)) as $knobs |
   138	    {
   139	      schema_version: 1,
   140	      id: $id,
   141	      profile: $sel.name,
   142	      profile_source: $sel.source,
   143	      profile_requested: (if $req == null then null else ($req | clean(64)) end),
   144	      profile_keys: $keys,
   145	      knobs: $knobs,
   146	      overrides: ([$knobs | to_entries[]
   147	                   | select(.value.source == "explicit" and .value.value != .value.profile_value)
   148	                   | "\(.key)=\(.value.value | clean(128))"] | sort),
   149	      warnings: ([if $sel.source == "invalid" then "unknown loa.profile \"\($req | clean(64))\"; using standard" else empty end]
   150	                 + [$bad[] | "profiles.yaml key \(.) names a floor key; ignored"])
   151	    }' 2>/dev/null) || out=""
   152	  if [[ -z "$out" ]]; then
   153	    _LOA_PL_JSON=""
   154	    return 1
   155	  fi
   156	  _LOA_PL_JSON="$out"
   157	  local w
   158	  while IFS= read -r w; do
   159	    [[ -n "$w" ]] && _loa_pl_warn "$w"
   160	  done < <(printf '%s' "$out" | jq -r '.warnings[]?' 2>/dev/null)
   161	  return 0
   162	}
   163	
   164	_loa_pl_write_cache() {
   165	  [[ -n "$_LOA_PL_CACHE" && -n "$_LOA_PL_CUR_ID" && -n "$_LOA_PL_JSON" ]] || return 0
   166	  local dir="${_LOA_PL_CACHE%/*}" tmp
   167	  [[ "$dir" == "$_LOA_PL_CACHE" ]] && dir="."
   168	  if [[ ! -d "$dir" ]]; then
   169	    mkdir -p "$dir" 2>/dev/null || return 0
   170	  fi
   171	  tmp="$_LOA_PL_CACHE.tmp.$$"
   172	  if printf '%s\n' "$_LOA_PL_JSON" > "$tmp" 2>/dev/null; then
   173	    mv -f "$tmp" "$_LOA_PL_CACHE" 2>/dev/null || rm -f "$tmp" 2>/dev/null
   174	  else
   175	    rm -f "$tmp" 2>/dev/null
   176	  fi
   177	  return 0
   178	}
   179	
   180	# Loads the resolved document into _LOA_PL_JSON (memo → cache → build).
   181	# Returns 1 when it cannot be resolved (jq or yq missing).
   182	_loa_pl_load() {
   183	  _loa_pl_paths
   184	  _loa_pl_id
   185	  if [[ -n "$_LOA_PL_JSON" && -n "$_LOA_PL_CUR_ID" && "$_LOA_PL_ID" == "$_LOA_PL_CUR_ID" ]]; then
   186	    return 0
   187	  fi
   188	  command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 1
   189	  if [[ -n "$_LOA_PL_CACHE" && -n "$_LOA_PL_CUR_ID" && -f "$_LOA_PL_CACHE" ]]; then
   190	    local j
   191	    j=$(jq -c --arg id "$_LOA_PL_CUR_ID" 'if .schema_version == 1 and .id == $id then . else empty end' \
   192	        "$_LOA_PL_CACHE" 2>/dev/null) || j=""
   193	    if [[ -n "$j" ]]; then
   194	      _LOA_PL_JSON="$j"
   195	      _LOA_PL_ID="$_LOA_PL_CUR_ID"
   196	      return 0
   197	    fi
   198	  fi
   199	  _loa_pl_build || return 1
   200	  _LOA_PL_ID="$_LOA_PL_CUR_ID"
   201	  _loa_pl_write_cache
   202	  return 0
   203	}
   204	
   205	# Live read of one explicit key (non-profile keys, or no resolution available).
   206	_loa_pl_live() {
   207	  local key="$1" fallback="$2" v
   208	  if [[ -f "${_LOA_PL_CFG:-}" ]] && command -v yq >/dev/null 2>&1 && command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1; then
   209	    v=$(yq -o=json ".$key" "$_LOA_PL_CFG" 2>/dev/null | jq -r 'if . == null then "__LOA_PL_MISS__" elif type == "string" then . elif type == "object" or type == "array" then tojson else tostring end' 2>/dev/null) || v=""
   210	    if [[ -n "$v" && "$v" != "__LOA_PL_MISS__" ]]; then
   211	      printf '%s\n' "$v"
   212	      return 0
   213	    fi
   214	  fi
   215	  printf '%s\n' "$fallback"
   216	  return 0
   217	}
   218	
   219	loa_knob() {
   220	  local path="${1:-}" fallback="${2:-}" key v
   221	  key="${path#.}"
   222	  if [[ ! "$key" =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9_]+(\.[A-Za-z0-9_]+)*$ ]]; then
   223	    _loa_pl_warn "loa_knob: malformed key path '${path//[^A-Za-z0-9._-]/?}'"
   224	    printf '%s\n' "$fallback"
   225	    return 2
   226	  fi
   227	  # Warm path: one stat + one jq straight from the cache file.
   228	  _loa_pl_paths
   229	  _loa_pl_id
   230	  if [[ -z "$_LOA_PL_JSON" && -n "$_LOA_PL_CACHE" && -n "$_LOA_PL_CUR_ID" && -f "$_LOA_PL_CACHE" ]] &&
   231	     command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1; then
   232	    v=$(jq -r --arg id "$_LOA_PL_CUR_ID" --arg k "$key" '
   233	          if .schema_version == 1 and .id == $id then
   234	            (if (.knobs | has($k)) then .knobs[$k].value
   235	               | (if type == "string" then . elif type == "object" or type == "array" then tojson else tostring end)
   236	             else "__LOA_PL_MISS__" end)
   237	          else "__LOA_PL_STALE__" end' "$_LOA_PL_CACHE" 2>/dev/null) || v="__LOA_PL_STALE__"
   238	    if [[ "$v" == "__LOA_PL_MISS__" ]]; then
   239	      _loa_pl_live "$key" "$fallback"
   240	      return 0
   241	    fi
   242	    if [[ -n "$v" && "$v" != "__LOA_PL_STALE__" ]]; then
   243	      printf '%s\n' "$v"
   244	      return 0
   245	    fi
   246	  fi
   247	  if ! _loa_pl_load; then
   248	    _loa_pl_live "$key" "$fallback"
   249	    return 0
   250	  fi
   251	  v=$(printf '%s' "$_LOA_PL_JSON" | jq -r --arg k "$key" '
   252	        if (.knobs | has($k)) then .knobs[$k].value
   253	          | (if type == "string" then . elif type == "object" or type == "array" then tojson else tostring end)
   254	        else "__LOA_PL_MISS__" end' 2>/dev/null) || v="__LOA_PL_MISS__"
   255	  if [[ -z "$v" || "$v" == "__LOA_PL_MISS__" ]]; then
   256	    _loa_pl_live "$key" "$fallback"
   257	    return 0
   258	  fi
   259	  printf '%s\n' "$v"
   260	  return 0
   261	}
   262	
   263	loa_profile() {
   264	  if _loa_pl_load; then
   265	    printf '%s' "$_LOA_PL_JSON" | jq -r '.profile // "standard"' 2>/dev/null || echo standard
   266	  else
   267	    echo standard
   268	  fi
   269	  return 0
   270	}
   271	
   272	loa_profile_source() {
   273	  if _loa_pl_load; then
   274	    printf '%s' "$_LOA_PL_JSON" | jq -r '.profile_source // "default"' 2>/dev/null || echo default
   275	  else
   276	    echo default
   277	  fi
   278	  return 0
   279	}
   280	
   281	loa_profile_overrides() {
   282	  if _loa_pl_load; then
   283	    printf '%s' "$_LOA_PL_JSON" | jq -r '.overrides[]?' 2>/dev/null || true
   284	  fi
   285	  return 0
   286	}
   287	
   288	loa_effective_json() {
   289	  if _loa_pl_load; then
   290	    printf '%s\n' "$_LOA_PL_JSON"
   291	  else
   292	    echo '{}'
   293	  fi
   294	  return 0
   295	}
   296	
   297	if [[ "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}" == "${0}" ]]; then
   298	  export LC_ALL=C
   299	  case "${1:-}" in
   300	    profile)   loa_profile ;;
   301	    source)    loa_profile_source ;;
   302	    knob)      [[ $# -ge 2 ]] || { echo "usage: profile-lib.sh knob <yq-path> [fallback]" >&2; exit 2; }
   303	               loa_knob "$2" "${3:-}"; exit $? ;;
   304	    overrides) loa_profile_overrides ;;
   305	    json)      loa_effective_json ;;
   306	    *)         sed -n '3,/^# =====/p' "$0" | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//' >&2; exit 2 ;;
   307	  esac
   308	fi
     1	# .claude/data/profiles.yaml — `loa.profile` defaults (cycle-129 SDD D-9.1, §3.5;
     2	# DEC-0143, DEC-0152).
     3	#
     4	# One knob, `loa.profile: lean | standard | full` in .loa.config.yaml, sets the
     5	# defaults of the optional surfaces below as a set. Resolution, per key
     6	# (.claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh `loa_knob`):
     7	#   1. the key set explicitly in .loa.config.yaml wins;
     8	#   2. else the selected profile's value (unset or unknown profile → standard);
     9	#   3. else the caller's fallback — never reached for a key listed here,
    10	#      because every profile defines every key (tests/unit/profile-lib.bats).
    11	#
    12	# `standard` is the post-cycle-129 example default of each key, written out
    13	# (tests/fixtures/profiles/standard-oracle.json records how each value was
    14	# captured). The two guardrail keys read false here because cycle-129 changed

    23

    41	    guardrails.danger_level.enforce: false

    47	    decisions.surface_at_session_start: true
    48	    karpathy_principles.surgical_diff_warning: true

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# =============================================================================
     3	# run-checkpoint.sh — task-granular checkpoint in .run/sprint-plan-state.json
     4	# (cycle-125 FR-3, SDD D-3.2). Beads are the task ledger; the checkpoint is a
     5	# HINT mirrored into state for visibility and fast resume.
     6	#
     7	#   run-checkpoint.sh write --sprint sprint-N --phase PHASE [--task BEAD-ID] [--file F]
     8	#       Atomically sets .schema_version = 2, .checkpoint = {sprint, task, phase, ts}
     9	#       and .timestamps.last_activity = ts: jq → F.tmp.$$ → mv -f, under flock
    10	#       on F.lock. F must already exist (a run in progress). Exit 0 · 2 usage /
    11	#       no run · 3 write failed (the previous file is untouched).
    12	#   run-checkpoint.sh read [--file F] [--json]
    13	#       Prints the checkpoint when it is trustworthy: parses, and when a task
    14	#       is named, `br show <task> --json` reports it closed (a checkpoint that
    15	#       names an open or unknown bead is DISCARDED with a logged line — beads
    16	#       remain the recovery source). schema_version 1 / no checkpoint → prints
    17	#       "sprint granularity". Exit 0 always when F exists; 2 when it does not.
    18	#
    19	# Default F: $LOA_RUN_DIR/sprint-plan-state.json, else <repo>/.run/sprint-plan-state.json.
    20	# Readers accept schema_version 1 and 2. No config key.
    21	# =============================================================================
    22	set -uo pipefail
    23	SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
    24	usage() { sed -n '3,/^# Default F/p' "$0" | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//' >&2; exit 2; }
    25	
    26	sub="${1:-}"; [[ -n "$sub" ]] || usage; shift
    27	file="" sprint="" task="" phase="" json=0
    28	while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
    29	  case "$1" in
    30	    --file)   [[ $# -ge 2 && -n "$2" ]] || usage; file="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    31	    --sprint) [[ $# -ge 2 && "$2" =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$ ]] || usage; sprint="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    32	    --task)   [[ $# -ge 2 && "$2" =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$ ]] || usage; task="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    33	    --phase)  [[ $# -ge 2 && "$2" =~ ^[A-Z_]+$ ]] || usage; phase="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    34	    --json)   json=1; shift ;;

    36	  esac
    37	done

    39	  root="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
    40	  file="${LOA_RUN_DIR:-$root/.run}/sprint-plan-state.json"
    41	fi
    42	
    43	cmd_write() {
    44	  [[ -n "$sprint" && -n "$phase" ]] || usage
    45	  if [[ ! -f "$file" ]]; then echo "run-checkpoint: no run state at $file (start a run first)" >&2; return 2; fi
    46	  local ts tmp lock rc=0
    47	  ts=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
    48	  tmp="$file.tmp.$$"; lock="$file.lock"
    49	  (
    50	    # flock is util-linux (Linux); without it (macOS) the write is still atomic
    51	    # (tmp + mv) but concurrent writers may interleave — last writer wins.
    52	    if command -v flock >/dev/null 2>&1; then flock -w 5 9 || { echo "run-checkpoint: lock timeout on $lock" >&2; exit 3; }; fi
    53	    if ! jq --arg s "$sprint" --arg t "$task" --arg p "$phase" --arg ts "$ts" \
    54	         '.schema_version = 2
    55	          | .checkpoint = {sprint: $s, task: (if $t == "" then null else $t end), phase: $p, ts: $ts}
    56	          | .timestamps = ((.timestamps // {}) + {last_activity: $ts})' "$file" > "$tmp" 2>/dev/null; then
    57	      rm -f -- "$tmp"; echo "run-checkpoint: $file is not valid JSON — checkpoint not written" >&2; exit 3
    58	    fi
    59	    jq -e . "$tmp" >/dev/null 2>&1 || { rm -f -- "$tmp"; echo "run-checkpoint: refusing to replace $file with unparseable output" >&2; exit 3; }
    60	    mv -f -- "$tmp" "$file"
    61	  ) 9>"$lock" || rc=$?
    62	  return $rc
    63	}
    64	
    65	bead_closed() {  # $1 bead id → 0 when br reports closed
    66	  command -v br >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 2
    67	  local js st
    68	  js=$(br show "$1" --json 2>/dev/null) || return 1
    69	  st=$(printf '%s' "$js" | jq -r 'if type=="array" then .[0] else . end | .status // .issue.status // empty' 2>/dev/null)
    70	  [[ "$st" == "closed" ]]
    71	}
    72	
    73	cmd_read() {
    74	  if [[ ! -f "$file" ]]; then echo "run-checkpoint: no run state at $file" >&2; return 2; fi
    75	  if ! jq -e . "$file" >/dev/null 2>&1; then echo "run-checkpoint: $file unparseable — no checkpoint; beads are the recovery truth" >&2; (( json )) && echo '{"checkpoint":null,"reason":"unparseable"}'; return 0; fi
    76	  local sv cp s t p ts reason=""
    77	  sv=$(jq -r '.schema_version // 1' "$file"); cp=$(jq -c '.checkpoint // null' "$file")
    78	  if [[ "$cp" == "null" || "$sv" -lt 2 ]]; then
    79	    (( json )) && echo '{"checkpoint":null,"reason":"sprint granularity"}' || echo "checkpoint: none (schema_version $sv → sprint granularity; resume at the first open bead of sprints.current)"
    80	    return 0
    81	  fi
    82	  s=$(jq -r '.checkpoint.sprint // empty' "$file"); t=$(jq -r '.checkpoint.task // empty' "$file"); p=$(jq -r '.checkpoint.phase // empty' "$file"); ts=$(jq -r '.checkpoint.ts // empty' "$file")
    83	  if [[ -z "$s" || -z "$p" ]]; then reason="malformed checkpoint"
    84	  elif [[ -n "$t" ]]; then
    85	    # A task checkpoint is trusted only when beads CONFIRMS the task closed;
    86	    # "br unavailable" is not a confirmation (Bridgebuilder PR #1269 FIND-003).
    87	    bead_closed "$t"; case $? in 0) ;; 2) reason="beads unavailable — task $t cannot be verified";; *) reason="task $t is not closed in beads";; esac
    88	  fi
    89	  if [[ -n "$reason" ]]; then
    90	    echo "run-checkpoint: discarding checkpoint ($reason) — resume from the first open bead of $s" >&2
    91	    (( json )) && jq -cn --arg r "$reason" --arg s "$s" '{checkpoint:null, reason:$r, sprint:$s}' || echo "checkpoint: discarded ($reason); resume at the first open bead of $s"
    92	    return 0
    93	  fi
    94	  if (( json )); then jq -c '{checkpoint: .checkpoint}' "$file"
    95	  else echo "checkpoint: $s ${t:+task $t }phase $p at $ts → resume at the first open bead after $t in $s"; fi
    96	}
    97	
    98	case "$sub" in
    99	  write) cmd_write ;;
   100	  read)  cmd_read ;;
   101	  *) usage ;;
   102	esac

     2	# =============================================================================
     3	# tools/check-knob-readers.sh — no direct read of a profile key outside
     4	# profile-lib.sh (cycle-129 SDD D-9.1, sprint-256 Task 2.7).
     5	#
     6	# Every key under any profile in .claude/data/profiles.yaml must be read
     7	# through `loa_knob` (.claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh), never by a reader's
     8	# own `yq '.<key> // <default>'`: a direct read skips the profile, and yq's
     9	# `//` reads an explicit `false` as absent. The check flags a line that names a
    10	# profile key in yq-path form (a leading dot: `.guardrails.input.enabled`)
    11	# under .claude/ (scripts, hooks, skills, data) and tools/, except
    12	# profile-lib.sh itself. Prose that names a key without the dot
    13	# (`guardrails.input.enabled: false`) is not a read and is not flagged.
    14	#
    15	# Misses: a key assembled at runtime (".guardrails.input.${x}.enabled") and a
    16	# reader in a language that indexes the config as nested keys.
    17	#
    18	# Usage: tools/check-knob-readers.sh [--root DIR]
    19	# Exit:  0 clean · 1 direct read found (each printed as path:line) · 2 usage
    20	# =============================================================================
    21	set -euo pipefail
    22	export LC_ALL=C
    23	
    24	ROOT="."
    25	while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
    26	  case "$1" in
    27	    --root) [[ $# -ge 2 ]] || { echo "check-knob-readers.sh: --root needs a directory" >&2; exit 2; }; ROOT="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    28	    -h|--help) sed -n '/^# Usage:/,/^# Exit:/p' "$0" | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//'; exit 0 ;;
    29	    *) echo "check-knob-readers.sh: unknown arg $1" >&2; exit 2 ;;
    30	  esac
    31	done
    32	PROFILES="$ROOT/.claude/data/profiles.yaml"
    33	[[ -f "$PROFILES" ]] || { echo "check-knob-readers.sh: $PROFILES not found" >&2; exit 2; }
    34	command -v yq >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "check-knob-readers.sh: yq v4 required" >&2; exit 2; }
    35	
    36	keys=$(yq -r '.profiles[] | keys | .[]' "$PROFILES" | sort -u)
    37	[[ -n "$keys" ]] || { echo "check-knob-readers.sh: no profile keys in $PROFILES" >&2; exit 2; }

    39	# not itself part of an identifier (start of line, quote, space, paren, ...).
    40	alt=$(printf '%s\n' "$keys" | sed 's/\./\\./g' | paste -sd'|' -)
    41	pattern="(^|[^A-Za-z0-9_])\\.(${alt})([^A-Za-z0-9_]|$)"
