1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# =============================================================================
     3	# implement-gate.sh — Dual-mode compliance hook for App Zone writes (FR-7)
     4	# =============================================================================
     5	# Checks whether Write/Edit to App Zone files occurs within an active
     6	# /implement or /bug skill invocation.
     7	#
     8	# Two detection modes:
     9	#   1. HEURISTIC (ADVISORY, the default): reads .run/ state files for RUNNING state
    10	#   2. AUTHORITATIVE: reads tool_input.active_skill from hook stdin, only when
    11	#      .loa.config.yaml sets implement_gate.mode: authoritative. The PreToolUse
    12	#      payload carries no harness-set skill field (cycle-126 D-4.4) and tool_input
    13	#      is model-authored, so nothing in .run/ selects this mode.
    14	#      TIGHTEN-ONLY (sprint-250 audit n17/n18): the model-authored claim can only
    15	#      add an ask, never grant an allow. A claimed implementation skill falls
    16	#      through to the heuristic exactly like an absent field; a claimed
    17	#      non-implementation skill asks and logs compliance.mode.model_signal to
    18	#      .run/audit.jsonl (plain hook log, not the signed audit_emit chain). Every
    19	#      claim leaves one row per invocation: decision "ask" for a non-implementation
    20	#      claim, decision "heuristic" for an implementation claim (run-2 finding 6).
    21	#
    22	# Evidence recorder (cycle-126 D-4.4): a lead-session payload carrying
    23	# tool_input.active_skill records active_skill_seen_at once in
    24	# .run/platform-features.json. It is evidence only and never changes the mode.
    25	#
    26	# Failure mode: FAIL-ASK for App Zone writes (not fail-open). A payload jq cannot
    27	# parse (or no jq), or a file_path that cannot be canonicalised, asks too (run-2
    28	# findings 1/5). The path is tool_input.file_path, or tool_input.notebook_path for
    29	# NotebookEdit; a relative path resolves from the payload's cwd, else PROJECT_ROOT
    30	# (run-3 finding 6). The zone test ORs a physical form (symlinks followed) and a
    31	# logical form (symlinks kept) and matches a lowercased copy (run-3 findings 1/2).
    32	# Root: PROJECT_ROOT, else CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR, else this script's location
    33	# (<root>/.claude/hooks/compliance/), never the process cwd, which follows
    34	# Claude's `cd` (audit MED-001); RUN_DIR defaults to <root>/.run.
    35	# Trust inputs: a write to .run/state.json, .run/sprint-plan-state.json,
    36	# .run/simstim-state.json, .run/platform-features.json, .run/audit.jsonl or
    37	# .loa.config.yaml asks and logs compliance.state_write (run-3 finding 3).
    38	# Other non-App-Zone writes always allowed.
    39	#
    40	# Output (Claude Code PreToolUse contract, sprint-250 audit n20): allow = silent
    41	# exit 0 with empty stdout; ask = exit 0 with
    42	#   {"hookSpecificOutput":{"hookEventName":"PreToolUse","permissionDecision":"ask","permissionDecisionReason":"…"}}
    43	# A top-level "decision" accepts approve|block only, so "ask" never goes there.
    44	# file_path and active_skill reach stderr only through strip_controls (n21;
    45	# run-2 findings 3/12; run-3 finding 5): cut to 256 bytes without splitting a
    46	# character, then C0 and DEL, UTF-8 C1 controls and the Unicode format/bidi/tag
    47	# code points are removed to a fixed point. Audit rows record the RAW values cut
    48	# the same way and written with jq -a, so every non-ASCII code point is \uXXXX:
    49	# faithful (implement+U+200B logs as implement\u200b) and terminal-safe (run-3 finding 4).
    50	#
    51	# IMPORTANT: No set -euo pipefail — hook must never crash-block.
    52	# Parse/read errors on App Zone writes → ask (not allow).
    53	#
    54	# Part of cycle-049/050: Upstream Platform Alignment (FR-7)
    55	# Red Team findings addressed: ATK-005 (state tampering), ATK-006 (fail-open),
    56	#   ATK-007 (prompt injection via file path)
    57	# Sprint-108 T4.4: Dual-mode (authoritative + heuristic)
    58	# Sprint-108 T4.5: Path normalization
    59	# =============================================================================
    60	
    61	# Read tool input from stdin
    62	input=$(cat 2>/dev/null) || input=""
    63	
    64	# The ask reply; jq builds it so any reason is a well-formed JSON string (run-3 finding 7); the printf literal is only
    65	# for the jq-missing branch, whose reason is a fixed string
    66	emit_ask() {
    67	    if command -v jq &>/dev/null; then
    68	        jq -nc --arg r "$1" '{hookSpecificOutput:{hookEventName:"PreToolUse",permissionDecision:"ask",permissionDecisionReason:$r}}'
    69	    else
    70	        printf '{"hookSpecificOutput":{"hookEventName":"PreToolUse","permissionDecision":"ask","permissionDecisionReason":"%s"}}\n' "$1"
    71	    fi
    72	}
    73	
    74	# Byte sequences strip_controls removes: UTF-8 C1 controls (C2 80..C2 9F) and the format/bidi code points
    75	# U+200B-U+200F, U+2028-U+202E, U+2060-U+2064, U+2066-U+206F, U+FEFF, U+00AD, U+061C, U+180E, U+FE00-U+FE0F,
    76	# U+FFF9-U+FFFB and the tag characters U+E0001, U+E0020-U+E007F (run-3 finding 5); each sequence starts with a lead
    77	# byte, so a byte-wise match never lands inside another character
    78	# printf -v keeps this portable (no GNU-sed \x); built on first use, not on every Write/Edit (BB-008)
    79	_IG_STRIP_SEQS=()
    80	_ig_strip_seqs_init() {
    81	    local _ig_i _ig_hex _ig_seq
    82	    for (( _ig_i = 128; _ig_i < 160; _ig_i++ )); do
    83	        printf -v _ig_hex '%02x' "$_ig_i"; printf -v _ig_seq "\\xc2\\x${_ig_hex}"; _IG_STRIP_SEQS+=("$_ig_seq")
    84	    done
    85	    for _ig_hex in 8b 8c 8d 8e 8f a8 a9 aa ab ac ad ae; do
    86	        printf -v _ig_seq "\\xe2\\x80\\x${_ig_hex}"; _IG_STRIP_SEQS+=("$_ig_seq")
    87	    done
    88	    for _ig_hex in a0 a1 a2 a3 a4 a6 a7 a8 a9 aa ab ac ad ae af; do
    89	        printf -v _ig_seq "\\xe2\\x81\\x${_ig_hex}"; _IG_STRIP_SEQS+=("$_ig_seq")
    90	    done
    91	    for _ig_seq in '\xef\xbb\xbf' '\xc2\xad' '\xd8\x9c' '\xe1\xa0\x8e' '\xef\xbf\xb9' '\xef\xbf\xba' '\xef\xbf\xbb' '\xf3\xa0\x80\x81'; do
    92	        printf -v _ig_seq "$_ig_seq"; _IG_STRIP_SEQS+=("$_ig_seq")
    93	    done
    94	    for (( _ig_i = 128; _ig_i < 144; _ig_i++ )); do   # U+FE00-U+FE0F = EF B8 80..EF B8 8F
    95	        printf -v _ig_hex '%02x' "$_ig_i"; printf -v _ig_seq "\\xef\\xb8\\x${_ig_hex}"; _IG_STRIP_SEQS+=("$_ig_seq")
    96	    done
    97	    for (( _ig_i = 160; _ig_i < 192; _ig_i++ )); do   # U+E0020-U+E003F = F3 A0 80 A0..F3 A0 80 BF
    98	        printf -v _ig_hex '%02x' "$_ig_i"; printf -v _ig_seq "\\xf3\\xa0\\x80\\x${_ig_hex}"; _IG_STRIP_SEQS+=("$_ig_seq")
    99	    done
   100	    for (( _ig_i = 128; _ig_i < 192; _ig_i++ )); do   # U+E0040-U+E007F = F3 A0 81 80..F3 A0 81 BF
   101	        printf -v _ig_hex '%02x' "$_ig_i"; printf -v _ig_seq "\\xf3\\xa0\\x81\\x${_ig_hex}"; _IG_STRIP_SEQS+=("$_ig_seq")
   102	    done
   103	}
   104	
   105	# Sets the variable named $1 to at most 256 bytes of $2, never ending inside a UTF-8 character: a trailing lead byte
   106	# whose sequence the cut left short, or stray continuation bytes, are dropped (run-3 finding 5; jq would read a split
   107	# character as U+FFFD). printf -v, not $(...), so a trailing newline in a raw value survives into the audit row
   108	cut_utf8_256() {
   109	    local LC_ALL=C
   110	    local _c_s=${2:0:256} _c_n _c_i _c_b _c_need
   111	    _c_n=${#_c_s}
   112	    for (( _c_i = _c_n - 1; _c_i >= 0 && _c_i >= _c_n - 4; _c_i-- )); do
   113	        printf -v _c_b '%d' "'${_c_s:_c_i:1}"
   114	        (( _c_b >= 128 && _c_b < 192 )) && continue   # continuation byte: keep walking back to its lead
   115	        if (( _c_b < 128 )); then _c_need=1; elif (( _c_b < 224 )); then _c_need=2; elif (( _c_b < 240 )); then _c_need=3; else _c_need=4; fi
   116	        if (( _c_n - _c_i < _c_need )); then _c_s=${_c_s:0:_c_i}          # the cut left this character short
   117	        elif (( _c_n - _c_i > _c_need )); then _c_s=${_c_s:0:_c_i+_c_need}   # continuation bytes after a complete character are stray
   118	        fi
   119	        printf -v "$1" '%s' "$_c_s"
   120	        return 0
   121	    done
   122	    printf -v "$1" '%s' "${_c_s:0:_c_i+1}"   # only continuation bytes at the end: drop them
   123	}
   124	
   125	# Display copy of a model-authored string: cut to 256 bytes first (the fixed point below then costs at most a few
   126	# passes over a short string), then C0 and DEL, then the sequences above byte-wise until nothing changes (deleting
   127	# one sequence can join its neighbours into another: C2 C2 9B 9B)
   128	strip_controls() {
   129	    local LC_ALL=C s prev seq
   130	    cut_utf8_256 s "$1"
   131	    s=$(printf '%s' "$s" | tr -d '\000-\037\177')
   132	    (( ${#_IG_STRIP_SEQS[@]} )) || _ig_strip_seqs_init
   133	    while :; do
   134	        prev=$s
   135	        for seq in "${_IG_STRIP_SEQS[@]}"; do s=${s//"$seq"/}; done
   136	        [[ "$s" == "$prev" ]] && break
   137	    done
   138	    printf '%s' "$s"
   139	}
   140	
   141	# The root never follows the process cwd, which follows Claude's `cd` (sprint-250 audit MED-001): PROJECT_ROOT, then
   142	# the harness's CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR (it stays at the session's project root), then this script's own location
   143	# (<root>/.claude/hooks/compliance/)
   144	PROJECT_ROOT="${PROJECT_ROOT:-${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR:-$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../../.." 2>/dev/null && pwd)}}"
   145	RUN_DIR="${RUN_DIR:-$PROJECT_ROOT/.run}"
   146	FEATURES_FILE="$RUN_DIR/platform-features.json"
   147	
   148	# Evidence recorder: lead session only (no teammate role, no subagent agent_id), once, atomic.
   149	if [[ -z "${LOA_TEAM_MEMBER:-}" && -d "$RUN_DIR" ]] \
   150	    && jq -e '(.tool_input.active_skill // "") != "" and (.agent_id // "") == ""' <<<"$input" >/dev/null 2>&1 \
   151	    && ! jq -e '.active_skill_seen_at' "$FEATURES_FILE" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
   152	    _ig_base=$(jq -c 'select(type == "object")' "$FEATURES_FILE" 2>/dev/null | tail -n 1)
   153	    _ig_tmp=$(mktemp "$RUN_DIR/.platform-features.XXXXXX" 2>/dev/null) && {
   154	        jq -nc --argjson b "${_ig_base:-{\}}" --arg ts "$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)" \
   155	            '$b + {active_skill_available: false, active_skill_seen_at: $ts, active_skill_source: "tool_input"}' > "$_ig_tmp" 2>/dev/null \
   156	            && mv -f "$_ig_tmp" "$FEATURES_FILE" 2>/dev/null
   157	        rm -f "$_ig_tmp" 2>/dev/null
   158	    }
   159	fi
   160	
   161	# No jq, or a payload jq cannot parse: the write cannot be evaluated, so ask (run-2 finding 5)
   162	if ! command -v jq &>/dev/null || ! jq -e . <<<"$input" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
   163	    echo "[GATE] could not evaluate tool_input (jq missing or payload unparsable)." >&2
   164	    emit_ask "[GATE] could not evaluate tool_input. Verify this write is intentional."
   165	    exit 0
   166	fi
   167	
   168	# Extract the path: Write/Edit/MultiEdit carry file_path, NotebookEdit carries notebook_path. jq -j plus a sentinel
   169	# byte keeps a trailing newline, which $(...) would otherwise strip from the raw value (run-3 finding 4)
   170	if ! file_path=$(jq -j '.tool_input.file_path // .tool_input.notebook_path // empty' <<<"$input" 2>/dev/null && printf x); then
   171	    echo "[GATE] could not evaluate tool_input (path not readable)." >&2
   172	    emit_ask "[GATE] could not evaluate tool_input. Verify this write is intentional."
   173	    exit 0
   174	fi
   175	file_path=${file_path%x}
   176	
   177	# A parsed payload without a path is not a file write the gate can classify: allow
   178	if [[ -z "$file_path" ]]; then
   179	    exit 0
   180	fi
   181	
   182	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   183	# Source compat-lib.sh for _date_to_epoch()
   184	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   185	SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd 2>/dev/null)" || SCRIPT_DIR=""
   186	COMPAT_LIB="${SCRIPT_DIR}/../../scripts/compat-lib.sh"
   187	# shellcheck source=../../scripts/compat-lib.sh
   188	source "$COMPAT_LIB" 2>/dev/null || true
   189	
   190	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   191	# T4.5: Path normalization — canonicalise both sides, then take file_path
   192	# relative to the project root (run-2 finding 1). A textual prefix test let
   193	# /proc/self/cwd/src/x, //ROOT/src/x, ROOT/../<name>/src/x or a symlinked root
   194	# reach an App-Zone file unseen. Two forms are tested and either one matching
   195	# counts (run-3 finding 1): the PHYSICAL form follows symlinks (realpath -m,
   196	# else readlink -f) against pwd -P of the root; the LOGICAL form keeps them
   197	# (realpath -m -s, else a pure-bash ./../// normaliser) against pwd -L, so a
   198	# src/ that is itself a symlink out of the root still asks. A relative path
   199	# resolves from the payload's cwd when it carries one (the harness resolves it
   200	# there and cwd follows `cd` in the Bash tool), else from PROJECT_ROOT (run-3
   201	# finding 6). Only the part under the root is matched, so parent directory
   202	# names never count (e.g., /home/user/src-projects/loa/grimoires/file.md is not src/*).
   203	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   204	# Lexical normaliser for an absolute path: drops empty and . components, resolves .. textually, follows no symlink
   205	_ig_lexical_norm() {
   206	    local rest=$1 part
   207	    local -a out=()
   208	    while [[ -n "$rest" ]]; do
   209	        part=${rest%%/*}
   210	        if [[ "$rest" == */* ]]; then rest=${rest#*/}; else rest=""; fi
   211	        case "$part" in
   212	            ''|.) ;;
   213	            ..) (( ${#out[@]} )) && unset 'out[${#out[@]}-1]' ;;
   214	            *) out+=("$part") ;;
   215	        esac
   216	    done
   217	    local IFS=/
   218	    printf '/%s' "${out[*]}"
   219	}
   220	
   221	# $1 relative to the root $2, or failure when $1 is not under $2
   222	_ig_under_root() {
   223	    [[ "$1" == "${2%/}/"* ]] || return 1
   224	    printf '%s' "${1#"${2%/}"/}"
   225	}
   226	
   227	canonical_root=$(cd "$PROJECT_ROOT" 2>/dev/null && pwd -P) || canonical_root=""
   228	logical_root=$(cd "$PROJECT_ROOT" 2>/dev/null && pwd -L) || logical_root=""
   229	payload_cwd=$(jq -r '.cwd // empty | strings' <<<"$input" 2>/dev/null) || payload_cwd=""
   230	if [[ "$file_path" == /* ]]; then
   231	    abs_path=$file_path
   232	else
   233	    base_dir=${payload_cwd:-$logical_root}
   234	    [[ "$base_dir" == /* ]] || base_dir="$logical_root/$base_dir"
   235	    abs_path="${base_dir%/}/$file_path"
   236	fi
   237	canonical_path=""
   238	logical_path=""
   239	if [[ -n "$canonical_root" && -n "$logical_root" ]]; then
   240	    # GNU realpath -m first (no component needs to exist), then readlink -f
   241	    canonical_path=$(cd "$PROJECT_ROOT" 2>/dev/null \
   242	        && { realpath -m -- "$abs_path" 2>/dev/null || readlink -f -- "$abs_path" 2>/dev/null; }) || canonical_path=""
   243	    logical_path=$(realpath -m -s -- "$abs_path" 2>/dev/null) || logical_path=""
   244	    [[ "$logical_path" == /* ]] || logical_path=$(_ig_lexical_norm "$abs_path")
   245	fi
   246	if [[ -z "$canonical_root" || -z "$canonical_path" ]]; then
   247	    echo "[GATE] could not canonicalise tool_input.file_path; asking." >&2
   248	    emit_ask "[GATE] could not canonicalise tool_input.file_path. Verify this write is intentional."
   249	    exit 0
   250	fi
   251	
   252	# The root-relative forms, lowercased: on a case-insensitive filesystem (macOS default, ext4 casefold) Src/ is src/,
   253	# and on a case-sensitive one this only adds asks for a directory literally named Src/ — tighten-only (run-3 finding 2)
   254	# bash 3.2 has no lowercase parameter expansion (BB-001: a bad substitution there left rel_forms empty and the hook exited 0); LC_ALL=C so a
   255	# BSD tr never stops at a byte that is not valid UTF-8 ("Illegal byte sequence") — the patterns are ASCII
   256	_ig_lower() { printf '%s' "$1" | LC_ALL=C tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]'; }
   257	rel_forms=()
   258	if rel=$(_ig_under_root "$canonical_path" "$canonical_root"); then rel_forms+=("$(_ig_lower "$rel")"); fi

   260	
   261	# Audit-row copy of a model-authored value: raw, cut to 256 bytes on a character boundary; jq -a escapes the rest
   262	cut_utf8_256 audit_file_path "$file_path"
   263	
   264	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   265	# Trust inputs (run-3 finding 3): the files this gate and the run state read are
   266	# writable through the same tool, so a write to one asks and leaves one
   267	# compliance.state_write row — evaluated before the App-Zone test, since they
   268	# are not App Zone. Everything else under .run/ and grimoires/ stays allow.
   269	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   270	for rel in "${rel_forms[@]}"; do
   271	    case "$rel" in
   272	        .run/state.json|.run/sprint-plan-state.json|.run/simstim-state.json|.run/platform-features.json|.run/audit.jsonl|.loa.config.yaml)

   274	            jq -nca \
   275	                --arg ts "$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ 2>/dev/null || echo unknown)" \
   276	                --arg path "$audit_file_path" \
   277	                '{timestamp: $ts, event: "compliance.state_write", file_path: $path}' \
   278	                >> "$RUN_DIR/audit.jsonl" 2>/dev/null || true
   279	            emit_ask "[GATE] write to an implement-gate trust input. Verify this write is intentional."
   280	            exit 0
   281	            ;;
   282	    esac
   283	done
   284	
   285	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   286	# Zone check: Is this an App Zone write?
   287	# App Zone: src/, lib/, app/ in either root-relative form; a path whose two
   288	# forms both fall outside the root is not App Zone

   291	for normalized_path in "${rel_forms[@]}"; do
   292	    case "$normalized_path" in
   293	        src/*|lib/*|app/*|*/src/*|*/lib/*|*/app/*)
   294	            is_app_zone=true
   295	            ;;
   296	    esac
   297	done
   298	
   299	# Non-App-Zone writes always allowed
   300	if [[ "$is_app_zone" == "false" ]]; then
   301	    exit 0
   302	fi
   303	
   304	# Display copy only: control and format characters never reach stderr (n21, run-2 finding 3)
   305	safe_file_path=$(strip_controls "$file_path")
   306	
   307	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   308	# Mode: heuristic unless the operator opts in through .loa.config.yaml (cycle-126 D-4.4)

   310	compliance_mode="heuristic"
   311	if command -v yq &>/dev/null && [[ -f "$PROJECT_ROOT/.loa.config.yaml" ]]; then
   312	    configured_mode=$(yq '.implement_gate.mode // ""' "$PROJECT_ROOT/.loa.config.yaml" 2>/dev/null) || configured_mode=""
   313	    [[ "${configured_mode//\"/}" == "authoritative" ]] && compliance_mode="authoritative"
   314	fi
   315	
   316	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   317	# Authoritative mode: read active_skill from hook input
   318	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   319	if [[ "$compliance_mode" == "authoritative" ]]; then
   320	    active_skill=$(jq -j '.tool_input.active_skill // empty' <<<"$input" 2>/dev/null && printf x) || active_skill="x"
   321	    active_skill=${active_skill%x}
   322	
   323	    if [[ -n "$active_skill" ]]; then
   324	        safe_skill=$(strip_controls "$active_skill")
   325	        cut_utf8_256 audit_skill "$active_skill"
   326	        # One model_signal row per invocation that carries a claim; the harness never sets the field,
   327	        # so a row means a model wrote it (run-2 finding 6). The row holds the raw claim, ASCII-escaped (run-3 finding 4)
   328	        log_model_signal() {
   329	            jq -nca \
   330	                --arg ts "$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ 2>/dev/null || echo unknown)" \
   331	                --arg skill "$audit_skill" \
   332	                --arg path "$audit_file_path" \
   333	                --arg decision "$1" \
   334	                '{timestamp: $ts, event: "compliance.mode.model_signal", mode: "authoritative", active_skill: $skill, file_path: $path, decision: $decision}' \
   335	                >> "$RUN_DIR/audit.jsonl" 2>/dev/null || true
   336	        }
   337	        case "$active_skill" in
   338	            implement|/implement|bug|/bug|run|/run|simstim|/simstim)
   339	                # Tighten-only (n17/n18): a model-authored implementation claim never
   340	                # allows by itself — log it, then fall through to the heuristic check below
   341	                log_model_signal heuristic
   342	                ;;
   343	            *)
   344	                # Non-implementation skill — log the model signal and ask
   345	                echo "[AUTHORITATIVE] App Zone write to '$safe_file_path' detected during /$safe_skill (not an implementation skill)." >&2

   347	                emit_ask "[AUTHORITATIVE] App Zone write outside implementation skill. Verify this is intentional."

   349	                ;;
   350	        esac
   351	    else
   352	        # active_skill field absent despite authoritative mode — fall back to heuristic

   354	        log_ts=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ 2>/dev/null) || log_ts="unknown"

   356	            jq -nc \
   357	                --arg ts "$log_ts" \
   358	                --arg from "authoritative" \
   359	                --arg to "heuristic" \
   360	                --arg reason "active_skill field absent in hook input" \
   361	                '{timestamp: $ts, event: "compliance.mode.fallback", from_mode: $from, to_mode: $to, reason: $reason}' \
   362	                >> "$RUN_DIR/audit.jsonl" 2>/dev/null || true
   363	        else
   364	            echo "{\"timestamp\":\"$log_ts\",\"event\":\"compliance.mode.fallback\",\"from_mode\":\"authoritative\",\"to_mode\":\"heuristic\",\"reason\":\"active_skill field absent in hook input\"}" \
   365	                >> "$RUN_DIR/audit.jsonl" 2>/dev/null || true
   366	        fi
   367	    fi
   368	    # Fall through to heuristic check below
   369	fi
   370	
   371	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   372	# Heuristic mode: Is an /implement or /bug skill currently active?
   373	# Check .run/sprint-plan-state.json, .run/simstim-state.json, .run/state.json
   374	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   375	# True when the ISO-8601 timestamp $1 parses and is within 24 h (86400 s) of now, either side; empty or unparsable is stale
   376	# (sprint-250 audit LOW-004: tighten-only; LOW-006: a future-dated stamp is not fresh forever)
   377	_ig_fresh() {
   378	    [[ -n "$1" ]] || return 1
   379	    local now last_epoch
   380	    now=$(date +%s 2>/dev/null) || return 1
   381	    if type _date_to_epoch &>/dev/null; then
   382	        last_epoch=$(_date_to_epoch "$1" 2>/dev/null) || last_epoch=""
   383	    else
   384	        last_epoch=$(date -d "$1" +%s 2>/dev/null || date -jf '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ' "$1" +%s 2>/dev/null) || last_epoch=""
   385	    fi
   386	    [[ "$last_epoch" =~ ^[0-9]+$ && "$now" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || return 1
   387	    (( last_epoch > 0 && now - last_epoch <= 86400 && last_epoch - now <= 86400 ))
   388	}
   389	
   390	check_implementation_active() {
   391	    # Check sprint-plan state
   392	    if [[ -f "$RUN_DIR/sprint-plan-state.json" ]]; then
   393	        local state plan_id last_activity
   394	        state=$(jq -r '.state // empty' "$RUN_DIR/sprint-plan-state.json" 2>/dev/null) || return 1
   395	        plan_id=$(jq -r '.plan_id // empty' "$RUN_DIR/sprint-plan-state.json" 2>/dev/null) || true
   396	
   397	        # Integrity: must have plan_id
   398	        if [[ -z "$plan_id" ]]; then
   399	            return 1
   400	        fi
   401	
   402	        # Integrity: check staleness (within 24 h either side, via _ig_fresh); an absent or unparsable
   403	        # last_activity is stale too (sprint-250 audit LOW-006: the check was skipped, so RUNNING + plan_id allowed)
   404	        last_activity=$(jq -r '.timestamps.last_activity // empty' "$RUN_DIR/sprint-plan-state.json" 2>/dev/null) || last_activity=""
   405	        if ! _ig_fresh "$last_activity"; then
   406	            return 1  # Stale, future-dated or unstamped state
   407	        fi
   408	
   409	        if [[ "$state" == "RUNNING" ]]; then
   410	            return 0
   411	        fi
   412	    fi
   413	
   414	    # Check simstim state; its writers (simstim-state.sh, simstim-orchestrator.sh) stamp .timestamps.last_activity,
   415	    # and a stale or unstamped file falls through (LOW-004)
   416	    if [[ -f "$RUN_DIR/simstim-state.json" ]]; then
   417	        local phase simstim_activity
   418	        phase=$(jq -r '.phase // empty' "$RUN_DIR/simstim-state.json" 2>/dev/null) || return 1
   419	        simstim_activity=$(jq -r '.timestamps.last_activity // empty | strings' "$RUN_DIR/simstim-state.json" 2>/dev/null) || simstim_activity=""
   420	        if [[ "$phase" == "implementation" ]] && _ig_fresh "$simstim_activity"; then
   421	            return 0
   422	        fi
   423	    fi
   424	
   425	    # Check run state; run-mode stamps .timestamps.last_activity (state-schemas.md), .updated_at is the fallback
   426	    # run-preflight.sh reads too; a stale or unstamped file falls through (LOW-004)
   427	    if [[ -f "$RUN_DIR/state.json" ]]; then
   428	        local run_state run_activity
   429	        run_state=$(jq -r '.state // empty' "$RUN_DIR/state.json" 2>/dev/null) || return 1
   430	        run_activity=$(jq -r '.timestamps.last_activity // .updated_at // empty | strings' "$RUN_DIR/state.json" 2>/dev/null) || run_activity=""
   431	        if [[ "$run_state" == "RUNNING" ]] && _ig_fresh "$run_activity"; then
   432	            return 0
   433	        fi
   434	    fi
   435	
   436	    return 1
   437	}
   438	
   439	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   440	# Decision: allow or ask
   441	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   442	if check_implementation_active; then
   443	    # Implementation is active — allow the write
   444	    exit 0
   445	else
   446	    # No active implementation detected — ADVISORY ask
   447	    echo "[ADVISORY] App Zone write to '$safe_file_path' detected outside active /implement or /bug." >&2
   448	    echo "No RUNNING state found in .run/ state files. This may bypass review gates." >&2
   449	    echo '{"hookSpecificOutput":{"hookEventName":"PreToolUse","permissionDecision":"ask","permissionDecisionReason":"[ADVISORY] App Zone write outside active implementation. Verify this is intentional."}}'
   450	    exit 0
   451	fi

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# =============================================================================
3	# run-checkpoint.sh — run position in .run/ (cycle-125 FR-3, SDD D-3.2;
4	# cycle-129 FR-4(f)/FR-5, SDD D-4.6, D-5.1 … D-5.4). Beads are the task ledger;
5	# the checkpoint is a HINT; the run state and the breaker are caches DERIVED
6	# from files (COMPLETED markers, LOA-VERDICT trailers, the ledger, git).
7	#
8	#   run-checkpoint.sh write --sprint sprint-N --phase PHASE [--task BEAD-ID] [--file F]
9	#       Atomically sets .schema_version = 2, .checkpoint = {sprint, task, phase, ts}
10	#       and .timestamps.last_activity = ts: jq → F.tmp.$$ → mv -f, under flock
11	#       on F.lock. F must already exist (a run in progress). Then runs
12	#       `derive --write` (a missing ledger is skipped). Exit 0 · 2 usage /
13	#       no run · 3 write failed (the previous file is untouched).
14	#   run-checkpoint.sh read [--file F] [--json]
15	#       Prints the checkpoint when it is trustworthy: parses, and when a task
16	#       is named, `br show <task> --json` reports it closed (a checkpoint that
17	#       names an open or unknown bead is DISCARDED with a logged line — beads
18	#       remain the recovery source). schema_version 1 / no checkpoint → prints
19	#       "sprint granularity". Exit 0 always when F exists; 2 when it does not.
20	#   run-checkpoint.sh derive [--json] [--write] [--root DIR] [--file F]
21	#       For the ledger's active cycle, per sprint: global_id, local_label,
22	#       ledger status, completed_marker (a2a/sprint-<gid>/COMPLETED exists and
23	#       the feedback trailers name this sprint, as sprint-<gid> or the local
24	#       label; a trailer or a `sprint:` line naming another sprint makes it a
25	#       stale_marker, treated as absent), review/audit verdicts (verdict-derive.sh;
26	#       APPROVED needs exit 0; a file without a trailer is legacy: no verdict,
27	#       listed in derivation.legacy_feedback), impl_commit (newest non-merge
28	#       commit on HEAD since max(sprint started|created, cycle created) touching
29	#       a path outside grimoires/, .run/, REPO-MAP.md, checksums.json,
30	#       CHANGELOG.md) and state complete | awaiting_marker | in_progress.
31	#       Run state, first match wins:
32	#         cache .state or .status JACKED_OUT, or .completion.merged_sha → JACKED_OUT (terminal)
33	#         breaker OPEN, or cache HALTED                                 → HALTED (sticky until /run-resume)
34	#         every sprint complete                                         → COMPLETE
35	#         cache COMPLETE and the ledger registers no new incomplete sprint → COMPLETE
36	#         last_activity within run_mode.stale_hours (12)                → RUNNING
37	#         otherwise                                                     → INTERRUPTED
38	#       Breaker (active sprint = first incomplete, else the last): the ordered
39	#       rounds engineer-feedback-r*.md, auditor-sprint-feedback-r*.md and the
40	#       current files (sorted by trailer ts, round, gate; rounds before the
41	#       breaker's reset_at are ignored) give cycle_count (non-APPROVED rounds),
42	#       same_issue (consecutive equal hashes) and no_progress (consecutive
43	#       equal counts); each cached counter is raised to its recomputed value,
44	#       never lowered; OPEN when a count threshold is met (timeout is left to
45	#       record-round). --json prints the derivation; --write rewrites F
46	#       (.state canonical, .status mirrored, derived_at, derivation {source,
47	#       stale_markers, legacy_feedback, sprint_ids}; schema_version kept) and
48	#       the breaker, under their locks — only when F exists, parses, and
49	#       run_mode.file_authoritative is not false (false = report-only).
50	#       Exit 0 · 4 no ledger / no active cycle · 2 usage.
51	#   run-checkpoint.sh record-round --gate review|audit --file FEEDBACK [--sprint sprint-N]
52	#                                  [--state-file F] [--breaker B]
53	#       After a review or audit: verdict-derive.sh --json on FEEDBACK; the
54	#       same-issue hash is md5 of `jq -Sc '{verdict,counts}'` of that output
55	#       (no trailer: md5 of the first 50 lines from ## Findings / ## Issues /
56	#       ## Changes Required). APPROVED (exit 0) leaves every counter as is.
57	#       Otherwise, atomically on B: same_issue +1 when the hash equals
58	#       last_hash, else count 1 and last_hash = hash; no_progress +1 when the
59	#       counts equal the previous round's, else 0; cycle_count.current +1; then
60	#       the triggers in order same_issue ≥ threshold, no_progress ≥ threshold,
61	#       cycle_count ≥ limit, timeout (now - started ≥ limit_hours). A trip sets
62	#       state OPEN, appends history {timestamp, trigger, reason, gate, sprint},
63	#       sets F (.run/state.json) .state = HALTED, prints
64	#       `TRIPPED: <trigger>: <reason>` and exits 10 (also when B is already OPEN).
65	#       Exit 0 recorded · 2 usage / missing file · 3 write failed · 10 tripped.
66	#   run-checkpoint.sh mark --skill implement|bug --sprint ID [--root DIR]
67	#       Writes .run/implement-active.json {skill, sprint, started_at} (the
68	#       implement gate's marker sanction, valid two hours), then runs
69	#       `derive --write` when F exists. `unmark` removes the marker. Exit 0 · 2 usage.
70	#
71	# Default F: $LOA_RUN_DIR/sprint-plan-state.json, else <root>/.run/sprint-plan-state.json
72	# (--root DIR sets <root> and ignores LOA_RUN_DIR). B: <run dir>/circuit-breaker.json.
73	# Readers accept schema_version 1 and 2 and files without derived_at/derivation.
74	# Config (<root>/.loa.config.yaml, yq; absent = defaults): run_mode.stale_hours (12),
75	# run_mode.file_authoritative (true), run_mode.circuit_breaker.{same_issue,no_progress}_threshold
76	# (3, 5), run_mode.defaults.{max_cycles,timeout_hours} (20, 8) for a new breaker file.
77	# =============================================================================
78	set -euo pipefail
79	export LC_ALL=C
80	SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
81	VERDICT_DERIVE="$SCRIPT_DIR/verdict-derive.sh"
82	usage() { sed -n '3,/^# Default F/p' "$0" | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//' >&2; exit 2; }
83	
84	sub="${1:-}"; [[ -n "$sub" ]] || usage; shift
85	file="" sprint="" task="" phase="" json=0 write=0 root="" gate="" state_file="" breaker="" skill=""
86	while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
87	  case "$1" in
88	    --file)   [[ $# -ge 2 && -n "$2" ]] || usage; file="$2"; shift 2 ;;
89	    --sprint) [[ $# -ge 2 && "$2" =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$ ]] || usage; sprint="$2"; shift 2 ;;
90	    --task)   [[ $# -ge 2 && "$2" =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$ ]] || usage; task="$2"; shift 2 ;;
91	    --phase)  [[ $# -ge 2 && "$2" =~ ^[A-Z_]+$ ]] || usage; phase="$2"; shift 2 ;;
92	    --json)   json=1; shift ;;
93	    --write)  write=1; shift ;;
94	    --root)   [[ $# -ge 2 && -d "${2:-}" ]] || usage; root="$(cd "$2" && pwd)"; shift 2 ;;
95	    --gate)   [[ $# -ge 2 && ( "$2" == review || "$2" == audit ) ]] || usage; gate="$2"; shift 2 ;;
96	    --state-file|--file-state) [[ $# -ge 2 && -n "$2" ]] || usage; state_file="$2"; shift 2 ;;
97	    --breaker) [[ $# -ge 2 && -n "$2" ]] || usage; breaker="$2"; shift 2 ;;
98	    --skill)  [[ $# -ge 2 && ( "$2" == implement || "$2" == bug ) ]] || usage; skill="$2"; shift 2 ;;
99	    *) usage ;;
100	  esac
101	done
102	
103	# Root and run dir: --root wins (and pins the run dir under it); else the
104	# directory holding a --file that sits in a .run/ dir (write/read/derive only);
105	# else this script's checkout with $LOA_RUN_DIR honoured.
106	if [[ -n "$root" ]]; then
107	  run_dir="$root/.run"
108	else
109	  root="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
110	  run_dir="${LOA_RUN_DIR:-$root/.run}"
111	  if [[ -n "$file" && "$sub" != record-round ]]; then
112	    fdir="$(cd "$(dirname "$file")" 2>/dev/null && pwd)" || fdir=""
113	    if [[ -n "$fdir" && "$(basename "$fdir")" == .run ]]; then root="$(dirname "$fdir")"; run_dir="$fdir"; fi
114	  fi
115	fi
116	if [[ "$sub" != record-round && -z "$file" ]]; then file="$run_dir/sprint-plan-state.json"; fi
117	[[ -n "$breaker" ]] || breaker="$run_dir/circuit-breaker.json"
118	[[ -n "$state_file" ]] || state_file="$run_dir/state.json"
119	CONFIG="$root/.loa.config.yaml"

121	now_iso() { date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ; }
122	
123	# cfg KEY → the raw yq value ("null" when absent or unreadable). yq's `//`
124	# treats false as absent, so callers compare the raw text.
125	cfg() {
126	  local v
127	  if command -v yq >/dev/null 2>&1 && [[ -f "$CONFIG" ]]; then
128	    v=$(yq "$1" "$CONFIG" 2>/dev/null) || v="null"
129	    printf '%s' "${v//\"/}"
130	  else
131	    printf 'null'
132	  fi
133	}
134	cfg_int() {  # KEY DEFAULT MAX → a positive integer ≤ MAX, else DEFAULT
135	  local v; v=$(cfg "$1")
136	  if [[ "$v" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] && (( v > 0 && v <= $3 )); then printf '%s' "$v"; else printf '%s' "$2"; fi

139	_md5() { if command -v md5sum >/dev/null 2>&1; then md5sum | cut -d' ' -f1; else md5 -q; fi; }

141	# atomic_update FILE JQ-ARGS... — jq over FILE (or {} when FILE is absent) →
142	# FILE.tmp.$$ → mv -f, under flock on FILE.lock. Exit 3 on any failure; the
143	# previous file is untouched.
144	atomic_update() {
145	  local f="$1"; shift
146	  local tmp="$f.tmp.$$" rc=0
147	  (
148	    # flock is util-linux (Linux); without it (macOS) the write is still atomic
149	    # (tmp + mv) but concurrent writers may interleave — last writer wins.
150	    if command -v flock >/dev/null 2>&1; then flock -w 5 9 || { echo "run-checkpoint: lock timeout on $f.lock" >&2; exit 3; }; fi
151	    if [[ -f "$f" ]]; then
152	      jq "$@" "$f" > "$tmp" 2>/dev/null || { rm -f -- "$tmp"; echo "run-checkpoint: $f is not valid JSON — not written" >&2; exit 3; }
153	    else
154	      jq "$@" <<<'{}' > "$tmp" 2>/dev/null || { rm -f -- "$tmp"; echo "run-checkpoint: could not build $f" >&2; exit 3; }
155	    fi
156	    jq -e . "$tmp" >/dev/null 2>&1 || { rm -f -- "$tmp"; echo "run-checkpoint: refusing to replace $f with unparseable output" >&2; exit 3; }
157	    mv -f -- "$tmp" "$f"
158	  ) 9>"$f.lock" || rc=$?
159	  return $rc
160	}

162	cmd_write() {
163	  [[ -n "$sprint" && -n "$phase" ]] || usage
164	  if [[ ! -f "$file" ]]; then echo "run-checkpoint: no run state at $file (start a run first)" >&2; return 2; fi
165	  local ts rc=0
166	  ts=$(now_iso)
167	  atomic_update "$file" --arg s "$sprint" --arg t "$task" --arg p "$phase" --arg ts "$ts" \
168	    '.schema_version = 2
169	     | .checkpoint = {sprint: $s, task: (if $t == "" then null else $t end), phase: $p, ts: $ts}
170	     | .timestamps = ((.timestamps // {}) + {last_activity: $ts})' || rc=$?
171	  (( rc == 0 )) || return $rc
172	  # Every checkpoint refreshes the derived caches (D-5.2); a missing ledger (4) is not an error here
173	  local err drc=0
174	  err=$( { write=1; json=0; cmd_derive >/dev/null; } 2>&1 ) || drc=$?
175	  if (( drc != 0 && drc != 4 )); then printf '%s\n' "$err" >&2; fi
176	  return 0
177	}
178	
179	bead_closed() {  # $1 bead id → 0 when br reports closed
180	  command -v br >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 2
181	  local js st
182	  js=$(br show "$1" --json 2>/dev/null) || return 1
183	  st=$(printf '%s' "$js" | jq -r 'if type=="array" then .[0] else . end | .status // .issue.status // empty' 2>/dev/null) || return 1
184	  [[ "$st" == "closed" ]]
185	}
186	
187	cmd_read() {
188	  if [[ ! -f "$file" ]]; then echo "run-checkpoint: no run state at $file" >&2; return 2; fi
189	  if ! jq -e . "$file" >/dev/null 2>&1; then echo "run-checkpoint: $file unparseable — no checkpoint; beads are the recovery truth" >&2; if (( json )); then echo '{"checkpoint":null,"reason":"unparseable"}'; fi; return 0; fi
190	  local sv cp s t p ts reason="" brc
191	  sv=$(jq -r '.schema_version // 1' "$file"); cp=$(jq -c '.checkpoint // null' "$file")
192	  [[ "$sv" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || sv=1
193	  if [[ "$cp" == "null" || "$sv" -lt 2 ]]; then
194	    if (( json )); then echo '{"checkpoint":null,"reason":"sprint granularity"}'; else echo "checkpoint: none (schema_version $sv → sprint granularity; resume at the first open bead of sprints.current)"; fi
195	    return 0
196	  fi
197	  s=$(jq -r '.checkpoint.sprint // empty' "$file"); t=$(jq -r '.checkpoint.task // empty' "$file"); p=$(jq -r '.checkpoint.phase // empty' "$file"); ts=$(jq -r '.checkpoint.ts // empty' "$file")
198	  if [[ -z "$s" || -z "$p" ]]; then reason="malformed checkpoint"
199	  elif [[ -n "$t" ]]; then
200	    # A task checkpoint is trusted only when beads CONFIRMS the task closed;
201	    # "br unavailable" is not a confirmation (Bridgebuilder PR #1269 FIND-003).
202	    brc=0; bead_closed "$t" || brc=$?
203	    case $brc in 0) ;; 2) reason="beads unavailable — task $t cannot be verified";; *) reason="task $t is not closed in beads";; esac
204	  fi
205	  if [[ -n "$reason" ]]; then
206	    echo "run-checkpoint: discarding checkpoint ($reason) — resume from the first open bead of $s" >&2
207	    if (( json )); then jq -cn --arg r "$reason" --arg s "$s" '{checkpoint:null, reason:$r, sprint:$s}'; else echo "checkpoint: discarded ($reason); resume at the first open bead of $s"; fi
208	    return 0
209	  fi
210	  if (( json )); then jq -c '{checkpoint: .checkpoint}' "$file"
211	  else echo "checkpoint: $s ${t:+task $t }phase $p at $ts → resume at the first open bead after $t in $s"; fi
212	}

214	# fb_parse FILE GATE → one compact JSON object: {file, exists, trailer, verdict,
215	# counts, exit_code, sprint_id, ts, approved, hash}. The hash is the run-mode
216	# same-issue hash (md5 of `jq -Sc '{verdict,counts}'` over verdict-derive's
217	# --json output; legacy files hash their findings section).
218	fb_parse() {
219	  local f="$1" g="$2" rel vj tl pj hash
220	  rel="${f#"$root"/}"
221	  if [[ ! -f "$f" ]]; then jq -nc --arg f "$rel" '{file: $f, exists: false}'; return 0; fi
222	  vj=$(bash "$VERDICT_DERIVE" --file "$f" --gate "$g" --json 2>/dev/null) || true
223	  jq -e 'type == "object"' >/dev/null 2>&1 <<<"$vj" || vj='{"trailer_found":false,"verdict":null,"counts":null,"exit_code":1}'

229	  else

233	    def sid: if type == "string" and test("^[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,64}$") then . else null end;
234	    def tsv: if type == "string" and test("^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}T[0-9:.]+Z$") then . else null end;
235	    {file: $f, exists: true, trailer: ($v.trailer_found == true),
236	     verdict: ($v.verdict | if type == "string" then . else null end),
237	     counts: ($v.counts // null), exit_code: ($v.exit_code // 1),
238	     sprint_id: ($p.sprint_id | sid), ts: ($p.ts | tsv), hash: $h}
239	    | .approved = (.exit_code == 0 and .verdict == "APPROVED")'

243	# SINCE touching a path outside the state/generated set, or nothing
244	impl_commit() {
245	  git -C "$root" rev-parse --git-dir >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0

248	    ':(exclude,glob)**/checksums.json' ':(exclude,glob)**/CHANGELOG.md' 2>/dev/null || true

251	# The ordered rounds of one sprint directory: every -rN file, then the current
252	# file unless it is byte-identical to the highest -rN of its gate
253	rounds_of() {
254	  local dir="$1" g base f n top topn cur
255	  for g in review audit; do
256	    if [[ "$g" == review ]]; then base=engineer-feedback; else base=auditor-sprint-feedback; fi
257	    top=""; topn=-1
258	    for f in "$dir/$base"-r*.md; do
259	      [[ -f "$f" ]] || continue
260	      n=${f##*-r}; n=${n%.md}
261	      [[ "$n" =~ ^[0-9]{1,6}$ ]] || continue
262	      fb_parse "$f" "$g" | jq -c --arg g "$g" --argjson n "$((10#$n))" '. + {gate: $g, round: $n}'
263	      if (( 10#$n > topn )); then topn=$((10#$n)); top="$f"; fi
264	    done
265	    cur="$dir/$base.md"
266	    if [[ -f "$cur" ]] && ! { [[ -n "$top" ]] && cmp -s "$cur" "$top"; }; then
267	      fb_parse "$cur" "$g" | jq -c --arg g "$g" '. + {gate: $g, round: 999999}'
268	    fi
269	  done
270	}

272	# Shared jq definitions: time, the breaker recompute and the run-state resolution
273	JQ_DEFS='
274	def epoch: if type == "string" then (sub("\\.[0-9]+Z$"; "Z") | try fromdateiso8601 catch null) else null end;
275	def fresh($now; $win): epoch as $t | $t != null and ($now - $t) <= $win and ($t - $now) <= 300;
276	def recompute($rounds; $reset):
277	  ($rounds
278	   | map(select($reset == null or ((.ts // "") > $reset)))
279	   | sort_by([(.ts // ""), .round, (if .gate == "review" then 0 else 1 end)])
280	   | map(select(.approved | not))) as $nr
281	  | reduce $nr[] as $r ({cycle: 0, same: 0, hash: null, np: 0, lc: null};
282	      .cycle += 1
283	      | (if $r.hash != "none" and $r.hash == .hash then .same += 1 else .same = 1 | .hash = $r.hash end)
284	      | ($r.counts | tojson) as $c
285	      | (if .lc != null and .lc == $c then .np += 1 else .np = 0 end)
286	      | .lc = $c);
287	def skeleton($th; $ts):
288	  {state: "CLOSED",
289	   triggers: {same_issue: {count: 0, threshold: $th.same, last_hash: null},
290	              no_progress: {count: 0, threshold: $th.np},
291	              cycle_count: {current: 0, limit: $th.cycles},
292	              timeout: {started: $ts, limit_hours: $th.hours}},
293	   history: []};
294	def merge_breaker($rc; $th; $ts):
295	  (if type == "object" then . else skeleton($th; $ts) end)
296	  | .triggers = (.triggers // {})
297	  | .triggers.cycle_count.current = ([(.triggers.cycle_count.current // 0), $rc.cycle] | max)
298	  | (if $rc.same > (.triggers.same_issue.count // 0)
299	     then .triggers.same_issue.count = $rc.same | .triggers.same_issue.last_hash = $rc.hash else . end)
300	  | (if $rc.np > (.triggers.no_progress.count // 0) or (.triggers.no_progress.last_counts == null and $rc.lc != null)
301	     then .triggers.no_progress.count = ([(.triggers.no_progress.count // 0), $rc.np] | max)
302	          | .triggers.no_progress.last_counts = $rc.lc else . end)
303	  | ( if (.triggers.same_issue.count // 0) >= (.triggers.same_issue.threshold // $th.same)
304	        then ["same_issue", "same issue hash repeated \(.triggers.same_issue.count) times (derived from the feedback history)"]
305	      elif (.triggers.no_progress.count // 0) >= (.triggers.no_progress.threshold // $th.np)
306	        then ["no_progress", "counts unchanged for \(.triggers.no_progress.count) consecutive rounds (derived from the feedback history)"]
307	      elif (.triggers.cycle_count.current // 0) >= (.triggers.cycle_count.limit // $th.cycles)
308	        then ["cycle_count", "\(.triggers.cycle_count.current) changes-required rounds (derived from the feedback history)"]
309	      else null end ) as $trip
310	  | if $trip != null and (.state // "CLOSED") != "OPEN"
311	    then .state = "OPEN" | .history = ((.history // []) + [{timestamp: $ts, trigger: $trip[0], reason: $trip[1], source: "derive"}])
312	    else .state = (.state // "CLOSED") end;
313	def known_ids: (.derivation.sprint_ids // null) // ((.sprints.list // []) | map(.id? // empty));
314	def resolve($f; $now; $win):
315	  . as $c
316	  | (if ($c | type) == "object" then $c else {} end) as $c
317	  | ($c.state // $c.status // "") as $cs
318	  | ($c | known_ids) as $known
319	  | ([$f.sprints[] | select(.state != "complete")
320	      | "sprint-\(.global_id)" as $g | .local_label as $l
321	      | select(($known | index($g)) == null and ($l == "" or ($known | index($l)) == null))] | length > 0) as $new
322	  | ((($c.completion // {}) | .merged_sha? // "") | type == "string" and length > 0) as $merged
323	  | if ($c.state // "") == "JACKED_OUT" or ($c.status // "") == "JACKED_OUT" or $merged then "JACKED_OUT"
324	    elif $f.breaker_open or $cs == "HALTED" then "HALTED"
325	    elif $f.all_complete then "COMPLETE"
326	    elif $cs == "COMPLETE" and ($new | not) then "COMPLETE"
327	    elif ($c.timestamps.last_activity? // null) | fresh($now; $win) then "RUNNING"
328	    else "INTERRUPTED" end;
329	'

331	cmd_derive() {
332	  local ledger="$root/grimoires/loa/ledger.json" a2a="$root/grimoires/loa/a2a" active rows
333	  if [[ ! -f "$ledger" ]] || ! jq -e 'type == "object"' "$ledger" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
334	    echo "run-checkpoint: derive: no readable ledger at $ledger — callers keep the cache" >&2; return 4
335	  fi
336	  active=$(jq -r '.active_cycle // empty | strings' "$ledger")
337	  if [[ -z "$active" ]] || ! jq -e --arg c "$active" 'any(.cycles[]?; .id == $c)' "$ledger" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
338	    echo "run-checkpoint: derive: the ledger has no active cycle — callers keep the cache" >&2; return 4
339	  fi
340	  local win now now_ts fa=1 th
341	  win=$(( $(cfg_int '.run_mode.stale_hours' 12 8760) * 3600 ))
342	  [[ "$(cfg '.run_mode.file_authoritative')" == false ]] && fa=0
343	  th=$(jq -nc --argjson s "$(cfg_int '.run_mode.circuit_breaker.same_issue_threshold' 3 1000)" \
344	              --argjson n "$(cfg_int '.run_mode.circuit_breaker.no_progress_threshold' 5 1000)" \
345	              --argjson c "$(cfg_int '.run_mode.defaults.max_cycles' 20 10000)" \
346	              --argjson h "$(cfg_int '.run_mode.defaults.timeout_hours' 8 8760)" \
347	              '{same: $s, np: $n, cycles: $c, hours: $h}')
348	  now=$(date +%s); now_ts=$(now_iso)
349	
350	  # Per-sprint facts
351	  local sprints="[]" gid label lstatus since dir rv au mex msid ic sj
352	  rows=$(jq -r --arg c "$active" '
353	    (.cycles[] | select(.id == $c)) as $cy
354	    | ($cy.sprints // [])[]
355	    | select((.global_id | type) == "number")
356	    | [(.global_id | tostring), ((.local_label // "") | tostring), ((.status // "") | tostring),
357	       ([.started, .created, $cy.created] | map(select(type == "string" and test("^[0-9]{4}-")))
358	        | if length == 0 then "" else ([.[0], ($cy.created // "")] | max) end)]
359	    | map(if . == "" then "-" else . end)
360	    | @tsv' "$ledger")
361	  # "-" stands for an empty field: IFS whitespace (tab) would collapse two adjacent separators
362	  while IFS=$'\t' read -r gid label lstatus since; do
363	    [[ "$gid" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || continue
364	    [[ "$label" == - ]] && label=""
365	    [[ "$since" == - ]] && since=""
366	    [[ "$label" =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,64}$ ]] || label=""
367	    [[ "$lstatus" =~ ^[a-z_]{1,32}$ ]] || lstatus="unknown"
368	    [[ "$since" =~ ^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}T[0-9:.]+Z$ ]] || since=""
369	    dir="$a2a/sprint-$gid"
370	    rv=$(fb_parse "$dir/engineer-feedback.md" review)
371	    au=$(fb_parse "$dir/auditor-sprint-feedback.md" audit)
372	    mex=false; msid=""
373	    if [[ -f "$dir/COMPLETED" ]]; then
374	      mex=true
375	      msid=$(sed -n 's/^sprint:[[:space:]]*\([A-Za-z0-9._-]*\).*/\1/p' "$dir/COMPLETED" | head -n 1) || msid=""
376	    fi
377	    ic=$(impl_commit "$since")
378	    sj=$(jq -nc --argjson gid "$gid" --arg label "$label" --arg status "$lstatus" --argjson rv "$rv" --argjson au "$au" \
379	              --argjson mex "$mex" --arg msid "$msid" --arg ic "$ic" '
380	      def mine: type == "string" and length > 0 and (. == "sprint-\($gid)" or ($label != "" and . == $label));
381	      ($rv.approved == true and ($rv.sprint_id | mine)) as $R
382	      | ($au.approved == true and ($au.sprint_id | mine)) as $A
383	      | ([$rv.sprint_id, $au.sprint_id, (if $msid == "" then null else $msid end)] | map(select(type == "string" and length > 0))) as $ids
384	      | ($mex and any($ids[]; mine | not)) as $stale
385	      | ($mex and ($stale | not) and (($rv.sprint_id | mine) or ($au.sprint_id | mine))) as $M
386	      | ($ic | split(" ")) as $c
387	      | ([$rv.ts, $au.ts] | map(select(. != null)) | max) as $vts
388	      | def verdict($x): if $x.exists then {verdict: $x.verdict, sprint_id: $x.sprint_id, consistent: ($x.exit_code == 0), file: $x.file} else null end;
389	      {global_id: $gid, local_label: $label, status: $status,
390	       completed_marker: $M, marker_present: $mex, stale_marker: $stale,
391	       review: verdict($rv), audit: verdict($au),
392	       impl_commit: (if ($c | length) == 2 then $c[0] else null end),
393	       commit_after_verdict: (if ($c | length) == 2 and $vts != null
394	                              then (($c[1] | tonumber) > ($vts | sub("\\.[0-9]+Z$"; "Z") | try fromdateiso8601 catch 0)) else null end),
395	       legacy_feedback: ([$rv, $au] | map(select(.exists and (.trailer | not)) | .file)),
396	       state: (if $M and $R and $A and $status == "completed" then "complete"
397	               elif ($M | not) and $R and $A then "awaiting_marker" else "in_progress" end)}')
398	    sprints=$(jq -c --argjson s "$sj" '. + [$s]' <<<"$sprints")
399	  done <<<"$rows"
400	
401	  # Breaker recompute over the active sprint's ordered rounds
402	  local active_gid rounds cache="null" cache_ok=1 bcache="null" reset rc merged
403	  active_gid=$(jq -r 'if length == 0 then "" else ((map(select(.state != "complete")) | .[0]) // .[-1]) | .global_id | tostring end' <<<"$sprints")
404	  rounds="[]"
405	  if [[ -n "$active_gid" && -d "$a2a/sprint-$active_gid" ]]; then
406	    rounds=$(rounds_of "$a2a/sprint-$active_gid" | jq -sc '.')
407	  fi
408	  if [[ -f "$file" ]]; then
409	    if cache=$(jq -c . "$file" 2>/dev/null) && [[ -n "$cache" ]]; then :; else cache="null"; cache_ok=0; fi

411	  if [[ -f "$breaker" ]]; then bcache=$(jq -c 'if type == "object" then . else null end' "$breaker" 2>/dev/null) || bcache="null"; [[ -n "$bcache" ]] || bcache="null"; fi
412	  reset=$(jq -c '.reset_at? // null | if type == "string" then . else null end' <<<"$bcache")
413	  rc=$(jq -nc --argjson r "$rounds" --argjson z "$reset" "$JQ_DEFS"' recompute($r; $z)')
414	  merged=$(jq -c --argjson rc "$rc" --argjson th "$th" --arg ts "$now_ts" "$JQ_DEFS"' merge_breaker($rc; $th; $ts)' <<<"$bcache")
415	
416	  local facts report
417	  facts=$(jq -nc --argjson s "$sprints" --argjson b "$merged" '
418	    {sprints: $s,
419	     all_complete: (($s | length) > 0 and all($s[]; .state == "complete")),
420	     breaker_open: ($b.state == "OPEN"),
421	     stale_markers: [$s[] | select(.stale_marker) | "sprint-\(.global_id)"],
422	     legacy_feedback: [$s[] | .legacy_feedback[]],
423	     sprint_ids: [$s[] | "sprint-\(.global_id)"]}')
424	  report=$(jq -nc --argjson f "$facts" --argjson c "$cache" --argjson b "$merged" --argjson rc "$rc" \
425	                  --argjson now "$now" --argjson win "$win" --arg ts "$now_ts" --arg cycle "$active" \
426	                  --argjson fa "$fa" --argjson cache_ok "$cache_ok" --arg ag "$active_gid" "$JQ_DEFS"'
427	    def st: if type == "string" then (if test("^[A-Z_]{1,32}$") then . else "INVALID" end) else null end;
428	    ($c | resolve($f; $now; $win)) as $s
429	    | ($c | if type == "object" then (.state | st) else null end) as $cs
430	    | ($c | if type == "object" then (.status | st) else null end) as $cst
431	    | {cycle: $cycle, derived_at: $ts, stale_hours: ($win / 3600), file_authoritative: ($fa == 1),
432	       state: $s, cache_state: $cs, cache_status: $cst,
433	       cache: (if $cache_ok == 0 then "unparseable" elif $c == null then "missing" else "present" end),
434	       drift: ($c != null and ($cs != $s or ($cst != null and $cst != $s))),
435	       notes: ([
436	         (if $cs != null and $cst != null and $cs != $cst then "cache .state \($cs) and .status \($cst) disagree" else empty end),
437	         (if $s == "JACKED_OUT" and ($f.all_complete | not) then "JACKED_OUT is terminal: files show incomplete sprints; the cache is kept" else empty end),
438	         (if $s == "COMPLETE" and ($f.all_complete | not) then "COMPLETE kept: no new incomplete sprint in the ledger" else empty end),
439	         ($f.sprints[] | select(.stale_marker) | "sprint-\(.global_id): COMPLETED marker names another sprint (stale_marker, not counted)"),
440	         ($f.sprints[] | select(.state == "awaiting_marker") | "sprint-\(.global_id): review and audit APPROVED, no COMPLETED marker")
441	       ]),
442	       sprints: $f.sprints,
443	       active_sprint: (if $ag == "" then null else "sprint-\($ag)" end),
444	       breaker: {state: $b.state, cycle_count: $b.triggers.cycle_count.current, same_issue: $b.triggers.same_issue.count,
445	                 no_progress: $b.triggers.no_progress.count, recomputed: {cycle_count: $rc.cycle, same_issue: $rc.same, no_progress: $rc.np}},
446	       derivation: {source: "files", stale_markers: $f.stale_markers, legacy_feedback: $f.legacy_feedback},
447	       written: false}')
448	
449	  if (( write )); then
450	    local why=""
451	    if (( fa == 0 )); then why="run_mode.file_authoritative: false — report-only"
452	    elif [[ ! -f "$file" ]]; then why="no run state at $file — nothing to rewrite"
453	    elif (( cache_ok == 0 )); then why="$file unparseable — kept for inspection, not rewritten"
454	    fi
455	    if [[ -z "$why" ]]; then
456	      atomic_update "$breaker" --argjson rc "$rc" --argjson th "$th" --arg ts "$now_ts" "$JQ_DEFS"' merge_breaker($rc; $th; $ts)' || return 3
457	      merged=$(jq -c . "$breaker")
458	      facts=$(jq -c --argjson b "$merged" '.breaker_open = ($b.state == "OPEN")' <<<"$facts")
459	      atomic_update "$file" --argjson f "$facts" --argjson now "$now" --argjson win "$win" --arg ts "$now_ts" "$JQ_DEFS"'
460	        resolve($f; $now; $win) as $s
461	        | .state = $s | .status = $s | .derived_at = $ts
462	        | .derivation = {source: "files", stale_markers: $f.stale_markers, legacy_feedback: $f.legacy_feedback, sprint_ids: $f.sprint_ids}
463	        | .schema_version = (.schema_version // 2)' || return 3
464	      report=$(jq -c --slurpfile c "$file" --argjson b "$merged" '.written = true | .state = $c[0].state | .breaker.state = $b.state' <<<"$report")
465	    else
466	      report=$(jq -c --arg w "$why" '.notes += [$w]' <<<"$report")
467	    fi
468	  fi
469	
470	  if (( json )); then
471	    jq . <<<"$report"
472	  else
473	    jq -r '"derive: files say \(.state), cache said \(.cache_state // "nothing") (\(if .drift then "drift" else "in sync" end))"
474	           + (if .written then " — caches rewritten" else "" end), (.notes[] | "  note: " + .)' <<<"$report"
475	  fi
476	  return 0
477	}

479	cmd_record_round() {
480	  [[ -n "$gate" && -n "$file" ]] || usage
481	  if [[ ! -f "$file" ]]; then echo "run-checkpoint: record-round: no feedback file at $file" >&2; return 2; fi
482	  local p th ts now out trip
483	  p=$(fb_parse "$file" "$gate")
484	  if [[ "$(jq -r '.approved' <<<"$p")" == true ]]; then
485	    echo "recorded: $gate APPROVED — breaker counters unchanged"
486	    return 0
487	  fi
488	  th=$(jq -nc --argjson s "$(cfg_int '.run_mode.circuit_breaker.same_issue_threshold' 3 1000)" \
489	              --argjson n "$(cfg_int '.run_mode.circuit_breaker.no_progress_threshold' 5 1000)" \
490	              --argjson c "$(cfg_int '.run_mode.defaults.max_cycles' 20 10000)" \
491	              --argjson h "$(cfg_int '.run_mode.defaults.timeout_hours' 8 8760)" \
492	              '{same: $s, np: $n, cycles: $c, hours: $h}')
493	  ts=$(now_iso); now=$(date +%s)
494	  atomic_update "$breaker" --argjson p "$p" --argjson th "$th" --arg ts "$ts" --argjson now "$now" \
495	      --arg gate "$gate" --arg sprint "$sprint" "$JQ_DEFS"'
496	    (if type == "object" and (.triggers | type) == "object" then . else skeleton($th; $ts) end)
497	    | ($p.counts | tojson) as $c
498	    | (if $p.hash != "none" and $p.hash == (.triggers.same_issue.last_hash // null)
499	       then .triggers.same_issue.count = ((.triggers.same_issue.count // 0) + 1)
500	       else .triggers.same_issue.count = 1 | .triggers.same_issue.last_hash = $p.hash end)
501	    | (if (.triggers.no_progress.last_counts // null) != null and .triggers.no_progress.last_counts == $c
502	       then .triggers.no_progress.count = ((.triggers.no_progress.count // 0) + 1)
503	       else .triggers.no_progress.count = 0 end)
504	    | .triggers.no_progress.last_counts = $c
505	    | .triggers.cycle_count.current = ((.triggers.cycle_count.current // 0) + 1)
506	    | (.triggers.timeout.started // null | epoch) as $start
507	    | ( if .triggers.same_issue.count >= (.triggers.same_issue.threshold // $th.same)
508	          then ["same_issue", "same issue hash \($p.hash[0:8]) seen \(.triggers.same_issue.count) times in a row"]
509	        elif .triggers.no_progress.count >= (.triggers.no_progress.threshold // $th.np)
510	          then ["no_progress", "finding counts unchanged for \(.triggers.no_progress.count) consecutive rounds"]
511	        elif .triggers.cycle_count.current >= (.triggers.cycle_count.limit // $th.cycles)
512	          then ["cycle_count", "\(.triggers.cycle_count.current) changes-required rounds reached the limit \(.triggers.cycle_count.limit // $th.cycles)"]
513	        elif $start != null and ($now - $start) >= ((.triggers.timeout.limit_hours // $th.hours) * 3600)
514	          then ["timeout", "run older than \(.triggers.timeout.limit_hours // $th.hours) hours"]
515	        elif (.state // "CLOSED") == "OPEN" then ["open", "breaker already OPEN"]
516	        else null end ) as $trip
517	    | .last_round = {gate: $gate, sprint: (if $sprint == "" then null else $sprint end), verdict: $p.verdict, hash: $p.hash, ts: $ts}
518	    | if $trip != null and $trip[0] != "open" and (.state // "CLOSED") != "OPEN"
519	      then .state = "OPEN" | .history = ((.history // []) + [{timestamp: $ts, trigger: $trip[0], reason: $trip[1], gate: $gate, sprint: (if $sprint == "" then null else $sprint end)}])
520	      elif $trip != null then .state = "OPEN"
521	      else .state = (.state // "CLOSED") end
522	    | .last_trip = $trip' || return 3
523	  trip=$(jq -r '.last_trip // empty | if type == "array" then "\(.[0]): \(.[1])" else empty end' "$breaker")
524	  out=$(jq -r '"recorded: \(.last_round.gate) \(.last_round.verdict // "no verdict") — cycle \(.triggers.cycle_count.current)/\(.triggers.cycle_count.limit), same_issue \(.triggers.same_issue.count)/\(.triggers.same_issue.threshold), no_progress \(.triggers.no_progress.count)/\(.triggers.no_progress.threshold)"' "$breaker")
525	  echo "$out"
526	  if [[ -n "$trip" ]]; then
527	    atomic_update "$state_file" --arg ts "$ts" '.state = "HALTED"' || return 3
528	    echo "TRIPPED: $trip"
529	    return 10
530	  fi
531	  return 0
532	}

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# run-corpus.sh — replay tests/fixtures/fence-corpus/corpus.jsonl through the
     3	# block-destructive-bash hook and summarise (cycle-125 Sprint 1, PRD FR-1).
     4	#
     5	# Usage: run-corpus.sh [--hook PATH] [--corpus PATH] [--json] [--knob-off] [--rows]
     6	# Each row: {id, cmd, expect: allow|block|residual, rule, why, cwd: repo|tmp, env?: {TMPDIR}}
     7	#   allow    → benign: the hook must exit 0

     9	#   residual → accepted false positive: counted, never gated
    10	# --knob-off  writes destructive_command_guard.heredoc_classifier: false into the
    11	#             replay root's .loa.config.yaml (cycle-129 FR-6: the pre-cycle scan);

    16	# --json prints {benign_pass, benign_total, dangerous_block, dangerous_total,
    17	#   residual_pass, residual_total, runtime_ms, p95_ms, rows, mismatches: [..]}.
    18	# p95_ms is the 95th percentile of the per-row hook wall time (the hook process
    19	# only; the jq row parsing is outside the timed span).
    20	set -uo pipefail
    21	export LC_ALL=C
    22	root="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../../.." && pwd)"
    23	hook="$root/.claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh"
    24	corpus="$root/tests/fixtures/fence-corpus/corpus.jsonl"
    25	json=0 knob_off=0 rows_out=0

    27	  case "$1" in
    28	    --hook) hook="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    29	    --corpus) corpus="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    30	    --json) json=1; shift ;;
    31	    --knob-off) knob_off=1; shift ;;
    32	    --rows) rows_out=1; shift ;;
    33	    *) echo "usage: run-corpus.sh [--hook PATH] [--corpus PATH] [--json] [--knob-off] [--rows]" >&2; exit 2 ;;
    34	  esac
    35	done
    36	[[ -x "$hook" || -f "$hook" ]] || { echo "hook not found: $hook" >&2; exit 2; }
    37	[[ -f "$corpus" ]] || { echo "corpus not found: $corpus" >&2; exit 2; }

    39	work="$(mktemp -d)"
    40	trap 'rm -rf -- "$work"' EXIT

    42	mkdir -p "$repo" "$scratch"
    43	export LOA_REPO_ROOT="$work"
    44	export LOA_AUDIT_REPLAY=1   # audit rows this replay writes carry replay: true (cycle-129 DEC-0167)
    45	if (( knob_off )); then
    46	  printf 'destructive_command_guard:\n  heredoc_classifier: false\n' > "$work/.loa.config.yaml"
    47	fi
    48	
    49	bp=0 bt=0 db=0 dt=0 rp=0 rt=0
    50	mismatches=()
    51	durations=()
    52	# Microsecond clock: $EPOCHREALTIME (bash ≥ 5) everywhere; GNU date fallback.
    53	now_us() {
    54	  if [[ -n "${EPOCHREALTIME:-}" ]]; then
    55	    local s="${EPOCHREALTIME%.*}" us="${EPOCHREALTIME#*.}"
    56	    echo $(( s * 1000000 + 10#${us:0:6} ))
    57	  else
    58	    echo $(( $(date +%s%N) / 1000 ))
    59	  fi
    60	}

    63	  [[ -n "$row" ]] || continue
    64	  id=$(jq -r '.id' <<<"$row"); cmd=$(jq -r '.cmd' <<<"$row"); expect=$(jq -r '.expect' <<<"$row")
    65	  cwd=$(jq -r '.cwd // "repo"' <<<"$row"); tmpdir=$(jq -r '.env.TMPDIR // empty' <<<"$row")
    66	  dir="$repo"; [[ "$cwd" == "tmp" ]] && dir="$scratch"
    67	  payload=$(jq -cn --arg c "$cmd" '{tool_input: {command: $c}}')
    68	  rc=0
    69	  t0=$(now_us)

    71	    (cd "$dir" && TMPDIR="$tmpdir" bash "$hook" <<<"$payload" >/dev/null 2>&1) || rc=$?
    72	  else
    73	    (cd "$dir" && env -u TMPDIR bash "$hook" <<<"$payload" >/dev/null 2>&1) || rc=$?
    74	  fi

    80	    block)    dt=$((dt+1)); if [[ $rc -eq 2 ]]; then db=$((db+1)); else mismatches+=("$id:expected-block:rc=$rc"); fi ;;

    82	    *) mismatches+=("$id:unknown-expect:$expect") ;;
    83	  esac
    84	done < "$corpus"

    87	n=${#durations[@]}

    90	  idx=$(( (n * 95 + 99) / 100 ))      # nearest-rank: ceil(0.95 n)
    91	  p95=$(printf '%s\n' "${durations[@]}" | sort -n | sed -n "${idx}p")
    92	fi
    93	
    94	(( rows_out )) && exit 0

    96	  printf '%s\n' "${mismatches[@]+"${mismatches[@]}"}" | jq -R . | jq -s \
    97	    --argjson bp "$bp" --argjson bt "$bt" --argjson db "$db" --argjson dt "$dt" \
    98	    --argjson rp "$rp" --argjson rt "$rt" --argjson ms "$runtime" --argjson p95 "$p95" --argjson n "$n" \
    99	    '{benign_pass:$bp, benign_total:$bt, dangerous_block:$db, dangerous_total:$dt, residual_pass:$rp, residual_total:$rt, runtime_ms:$ms, p95_ms:$p95, rows:$n, mismatches: map(select(length>0))}'
   100	else
   101	  printf '%s\n' "${mismatches[@]+"${mismatches[@]}"}" | sed '/^$/d'
   102	  echo "benign $bp/$bt dangerous $db/$dt residual $rp/$rt runtime_ms $runtime p95_ms $p95"
   103	fi

#   override          — LOA_IMPLEMENT_GATE_OVERRIDE=1 in the hook's environment
# Rows go to .run/audit.jsonl as {ts, hook: "implement-gate", action, decision,
# mode, path} with path control-stripped and cut to 256 bytes; LOA_AUDIT_REPLAY=1
# adds replay: true to every row this gate writes (DEC-0167).
#
# Claims modifier (implement_gate.claims: authoritative; the legacy
# implement_gate.mode: authoritative means mode ask + claims authoritative):
#   reads tool_input.active_skill from hook stdin. The PreToolUse
#      payload carries no harness-set skill field (cycle-126 D-4.4) and tool_input
#      is model-authored, so nothing in .run/ selects this modifier.
#      TIGHTEN-ONLY (sprint-250 audit n17/n18): the model-authored claim can only
#      add an ask, never grant an allow. A claimed implementation skill falls
#      through to the heuristic exactly like an absent field; a claimed
#      non-implementation skill asks (or, under deny with a known position and no
#      sanction, is denied) and logs compliance.mode.model_signal to
#      .run/audit.jsonl (plain hook log, not the signed audit_emit chain). Every
#      claim leaves one row per invocation: decision "ask"/"deny" for a non-implementation
#      claim, decision "heuristic" for an implementation claim (run-2 finding 6).
#
# `implement-gate.sh --effective-mode [CONFIG]` prints the effective mode (and the
# claims modifier) without reading stdin — the /loa Gate line.
#
# Evidence recorder (cycle-126 D-4.4): a lead-session payload carrying
# tool_input.active_skill records active_skill_seen_at once in
# .run/platform-features.json. It is evidence only and never changes the mode.
#
# Failure mode: FAIL-ASK for App Zone writes (not fail-open). A payload jq cannot
# parse (or no jq), or a file_path that cannot be canonicalised, asks too (run-2
# findings 1/5). The path is tool_input.file_path, or tool_input.notebook_path for
# NotebookEdit; a relative path resolves from the payload's cwd, else PROJECT_ROOT
# (run-3 finding 6). The zone test ORs a physical form (symlinks followed) and a
# logical form (symlinks kept) and matches a lowercased copy (run-3 findings 1/2).
# Root: PROJECT_ROOT, else CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR, else this script's location
# (<root>/.claude/hooks/compliance/), never the process cwd, which follows
# Claude's `cd` (audit MED-001); RUN_DIR defaults to <root>/.run.
# Trust inputs: a write to .run/state.json, .run/sprint-plan-state.json,
# .run/simstim-state.json, .run/platform-features.json, .run/audit.jsonl,
# .run/implement-active.json or .loa.config.yaml asks in every mode and under
# every sanction, and logs compliance.state_write (run-3 finding 3).
# Other non-App-Zone writes always allowed.
#
# Output (Claude Code PreToolUse contract, sprint-250 audit n20): allow = silent
# exit 0 with empty stdout; ask = exit 0 with
#   {"hookSpecificOutput":{"hookEventName":"PreToolUse","permissionDecision":"ask","permissionDecisionReason":"…"}}
# deny = the same shape with "permissionDecision":"deny".
# A top-level "decision" accepts approve|block only, so "ask" never goes there.
# file_path and active_skill reach stderr only through strip_controls (n21;
# run-2 findings 3/12; run-3 finding 5): cut to 256 bytes without splitting a
# character, then C0 and DEL, UTF-8 C1 controls and the Unicode format/bidi/tag
# code points are removed to a fixed point. Audit rows record the RAW values cut
# the same way and written with jq -a, so every non-ASCII code point is \uXXXX:
# faithful (implement+U+200B logs as implement\u200b) and terminal-safe (run-3 finding 4).
#
# IMPORTANT: No set -euo pipefail — hook must never crash-block.
# Parse/read errors on App Zone writes → ask (not allow).
#
# Part of cycle-049/050: Upstream Platform Alignment (FR-7)
# Red Team findings addressed: ATK-005 (state tampering), ATK-006 (fail-open),
#   ATK-007 (prompt injection via file path)
# Sprint-108 T4.4: Dual-mode (authoritative + heuristic)
# Sprint-108 T4.5: Path normalization
# =============================================================================

# Read tool input from stdin (not for --effective-mode, which reads no payload)
input=""
if [[ "${1:-}" != "--effective-mode" ]]; then
    input=$(cat 2>/dev/null) || input=""
fi

# The ask reply; jq builds it so any reason is a well-formed JSON string (run-3 finding 7); the printf literal is only
# for the jq-missing branch, whose reason is a fixed string
emit_ask() {
    if command -v jq &>/dev/null; then
        jq -nc --arg r "$1" '{hookSpecificOutput:{hookEventName:"PreToolUse",permissionDecision:"ask",permissionDecisionReason:$r}}'
    else
        printf '{"hookSpecificOutput":{"hookEventName":"PreToolUse","permissionDecision":"ask","permissionDecisionReason":"%s"}}\n' "$1"
    fi
}

# Byte sequences strip_controls removes: UTF-8 C1 controls (C2 80..C2 9F) and the format/bidi code points
# U+200B-U+200F, U+2028-U+202E, U+2060-U+2064, U+2066-U+206F, U+FEFF, U+00AD, U+061C, U+180E, U+FE00-U+FE0F,
# U+FFF9-U+FFFB and the tag characters U+E0001, U+E0020-U+E007F (run-3 finding 5); each sequence starts with a lead
# byte, so a byte-wise match never lands inside another character
# printf -v keeps this portable (no GNU-sed \x); built on first use, not on every Write/Edit (BB-008)
_IG_STRIP_SEQS=()
_ig_strip_seqs_init() {
    local _ig_i _ig_hex _ig_seq
    for (( _ig_i = 128; _ig_i < 160; _ig_i++ )); do
        printf -v _ig_hex '%02x' "$_ig_i"; printf -v _ig_seq "\\xc2\\x${_ig_hex}"; _IG_STRIP_SEQS+=("$_ig_seq")
    done
    for _ig_hex in 8b 8c 8d 8e 8f a8 a9 aa ab ac ad ae; do
        printf -v _ig_seq "\\xe2\\x80\\x${_ig_hex}"; _IG_STRIP_SEQS+=("$_ig_seq")
    done
    for _ig_hex in a0 a1 a2 a3 a4 a6 a7 a8 a9 aa ab ac ad ae af; do

259	# T4.5: Path normalization — canonicalise both sides, then take file_path
260	# relative to the project root (run-2 finding 1). A textual prefix test let
261	# /proc/self/cwd/src/x, //ROOT/src/x, ROOT/../<name>/src/x or a symlinked root
262	# reach an App-Zone file unseen. Two forms are tested and either one matching
263	# counts (run-3 finding 1): the PHYSICAL form follows symlinks (realpath -m,
264	# else readlink -f) against pwd -P of the root; the LOGICAL form keeps them
265	# (realpath -m -s, else a pure-bash ./../// normaliser) against pwd -L, so a
266	# src/ that is itself a symlink out of the root still asks. A relative path
267	# resolves from the payload's cwd when it carries one (the harness resolves it
268	# there and cwd follows `cd` in the Bash tool), else from PROJECT_ROOT (run-3
269	# finding 6). Only the part under the root is matched, so parent directory
270	# names never count (e.g., /home/user/src-projects/loa/grimoires/file.md is not src/*).
271	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
272	# Lexical normaliser for an absolute path: drops empty and . components, resolves .. textually, follows no symlink
273	_ig_lexical_norm() {
274	    local rest=$1 part
275	    local -a out=()
276	    while [[ -n "$rest" ]]; do
277	        part=${rest%%/*}
278	        if [[ "$rest" == */* ]]; then rest=${rest#*/}; else rest=""; fi
279	        case "$part" in
280	            ''|.) ;;
281	            ..) (( ${#out[@]} )) && unset 'out[${#out[@]}-1]' ;;
282	            *) out+=("$part") ;;
283	        esac
284	    done
285	    local IFS=/
286	    printf '/%s' "${out[*]}"
287	}

289	# $1 relative to the root $2, or failure when $1 is not under $2
290	_ig_under_root() {
291	    [[ "$1" == "${2%/}/"* ]] || return 1
292	    printf '%s' "${1#"${2%/}"/}"
293	}

296	logical_root=$(cd "$PROJECT_ROOT" 2>/dev/null && pwd -L) || logical_root=""
297	payload_cwd=$(jq -r '.cwd // empty | strings' <<<"$input" 2>/dev/null) || payload_cwd=""

     2	# generate-constraints.sh — DRY Constraint Registry generator

     6	SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"

    10

    18	readonly -a SECTIONS=(

    53	# ============================================================================

    57	log() { echo "[generate-constraints] $*" >&2; }

    61	compute_section_hash() {
    62	  # SHA-256, first 16 chars, LF-normalized, trailing whitespace trimmed

    64	    | tr -d '\r' \
    65	    | sed 's/[[:space:]]*$//' \

    70	# ============================================================================
    71	# Registry validation

    73	
    74	validate_registry() {

    77	  fi
    78	
    79	  if ! jq empty "$REGISTRY" 2>/dev/null; then

    82	
    83	  # Check for duplicate IDs

    93	# ============================================================================
    94	# Rendering

    96	
    97	render_section() {

    99	  local template="$2"
   100	  local filter_jq="$3"

   102	  local template_file="${TEMPLATE_DIR}/${template}"

   114	insert_generated_section() {

   116	  local section="$2"
   117	  local content="$3"

   119	  local hash

   122	  local start_marker="<!-- @constraint-generated: start ${section} | hash:${hash} -->"
   123	  local end_marker="<!-- @constraint-generated: end ${section} -->"
   124	  local warning="<!-- DO NOT EDIT — generated from .claude/data/constraints.json -->"

   132	        -v new_warning="$warning" \
   133	        -v new_content="$content" \
   134	        -v new_end="$end_marker" \

   137	        $0 ~ end   { print new_end; skip=0; next }
   138	        !skip       { print }

   147	# Prints the heading of an optional table section; returns 1 when the section

   149	optional_table_heading() {

   161	# Removes an optional table block from FILE: the exact heading line, the
   162	# table-header lines between it and the start marker, the marker block, and
   163	# one blank line after the end marker. A file without the start marker is
   164	# already pruned (no-op). Anything else between the heading and the start
   165	# marker, a missing heading or a missing end marker is an error and leaves
   166	# FILE untouched.
   167	prune_optional_table() {
   168	  local file="$1" section="$2" heading="$3"

   170	    verbose "Optional section ${section} already absent from ${file}"

   175	      -v start="@constraint-generated: start ${section} " \
   176	      -v end="@constraint-generated: end ${section} " '
   177	    function flush(   i) { for (i = 1; i <= n; i++) print buf[i]; n = 0 }

   214	  "task_tracking_hierarchy|^### Task Tracking Hierarchy$|^$|^---$"

   221	bootstrap_section() {

   237	
   238	  # Find anchor for this section
   239	  local anchor_start="" anchor_end=""

   242	    IFS='|' read -r a_section a_start a_end <<< "$anchor"

   275	      -v end_pat2="$end_pat2" \

   277	      -v warning_m="$warning" \
   278	      -v end_m="$end_marker" \
   279	      -v content_m="$content" \

   284	      }

   297	      state == "skipping" {

   303	        }

   305	        next

   326	generate_all_sections() {

#       Run state, first match wins:
#         cache .state or .status JACKED_OUT, or .completion.merged_sha → JACKED_OUT (terminal)
#         breaker OPEN, or cache HALTED                                 → HALTED (sticky until /run-resume)
#         every sprint complete                                         → COMPLETE
#         cache COMPLETE and the ledger registers no new incomplete sprint → COMPLETE
#         last_activity within run_mode.stale_hours (12)                → RUNNING
#         otherwise                                                     → INTERRUPTED
#       Breaker (active sprint = first incomplete, else the last): the ordered
#       rounds engineer-feedback-r*.md, auditor-sprint-feedback-r*.md and the
#       current files (sorted by trailer ts, round, gate; rounds before the
#       breaker's reset_at are ignored) give cycle_count (non-APPROVED rounds),
#       same_issue (consecutive equal hashes) and no_progress (consecutive
#       equal counts); each cached counter is raised to its recomputed value,
#       never lowered; OPEN when a count threshold is met (timeout is left to
#       record-round). --json prints the derivation; --write rewrites F
#       (.state canonical, .status mirrored, derived_at, derivation {source,
#       stale_markers, legacy_feedback, sprint_ids}; schema_version kept) and
#       the breaker, under their locks — only when F exists, parses, and
#       run_mode.file_authoritative is not false (false = report-only).
#       Exit 0 · 4 no ledger / no active cycle · 2 usage.
#   run-checkpoint.sh record-round --gate review|audit --file FEEDBACK [--sprint sprint-N]
#                                  [--state-file F] [--breaker B]
#       After a review or audit: verdict-derive.sh --json on FEEDBACK; the
#       same-issue hash is md5 of `jq -Sc '{verdict,counts}'` of that output
#       (no trailer: md5 of the first 50 lines from ## Findings / ## Issues /
#       ## Changes Required). APPROVED (exit 0) leaves every counter as is.
#       Otherwise, atomically on B: same_issue +1 when the hash equals
#       last_hash, else count 1 and last_hash = hash; no_progress +1 when the
#       counts equal the previous round's, else 0; cycle_count.current +1; then
#       the triggers in order same_issue ≥ threshold, no_progress ≥ threshold,
#       cycle_count ≥ limit, timeout (now - started ≥ limit_hours). A trip sets
#       state OPEN, appends history {timestamp, trigger, reason, gate, sprint},
#       sets F (.run/state.json) .state = HALTED, prints
#       `TRIPPED: <trigger>: <reason>` and exits 10 (also when B is already OPEN).
#       Exit 0 recorded · 2 usage / missing file · 3 write failed · 10 tripped.
#   run-checkpoint.sh mark --skill implement|bug --sprint ID [--root DIR]
#       Writes .run/implement-active.json {skill, sprint, started_at} (the
#       implement gate's marker sanction, valid two hours), then runs
#       `derive --write` when F exists. `unmark` removes the marker. Exit 0 · 2 usage.
#
# Default F: $LOA_RUN_DIR/sprint-plan-state.json, else <root>/.run/sprint-plan-state.json
# (--root DIR sets <root> and ignores LOA_RUN_DIR). B: <run dir>/circuit-breaker.json.
# Readers accept schema_version 1 and 2 and files without derived_at/derivation.
# Config (<root>/.loa.config.yaml, yq; absent = defaults): run_mode.stale_hours (12),
# run_mode.file_authoritative (true), run_mode.circuit_breaker.{same_issue,no_progress}_threshold
