rr() { run --separate-stderr bash "$CK" record-round --root "$T" --breaker "$B" --state-file "$S" --sprint sprint-1 "$@"; }

@test "RCR-1 a CHANGES_REQUIRED review increments cycle_count.current, sets same_issue {count 1, last_hash} to the SKILL's derived hash, exit 0" {
  breaker
  fb engineer-feedback.md review CHANGES_REQUIRED 1
  rr --gate review --file "$T/a2a/engineer-feedback.md"
  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
  [[ "$output" == "recorded: review CHANGES_REQUIRED — cycle 1/20, same_issue 1/3, no_progress 0/5" ]]
  local want
  want=$(bash "$VD" --file "$T/a2a/engineer-feedback.md" --gate review --json 2>/dev/null | jq -Sc '{verdict,counts}' | _md5)
  run jq -r '[.state, .triggers.cycle_count.current, .triggers.same_issue.count, .triggers.same_issue.last_hash, (.history | length)] | map(tostring) | join(" ")' "$B"
  [ "$output" = "CLOSED 1 1 $want 0" ]
  [ "$(jq -r .state "$S")" = RUNNING ]
}

@test "RCR-2 the same hash again counts up; a different finding set resets same_issue to 1 with the new last_hash" {
  breaker
  fb engineer-feedback.md review CHANGES_REQUIRED 1
  rr --gate review --file "$T/a2a/engineer-feedback.md"
  rr --gate review --file "$T/a2a/engineer-feedback.md"
  [ "$(jq -r .triggers.same_issue.count "$B")" = 2 ]
  local h1; h1=$(jq -r .triggers.same_issue.last_hash "$B")
  fb engineer-feedback.md review CHANGES_REQUIRED 2
  rr --gate review --file "$T/a2a/engineer-feedback.md"
  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
  [ "$(jq -r .triggers.same_issue.count "$B")" = 1 ]
  [ "$(jq -r .triggers.same_issue.last_hash "$B")" != "$h1" ]
  [ "$(jq -r .triggers.cycle_count.current "$B")" = 3 ]
}

@test "RCR-3 no_progress counts consecutive rounds whose counts are unchanged and resets when they change" {
  breaker '.triggers.same_issue.threshold = 99'
  fb engineer-feedback.md review CHANGES_REQUIRED 1
  rr --gate review --file "$T/a2a/engineer-feedback.md"
  [ "$(jq -r .triggers.no_progress.count "$B")" = 0 ]
  rr --gate review --file "$T/a2a/engineer-feedback.md"
  rr --gate review --file "$T/a2a/engineer-feedback.md"
  [ "$(jq -r .triggers.no_progress.count "$B")" = 2 ]
  fb engineer-feedback.md review CHANGES_REQUIRED 3
  rr --gate review --file "$T/a2a/engineer-feedback.md"
  [ "$(jq -r .triggers.no_progress.count "$B")" = 0 ]
}

@test "RCR-4 a trip at threshold writes state OPEN, appends one history entry, sets .run/state.json HALTED, prints TRIPPED and exits 10" {
  breaker
  fb auditor-sprint-feedback.md audit CHANGES_REQUIRED 1
  rr --gate audit --file "$T/a2a/auditor-sprint-feedback.md"
  rr --gate audit --file "$T/a2a/auditor-sprint-feedback.md"
  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
  rr --gate audit --file "$T/a2a/auditor-sprint-feedback.md"
  [ "$status" -eq 10 ]
  [[ "$output" == *$'\n'"TRIPPED: same_issue: same issue hash "*" seen 3 times in a row" ]]
  run jq -r '[.state, (.history | length), .history[0].trigger, .history[0].gate, .history[0].sprint] | map(tostring) | join(" ")' "$B"
  [ "$output" = "OPEN 1 same_issue audit sprint-1" ]
  [ "$(jq -r '.state + " " + .run_id' "$S")" = "HALTED r" ]
  # a further round on an OPEN breaker still exits 10 and does not duplicate the history entry
  rr --gate audit --file "$T/a2a/auditor-sprint-feedback.md"
  [ "$status" -eq 10 ]
  [ "$(jq -r '.history | length' "$B")" = 1 ]
}

@test "RCR-5 the cycle limit, the no-progress threshold and the timeout trip in that documented order" {
  fb engineer-feedback.md review CHANGES_REQUIRED 1
  breaker '.triggers.same_issue.threshold = 99 | .triggers.cycle_count.current = 19'
  rr --gate review --file "$T/a2a/engineer-feedback.md"
  [ "$status" -eq 10 ]
  [[ "$output" == *"TRIPPED: cycle_count: 20 changes-required rounds reached the limit 20" ]]
  breaker '.triggers.same_issue.threshold = 99 | .triggers.no_progress.count = 4 | .triggers.no_progress.last_counts = "{\"critical\":0,\"high\":0,\"medium\":1,\"low\":0}"'
  rr --gate review --file "$T/a2a/engineer-feedback.md"
  [ "$status" -eq 10 ]
  [[ "$output" == *"TRIPPED: no_progress: "* ]]
  breaker '.triggers.same_issue.threshold = 99 | .triggers.timeout.started = (now - 9 * 3600 | floor | todate)'
  rr --gate review --file "$T/a2a/engineer-feedback.md"
  [ "$status" -eq 10 ]
  [[ "$output" == *"TRIPPED: timeout: run older than 8 hours" ]]
  [ "$(jq -r .history[-1].trigger "$B")" = timeout ]
}

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# =============================================================================
# loa-decisions-surface.sh: SessionStart hook that surfaces pending decision rows.
#
# Prints up to 10 `proposed` then `open` rows of grimoires/loa/decisions.yaml (id, status,
# summary only) so the operator sees what awaits /decisions confirm. DEFAULT-OFF: gated on
# `decisions.surface_at_session_start` (default false) in .loa.config.yaml.
#
# CONTRACT (observability, never a gate; same as loa-kf-surface.sh):
#   - Exits 0 on every path and never blocks a session.
#   - Disabled or no config: prints nothing (read with yq, or a plain-text fallback without it).
#   - Enabled but Mike Farah yq v4 or jq is missing, or the ledger is unreadable or has an
#     unknown schema_version: one "[DECISIONS] WARNING ..." line on stdout.
#   - Enabled and healthy: the block on stdout (SessionStart injects stdout as context);
#     nothing when no row is open or proposed and no marker is stale.
#   - A stale .run/unattended.json (another session, or older than
#     decisions.unattended_marker_ttl_hours, default 24) adds one notice line.
#

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# =============================================================================
# loa-l7-surface-soul.sh — SessionStart hook (cycle-098 Sprint 7B).
#
# At session start, read SOUL.md (project root, descriptive identity doc),
# validate against the L7 schema, and surface the body wrapped in
# sanitize_for_session_start("L7", body) into the session context. Always
# silent (exit 0 with no stdout) when:
#   - soul_identity_doc.enabled is not true in .loa.config.yaml
#   - SOUL.md is missing
#   - the config file is absent or malformed
#   - schema_mode=strict and validation fails (NFR-Sec3 prescriptive
#     rejection or required-section absence)
#
# For enabled, existing files that pass preflight, attempts a soul.surface
# audit event: surfaced | schema-warning | schema-refused. Audit failures
# are non-fatal. Missing files and disabled L7 do not emit audit events.
# The shared payload schema permits file-missing and disabled outcomes for
# other callers; that permissiveness does not promise emission by this hook.
#
# FR-L7-1 (load at session start), FR-L7-2 (warn|strict), FR-L7-4 (cap +
# reference path), FR-L7-5 (single-fire — re-source no-ops via LOA_L7_SURFACED
# env marker), FR-L7-6 (silent on disabled / missing / refused).
#
# Trust boundary: the SOUL.md body is OPERATOR-AUTHORED but UNTRUSTED at
# surfacing. soul_load wraps the body via sanitize_for_session_start("L7",
# body) before reaching session context — never interpret as instructions.
# =============================================================================

set -uo pipefail

HOOK_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
REPO_ROOT="$(cd "${HOOK_DIR}/../../.." && pwd)"
LIB="${REPO_ROOT}/.claude/scripts/lib/soul-identity-lib.sh"
[[ -f "$LIB" ]] || exit 0

# Cache scoped to session — re-source no-ops (FR-L7-5).
[[ "${LOA_L7_SURFACED:-0}" == "1" ]] && exit 0

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Test-mode env-gated path overrides (LOA_SOUL_TEST_CONFIG +
# LOA_SOUL_TEST_PATH). Honored ONLY under bats / LOA_SOUL_TEST_MODE=1 with a
# bats-detected ancestor. Mirrors L4/L6 cycle-098 patterns.
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
_l7_test_mode_active() {
    # cycle-098 sprint-7 cypherpunk CRIT-1 remediation: require BOTH a
    # robust bats marker AND opt-in `LOA_SOUL_TEST_MODE=1`. Mirrors the
    # lib-side gate at .claude/scripts/lib/soul-identity-lib.sh.
    [[ "${LOA_SOUL_TEST_MODE:-0}" == "1" ]] || return 1
    [[ -n "${BATS_TEST_FILENAME:-}" ]] && return 0
    [[ -n "${BATS_VERSION:-}" ]] && return 0
    return 1
}

config_path="${REPO_ROOT}/.loa.config.yaml"
if _l7_test_mode_active && [[ -n "${LOA_SOUL_TEST_CONFIG:-}" ]]; then
    config_path="$LOA_SOUL_TEST_CONFIG"
fi

# Gate on yq availability + config presence.
command -v yq >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 0
[[ -f "$config_path" ]] || exit 0

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# =============================================================================
# loa-kf-surface.sh — SessionStart hook (cycle-115 sprint-1, D1).
#
# Surfaces a compact symptom -> KF table from grimoires/loa/known-failures.md
# at session start so an agent sees the operational-failure log before
# triaging. DEFAULT-OFF: gated on `known_failures.surface_at_session_start`
# (default false) in .loa.config.yaml.
#
# STREAM ROUTING: Claude Code's SessionStart contract injects a hook's STDOUT
#   (on exit 0) into the session as context; STDERR is transcript-only and never
#   reaches the agent. This surface is only useful IN CONTEXT, so every ENABLED
#   path — the healthy table AND the enabled-but-degraded WARNINGs — writes to
#   STDOUT (an agent under the index-first intake contract must SEE that the KF
#   surface is degraded so it falls back to regenerating the index). Sibling
#   surfacing hooks (loa-l6-surface-handoffs.sh, loa-l7-surface-soul.sh) route
#   the same way. The DISABLED path emits nothing at all.
#
# CONTRACT (loud-but-nonblocking — this is OBSERVABILITY, never a gate):
#   - It MUST exit 0 in ALL paths. It MUST NOT block a session.
#   - When the flag is DISABLED (or config/yq absent): emit NOTHING, exit 0.
#   - When ENABLED but the surface is degraded — known-failures.md unreadable,
#     or zero KF entries parsed — emit a visible "[KF-SURFACE] WARNING ..."
#     to STDOUT and exit 0 (loud + in-context, so the agent notices a broken
#     knowledge surface; never silent on an enabled-but-broken path).
#   - When ENABLED and healthy: emit a compact symptom -> KF table to STDOUT,
#     exit 0.
#
# TRUST BOUNDARY: known-failures.md bodies are UNTRUSTED at surfacing. Every
#   field is control-byte-sanitized + length-capped before reaching session
#   context; body prose is NEVER interpreted as instructions (CLAUDE.md
#   agent-network universal invariant).
# =============================================================================
set -uo pipefail

HOOK_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
REPO_ROOT="$(cd "${HOOK_DIR}/../.." && pwd)"

# --- test-mode seam (mirrors L4/L6/L7 cycle-098 gate): the config + path
#     overrides are honored ONLY under LOA_KF_SURFACE_TEST_MODE=1 with a bats
#     marker present. In production neither override is consulted. -----------
_kf_test_mode_active() {
  [[ "${LOA_KF_SURFACE_TEST_MODE:-0}" == "1" ]] || return 1
  [[ -n "${BATS_TEST_FILENAME:-}" ]] && return 0
  [[ -n "${BATS_VERSION:-}" ]] && return 0
  return 1
}

# Sanitize: drop control bytes (keep UTF-8 multibyte), flatten whitespace, cap.
_san() { printf '%s' "${1-}" | tr -d '\000-\010\013\014\016-\037\177' | tr '\t\n\r' '   ' | sed -E 's/  +/ /g; s/^ //; s/ $//' | cut -c1-100; }

# --- resolve enabled flag -----------------------------------------------------
enabled="false"
if _kf_test_mode_active && [[ -n "${LOA_KF_SURFACE_TEST_CONFIG-}" ]]; then
  # In test mode the override stands in for the parsed config value.
  enabled="${LOA_KF_SURFACE_TEST_CONFIG}"
else
  config_path="${REPO_ROOT}/.loa.config.yaml"
  # No yq or no config -> the feature is opt-in and unconfigurable here: silent.
  if command -v yq >/dev/null 2>&1 && [[ -f "$config_path" ]]; then
    # Explicit key, else the loa.profile default (cycle-129 D-9.1).
    # shellcheck source=scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh
    source "${REPO_ROOT}/.claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh" 2>/dev/null &&
      enabled="$(loa_knob known_failures.surface_at_session_start false 2>/dev/null || echo false)"
  fi
fi

# DISABLED (or unconfigurable) -> emit nothing, exit 0. This is the ONLY silent path.
[[ "$enabled" == "true" ]] || exit 0

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# =============================================================================
# loa-l6-surface-handoffs.sh — SessionStart hook (cycle-098 Sprint 6C).
#
# At session start, identify the current operator (via git config user.email
# → OPERATORS.md slug match), then surface any unread L6 handoffs addressed
# to them. Body content is sanitized via context-isolation-lib's
# sanitize_for_session_start("L6", body) before reaching session context.
#
# This hook is silent (exit 0 with no stdout) when:
#   - structured_handoff.enabled is not true in .loa.config.yaml
#   - operator slug cannot be resolved (no git config user.email match)
#   - no unread handoffs for this operator
# =============================================================================

set -uo pipefail

HOOK_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
REPO_ROOT="$(cd "${HOOK_DIR}/../../.." && pwd)"
LIB="${REPO_ROOT}/.claude/scripts/lib/structured-handoff-lib.sh"
[[ -f "$LIB" ]] || exit 0

# Gate on config.
if command -v yq >/dev/null 2>&1 && [[ -f "${REPO_ROOT}/.loa.config.yaml" ]]; then
    # Explicit key, else the loa.profile default (cycle-129 D-9.1).
    enabled="false"
    # shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh
    source "${REPO_ROOT}/.claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh" 2>/dev/null &&
        enabled="$(loa_knob structured_handoff.enabled false 2>/dev/null || echo false)"
    [[ "$enabled" == "true" ]] || exit 0
else
    # No config → silent (the primitive is opt-in).
    exit 0
fi

# Resolve current operator slug from git config.
git_email="$(git -C "$REPO_ROOT" config user.email 2>/dev/null || echo "")"
[[ -n "$git_email" ]] || exit 0

# Source operator-identity to map email → slug. Fall back: skip surfacing.
OI="${REPO_ROOT}/.claude/scripts/operator-identity.sh"
[[ -f "$OI" ]] || exit 0
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "$OI" 2>/dev/null || exit 0

# Find an operator whose declared git_email matches.
OPERATORS_FILE="${LOA_OPERATORS_FILE:-${REPO_ROOT}/grimoires/loa/operators.md}"
[[ -f "$OPERATORS_FILE" ]] || exit 0
operator_slug="$(_oi_parse_yaml_to_json "$OPERATORS_FILE" \
    | jq -r --arg em "$git_email" \
        '.operators[]? | select(.git_email == $em) | .id' \
    | head -n 1)"
[[ -n "$operator_slug" ]] || exit 0

# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "$LIB" 2>/dev/null || exit 0

surface_unread_handoffs "$operator_slug" 2>/dev/null || true
exit 0

content.content:
#!/usr/bin/env bats
# =============================================================================
# Issue #961 K-1 — Karpathy surgical-diff hook
# =============================================================================
# Pins the contract for .claude/hooks/quality/karpathy-surgical-diff-check.sh:
# fires `[karpathy-surgical-warn]` stderr line + trajectory event when the
# session diff accumulator exceeds `karpathy_principles.diff_lines_per_task`,
# while remaining non-blocking (always exits 0) per v1 invariant.
# =============================================================================

setup() {
    REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$BATS_TEST_DIRNAME/../.." && pwd)"
    HOOK="$REPO_ROOT/.claude/hooks/quality/karpathy-surgical-diff-check.sh"
    [[ -x "$HOOK" ]] || skip "hook not executable"
    command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || skip "jq not available"
    command -v yq >/dev/null 2>&1 || skip "yq not available"

    TMP_DIR="$(mktemp -d)"
    # cycle-129 D-4.3: per-task state under KARPATHY_STATE_DIR; with no run in
    # progress (empty LOA_RUN_DIR) the key is the session id.
    export KARPATHY_STATE_DIR="$TMP_DIR/state"
    export KARPATHY_SUMMARY_FILE="$TMP_DIR/summary.json"
    export KARPATHY_LEGACY_STATE="$TMP_DIR/legacy-task-state.jsonl"
    export LOA_RUN_DIR="$TMP_DIR/run"
    export LOA_SESSION_ID="test-session"
    KARPATHY_TASK_STATE="$KARPATHY_STATE_DIR/test-session.jsonl"
    export KARPATHY_TRAJECTORY_DIR="$TMP_DIR/trajectory"
    export LOA_CONFIG_OVERRIDE="$TMP_DIR/config.yaml"

    # Default test config — surgical_diff_warning on, threshold deliberately
    # tiny so we can trip it with a few small Write calls.
    cat > "$LOA_CONFIG_OVERRIDE" <<EOF
karpathy_principles:
  surgical_diff_warning: true
  diff_lines_per_task: 5
  enforce: warn
EOF
}

teardown() {
    rm -rf "$TMP_DIR"
}

_write_input() {
    local content="$1"
    jq -nc --arg c "$content" '{tool_name:"Write", tool_input:{file_path:"/tmp/x.txt", content:$c}}'
}

_edit_input() {
    local new="$1"
    jq -nc --arg n "$new" '{tool_name:"Edit", tool_input:{file_path:"/tmp/x.txt", old_string:"", new_string:$n}}'
}

@test "#961 K-1: hook exits 0 with no stdin (graceful degradation)" {
    run bash -c "echo '' | '$HOOK'"
    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
}

@test "#961 K-1: hook respects surgical_diff_warning:false (no state file written)" {
    cat > "$LOA_CONFIG_OVERRIDE" <<EOF
karpathy_principles:
  surgical_diff_warning: false
EOF
    local input
    input="$(_write_input "line1
line2
line3
line4
line5
line6")"
    run bash -c "echo '$input' | '$HOOK'"
    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
    [ ! -f "$KARPATHY_TASK_STATE" ]
}

@test "#961 K-1: hook accumulates lines across multiple invocations" {
    local input
    input="$(_write_input "a
b
c")"
    run bash -c "echo '$input' | '$HOOK'"
    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
    [ -f "$KARPATHY_TASK_STATE" ]
    local n
    n=$(wc -l < "$KARPATHY_TASK_STATE")
    [ "$n" -eq 1 ]

    # Second invocation appends, doesn't overwrite
    run bash -c "echo '$input' | '$HOOK'"
    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
    n=$(wc -l < "$KARPATHY_TASK_STATE")
    [ "$n" -eq 2 ]
}

@test "#961 K-1: hook emits [karpathy-surgical-warn] when threshold exceeded" {
    # threshold=5 in setup; this content has 7 lines → exceeds on first call
    local content="a
b
c
d
e
f
g"
    local input
    input="$(_write_input "$content")"
    run bash -c "echo '$input' | '$HOOK' 2>&1"
    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
    [[ "$output" == *"[karpathy-surgical-warn]"* ]]
}

@test "#961 K-1: hook exits 0 even when warning fires (non-blocking invariant)" {
    # Even with enforce: block set, v1 hook MUST return 0
    cat > "$LOA_CONFIG_OVERRIDE" <<EOF
karpathy_principles:
  surgical_diff_warning: true
  diff_lines_per_task: 5
  enforce: block
EOF
    local content="a
b
c
d
e
f
g
h
i
j"
    local input
    input="$(_write_input "$content")"
    run bash -c "echo '$input' | '$HOOK' 2>&1"
    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
    # Warning STILL fires (the WARN signal is the v1 deliverable)
    [[ "$output" == *"[karpathy-surgical-warn]"* ]]
}

@test "#961 K-1 NFR-Sec-1: tool_input.content NEVER appears in state or trajectory" {
    # The hook MUST log only line counts + file paths, not the content itself.
    # This regression guard prevents secrets in code snippets from leaking
    # into the per-task state (.run/karpathy-surgical/) or the trajectory file.
    local REDACTED-TEST-SECRET"
    local content="line1
${secret}
line3
line4
line5
line6
line7"
    local input
    input="$(_write_input "$content")"
    run bash -c "echo '$input' | '$HOOK' 2>&1"
    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]

    # Secret MUST NOT appear in state or trajectory
    if [[ -f "$KARPATHY_TASK_STATE" ]]; then
        ! grep -qF "$secret" "$KARPATHY_TASK_STATE"
    fi
    if [[ -d "$KARPATHY_TRAJECTORY_DIR" ]]; then
        ! grep -rqF "$secret" "$KARPATHY_TRAJECTORY_DIR"
    fi
}

#!/usr/bin/env bats
bats_require_minimum_version 1.5.0
# =============================================================================
# tests/unit/guard-yield.bats — cycle-129 Sprint 1 (PRD FR-1 AC-1.2 … AC-1.4,
# SDD D-1.3, D-1.4)
# guard-yield.sh over a fixture audit log and a rotated segment, at a fixed
# --now: replay exclusion (flag, cwd, burst) counted in the header, the
# likely-false-positive heuristic (heredoc, outside-repo cwd, prose class without
# a destructive verb at statement start), day-granular last_real_catch, the
# --check drift gate (0 after generation, 1 after an origin edit, 0 after a
# yield-only change), the --json shape, and no command text or cwd in any output.
# =============================================================================

NOW="2026-10-14T12:00:00Z"

setup() {
  export LOA_AUDIT_REPLAY=1
  ROOT="$(cd "$BATS_TEST_DIRNAME/../.." && pwd -P)"
  GY="$ROOT/.claude/scripts/guard-yield.sh"
  T="$(mktemp -d "${BATS_TEST_TMPDIR:-/tmp}/gyield.XXXXXX")"
  T="$(cd "$T" && pwd -P)"
  mkdir -p "$T/run" "$T/scratch"
  # A temp prefix the fixture controls (the script's own mktemp also uses it).
  export TMPDIR="$T"
  cp "$ROOT/.claude/data/guard-origins.yaml" "$T/origins.yaml"
  cp "$ROOT/.claude/loa/reference/hooks-reference.md" "$T/hooks-reference.md"
  A="$T/audit.jsonl"
  row() {  # ts pattern cwd command [extra-json]
    jq -cn --arg ts "$1" --arg p "$2" --arg cwd "$3" --arg c "$4" --argjson x "${5:-{\}}" \
      '{ts: $ts, tool: "Bash", command: $c, exit_code: 2, cwd: $cwd, model: "claude-test-model", hook: "block-destructive-bash", action: "block", pattern_id: $p, matched: "m"} + $x'
  }
  {
    # live, inside the repo
    row "2026-10-12T08:00:00Z" "FR-SZ2-REDIR" "$ROOT" "cat > .claude/x.md <<'EOF'"$'\n'"hello"$'\n'"EOF"   # complete non-executing heredoc → likely FP (FR-6 classifier via lib/heredoc-classifier.sh)
    row "2026-10-12T09:00:00Z" "P2" "/srv/elsewhere/scratch" "git push --force origin topic"    # outside repo → likely FP
    row "2026-10-12T10:00:00Z" "SP-1" "$ROOT" "br comments add bd-1 'note about spike/x merge'" # prose class, no verb → likely FP
    row "2026-10-13T23:59:00Z" "FR-2-AMBIGUOUS" "$ROOT" "cd sub && rm -rf ./.cache"             # prose class WITH verb → real
    # replays
    row "2026-10-11T08:00:00Z" "P3" "$ROOT" "git reset --hard HEAD~1" '{"replay": true}'        # flag
    row "2026-10-11T09:00:00Z" "P3" "$T/scratch" "git reset --hard HEAD~2"                       # cwd under TMPDIR
    row "2026-10-11T10:00:00Z" "P3" "/home/u/bats-run-42/repo" "git reset --hard HEAD~3"        # cwd /bats-run-
    for s in 00 01 02 03 04 05 06 07 08 09; do                                                  # burst: 10 in one minute
      row "2026-10-09T10:00:${s}Z" "P2" "$ROOT" "git push --force origin main"
    done
    # outside the window
diff --git a/base/tests/unit/guard-yield.bats b/head/tests/unit/guard-yield.bats
index afae0f0..28bdc8e 100644
--- a/base/tests/unit/guard-yield.bats
+++ b/head/tests/unit/guard-yield.bats
@@ -31,7 +31,7 @@ setup() {
   }
   {
     # live, inside the repo
-    row "2026-10-12T08:00:00Z" "FR-SZ2-REDIR" "$ROOT" "cat > .claude/x.md <<'EOF'"            # heredoc → likely FP
+    row "2026-10-12T08:00:00Z" "FR-SZ2-REDIR" "$ROOT" "cat > .claude/x.md <<'EOF'"$'\n'"hello"$'\n'"EOF"   # complete non-executing heredoc → likely FP (FR-6 classifier via lib/heredoc-classifier.sh)
     row "2026-10-12T09:00:00Z" "P2" "/srv/elsewhere/scratch" "git push --force origin topic"    # outside repo → likely FP
     row "2026-10-12T10:00:00Z" "SP-1" "$ROOT" "br comments add bd-1 'note about spike/x merge'" # prose class, no verb → likely FP

#                                  repository; no timestamp, no yield) — --check gates it
#   .run/guard-yield.md, .json     untracked host yield: blocks_30d, likely_fp_30d,
#                                  telemetry_30d, last_real_catch per guard
#   hooks-reference.md table       with --hooks-table, the rows between
#                                  <!-- guard-register:begin --> and <!-- guard-register:end -->
#
# Yield (SDD D-1.3): rows of .run/audit.jsonl and its rotated segments
# .run/audit.jsonl.* with action == "block", plus implement-gate rows (telemetry
# when action is telemetry or ask), with ts inside the window. Replays are
# excluded and counted: replay == true (LOA_AUDIT_REPLAY=1 at the source), or,
# for rows that predate the flag, a cwd under ${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/ or containing
# /bats-run-, /bats., /evals/results/ or /sandbox/, or a UTC minute holding
# BURST_ROWS (10) or more block rows (a suite replaying fixtures into the live
# log from inside the repository; no interactive session blocks ten commands in
# one minute). A block is a likely false
# positive (a heuristic) when its command holds a heredoc (`<<`; or, when
# .claude/scripts/lib/heredoc-classifier.sh defines heredoc_nonexec, a heredoc
# that function calls non-executing), when its cwd lies outside the repository
# (this checkout and its main worktree), or when its pattern id is a prose class
# (SP-1, FR-MERGE-2, FR-2-AMBIGUOUS) with no destructive verb at statement start.
# A real catch is a block that is not a likely false positive.
    --argjson burst_rows "$BURST_ROWS" \
    --arg tmp "$TMP_PREFIX" \
    --arg root "$ROOT" \
    --arg mainroot "$MAIN_ROOT" '
  def epoch: (.ts // .timestamp // null) | if type == "string" then (sub("\\.[0-9]+Z$"; "Z") | try fromdateiso8601 catch null) else null end;
  def under($r): . as $c | ($r != "") and ($c == $r or ($c | startswith($r + "/")));
  def minute: (.ts // .timestamp // "") | tostring | .[0:16];
  def replay($burst): (.replay == true)
    or ((.cwd // "") | type == "string" and (startswith($tmp) or contains("/bats-run-") or contains("/bats.") or contains("/evals/results/") or contains("/sandbox/")))
    or (minute | IN($burst[]));
  def outside_repo: (.cwd // "") as $c | ($c | type == "string") and $c != "" and (($c | under($root)) or ($c | under($mainroot)) | not);
  def verbs: ["rm","git","find","dd","mkfs","shred","truncate","kubectl","terraform","aws","gcloud","psql","mysql","DROP","DELETE","TRUNCATE"];
  def destructive_start: (.command // "") | tostring | [splits("(;|&&|\\|\\||\\||\n)")] | map(sub("^\\s+"; "") | (split("\\s+"; null)[0] // "")) | any(.[]; IN(verbs[]));
  def heredoc: if $nonexec == null then ((.command // "") | tostring | contains("<<")) else (._i | IN($nonexec[])) end;
  def prose_class: (.pattern_id // "") | IN("SP-1", "FR-MERGE-2", "FR-2-AMBIGUOUS");
  def likely_fp: heredoc or outside_repo or (prose_class and (destructive_start | not));
  def day: strftime("%Y-%m-%d");
  def origin_txt: .origin as $o | if ($o.ref | tostring | startswith($o.kind | tostring)) then ($o.ref | tostring) else "\($o.kind) \($o.ref)" end;
  ($hooks | map({key: (.rel | split("/") | last | sub("\\.sh$"; "")), value: .id}) | from_entries) as $hookid
  | ($map.guards | map(.id)) as $known
  | [inputs | select(test("\\S")) | (try fromjson catch null)] as $raw
  | ($raw | to_entries | map(.value as $v | if ($v | type) == "object" then ($v + {_i: .key}) else null end)) as $all
  | ($all | map(select(. != null))) as $rows
  | ($rows | length) as $read
  | ($rows | map(select(.action == "block" or .hook == "implement-gate") | . + {_t: epoch})) as $cand
  | ($cand | map(select(._t != null and ._t >= ($now - $win * 86400) and ._t <= ($now + 86400)))) as $inwin
  | ($inwin | map(select(.action == "block" and .replay != true)) | group_by(minute)
     | map(select(length >= $burst_rows) | .[0] | minute)) as $burst
  | ($inwin | map(select(replay($burst) | not))) as $live
  | ($live | map(
      (if .hook == "block-destructive-bash" then
         ["hook:safety/block-destructive-bash.sh"] + (if ((.pattern_id // "") | tostring | test("^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$")) then ["fence:" + .pattern_id] else [] end)
       elif .hook == "implement-gate" then ["hook:compliance/implement-gate.sh", "gate:implement-gate"]
       elif ((.hook // "") | type) == "string" and $hookid[.hook] != null then [$hookid[.hook]]
       else [] end) as $ids
      | {ids: ($ids | map(select(IN($known[])))),
         block: (.action == "block" or .action == "deny"),
         telemetry: (.action == "telemetry" or .action == "ask"),
         fp: ((.action == "block" or .action == "deny") and likely_fp),
         t: ._t})) as $cls
  | ($cls | map(.ids[]) | unique) as $seen
  | (["hook:safety/block-destructive-bash.sh", "hook:compliance/implement-gate.sh", "gate:implement-gate"]
     + ($map.guards | map(select(.kind == "fence") | .id)) + $seen | unique) as $writers
  | ($map.guards | map(. as $g
      | if ($g.id | IN($writers[])) then
          ($cls | map(select(any(.ids[]; . == $g.id)))) as $mine
          | ($mine | map(select(.block and (.fp | not))) | map(.t) | max) as $last
          | {id, kind, class, status, origin: origin_txt, knob, floor, registrations: (.registrations // []), audited: true,
             blocks_30d: ($mine | map(select(.block)) | length),
             likely_fp_30d: ($mine | map(select(.fp)) | length),
             telemetry_30d: ($mine | map(select(.telemetry)) | length),
             last_real_catch: (if $last == null then "none in window" else ($last | day) end)}
        else
          {id, kind, class, status, origin: origin_txt, knob, floor, registrations: (.registrations // []), audited: false,
           blocks_30d: null, likely_fp_30d: null, telemetry_30d: null, last_real_catch: "n/a"}
        end)) as $guards
  | {
      schema_version: 1,
      generated_at: ($now | day),
      window_days: $win,
      scope: "host",
      audit_segments: $segs,
      audit_rows_read: $read,
      audit_rows_unparseable: (($raw | length) - $read),
      audit_rows_considered: ($inwin | length),
      replay_rows_excluded: (($inwin | length) - ($live | length)),
      replay_rows_by_rule: {
        flag: ($inwin | map(select(.replay == true)) | length),
        cwd: ($inwin | map(select(.replay != true and replay([]))) | length),
        burst: ($inwin | map(select(.replay != true and (replay([]) | not) and replay($burst))) | length)
      },
      heuristic: "likely_fp = heredoc in the command OR cwd outside the repository OR (pattern SP-1, FR-MERGE-2 or FR-2-AMBIGUOUS with no destructive verb at statement start); real = block AND NOT likely_fp",
      totals: {
        guards: ($map.guards | length),
        guards_without_origin: 0,
        dormant: ($map.guards | map(select(.status == "dormant")) | length),
        blocks_30d: ($cls | map(select(.block)) | length),
        real_blocks_30d: ($cls | map(select(.block and (.fp | not))) | length),
        likely_fp_30d: ($cls | map(select(.fp)) | length),
        telemetry_30d: ($cls | map(select(.telemetry)) | length),
        unattributed_30d: ($cls | map(select(.ids | length == 0)) | length)

content.text:
I found six real defects in my focus area. The two most serious: KS-9 and KS-8 in `karpathy-surgical-diff.bats` don't actually check what they claim, and `deny` mode refuses writes during any `/implement` or `/bug` session that runs longer than two hours. I confirmed each finding by running it.

**How I ran it:** I copied the tree to `~/ig-review`, because `/tmp` is mounted noexec. All of `karpathy-surgical-diff.bats` (11/11) and `karpathy-surgical-diff-hook.bats` (6/6) pass, as do the matrix tests IG-24 to IG-33 in `implement-gate.bats` (10/10). IG-1 to IG-23 and `karpathy-trajectory-event.bats` can't run, because the snapshot lacks `tests/fixtures/pretooluse-payloads/` and the trajectory schema. These are snapshot problems, not PR defects: the `local REDACTED-TEST-SECRET"` lines at `karpathy-surgical-diff.bats:165` and `karpathy-surgical-diff-hook.bats:141` are a syntax error from redaction, and exec bits were dropped. I patched both in my copy only.

## Findings, by severity

**1. High (test defect): KS-9 can't fail.** `pr/head/tests/unit/karpathy-surgical-diff.bats:173`
- `! grep -rqF "$secret" …` is not the last line of the test. bats runs under `set -e`, which never fires on a negated command, so this assertion is skipped.
- Evidence: I changed the hook to append the whole payload, content included, into the state and trajectory directories. KS-9 still passed, and `grep` found the secret in `st/leak.txt` and `tr/leak.jsonl`.
- So the content-never-leaks guarantee (NFR-Sec-1) has no working test for the new layout.
- The same pre-existing pattern makes the state-file half of `karpathy-surgical-diff-hook.bats:155-157` a no-op too.

**2. Medium-high (test defect): KS-8 can't detect the noise it is named for.** `karpathy-surgical-diff.bats:153`, `:154`, `:158`
- Lines like `[ -z "$output" ] && [ -z "$stderr" ]` sit mid-test. `set -e` ignores a failure in any part of an `&&` list except the last, so when the first check fails nothing is reported.
- Evidence: I changed the knob-off path to create `$KARPATHY_STATE_DIR`, print to stdout and print to stderr. KS-8 still passed.

**3. Medium (logic): `deny` refuses writes in long `/implement` or `/bug` sessions.** `pr/head/.claude/hooks/compliance/implement-gate.sh:550`, plus `read_position` at `:558-569` and the deny branch at `:628-634`
- The marker only counts for 7200 s after `started_at`.
- `run-checkpoint.sh mark` (`pr/head/.claude/scripts/run-checkpoint.sh:537-541`) writes `started_at` once, and also runs `derive --write`, which refreshes `derived_at` whenever `.run/sprint-plan-state.json` exists.
- The skills call `mark` only once, at the start (`implementing-tasks/SKILL.md:229`, `bug-triaging/SKILL.md:435`).
- Result: a direct `/implement` (no `/run`) in a repo that still has an old cache gets a known, non-RUNNING position. From two to twelve hours after `mark`, every App Zone write is denied mid-implementation.
- Matrix cell `deny` + `marker_stale` + fresh cache → deny (IG-27, passing) confirms this is the behaviour.

**4. Medium (behaviour vs docs): the surgical-diff key is the last closed task, not the current one, and it doesn't fall back to the session after a run ends.** `pr/head/.claude/hooks/quality/karpathy-surgical-diff-check.sh:129-137` (header `:10-14`)
- The key comes from `run-checkpoint.sh read --json` → `.checkpoint.task`. That field holds the last closed bead (`state-schemas.md:107`), and the checkpoint is written right after `br close` (`implementing-tasks/SKILL.md:211`).
- So `.run/karpathy-surgical/<bead>.jsonl` holds the next task's lines, and the first task's lines go under `sprint-N`. The review's SURGICAL check reads `<bead>.jsonl` (`reviewing-code/SKILL.md:220`), so it gets the wrong task's lines.
- Nothing checks that a run is in progress. Evidence: with a `JACKED_OUT` cache whose checkpoint is `bd-last`, three different session ids each wrote 40 lines. All went to `bd-last.jsonl` (totals 40, 80, 120) and the third warned.
- This contradicts the header and KS-2 ("with no run in progress the key is the session id").

**5. Low-medium (regression from base): a stale `derived_at` hides fresh simstim and state.json runs.** `implement-gate.sh:509-512`
- In `check_implementation_active`, a `.run/sprint-plan-state.json` whose `derived_at` is older than `stale_hours` now returns 1 immediately. It no longer falls through to `simstim-state.json` / `state.json`.
- Evidence (`~/ig-review/scen.sh`): sprint-plan cache COMPLETE with fresh `last_activity` and `derived_at` 13 h old, plus a fresh `simstim-state.json` with phase `implementation`. Base allows; head asks. This is the default `ask` mode.

**6. Low (docs contradict code).** `pr/head/.claude/loa/reference/hooks-reference.md:248`, `:252-258`
- The doc says "the legacy state files below keep sanctioning as before".
- The table lists only `last_activity` freshness for `sprint-plan-state.json` and `state.json`. The code also requires `derived_at` (when present) to be within `run_mode.stale_hours` for both files (`:510`, `:536`), and finding 5 shows the old fall-through is gone.
- Line 248 calls sanctioned_run "a derived RUNNING cache with a fresh derived_at", but code also sanctions caches with no `derived_at` at all.

## Checked and found sound
- **implement-gate:** the jq expressions (`_ig_within`, the marker check, `log_model_signal`, `log_gate_row`) and the yq/jq config loader. Also the deny/ask JSON shape, the trust-input path including `implement-active.json`, `--effective-mode`, replay tagging, and the claims tighten-only logic.
- **The four session-start hooks:** `loa_knob` handles explicit-over-profile precedence correctly. I smoke-tested `loa-kf-surface.sh` with the `full` profile, `full` with an explicit false, an explicit true, and an empty config.
- **One possible issue I couldn't test:** `profile-lib.sh` uses only Mike Farah yq syntax (`yq -o=json`). On a python-yq host, explicit `true` enables in the session-start hooks would read as false; base's `yq '.x // false'` worked there. No python yq was installed to confirm.

Try each source in priority order; use the first that returns non-empty:

content.text:
I found two High, one Medium and four Low defects in `run-checkpoint.sh` and the run-mode docs.

**How I checked:** I built the PR tree from upstream commit `40df53ed`, which matches `pr/head` byte-for-byte for these files. I ran it under the container's jq 1.6 and under jq 1.7.1, which I downloaded to `~/rcbin`.
- **jq 1.6:** 20 of the 22 derive tests fail, and RCR-7 fails.
- **jq 1.7.1:** everything passes except RCD-R5. RCD-R5 depends on `loa-status.sh` showing its workflow-state section, which my extracted tree doesn't trigger, so I treat it as environment-related, not a finding.

## High

**1. `derive` doesn't compile on jq 1.6 because `$label` is a reserved word there.**
`pr/head/.claude/scripts/run-checkpoint.sh:378-380, 389`
- **Evidence:** `jq -n --arg label x '$label'` on jq 1.6 gives `syntax error, unexpected label, expecting IDENT`; jq 1.7 accepts it.
- **Effect on `derive`:** it exits 3 for every ledger with at least one sprint. The SDD (`grimoires/loa/sdd.md:159`) says "jq 1.6+", and Debian 12 and Ubuntu 22.04 still ship 1.6.
- **Effect on `write`:** it swallows the error (lines 174-176) and returns 0. Every checkpoint prints jq compile errors plus a misleading "`sprint-plan-state.json` is not valid JSON — not written" (from `atomic_update`). The breaker file still gets written, but the run state is never derived.
- **Knock-on:** the implement gate, `/loa` drift and the run-resume drift check all lose the derived position.
- **Why CI misses it:** `ubuntu-latest` ships jq 1.7.
- **Fix:** rename the variable (e.g. `$lbl`). With that rename, 1.6 gets down to only the failures in finding 2.

**2. Feedback files without a trailer (legacy files) crash `fb_parse` on jq 1.6.**
`pr/head/.claude/scripts/run-checkpoint.sh:223, 226`
- **Cause:** the guard `jq -e 'type == "object"' <<<"$pj"` is meant to catch empty input. On jq 1.6, `-e` with no output exits 0 (jq 1.7 exits 4), so `pj` stays `""` and `--argjson p ""` fails ("invalid JSON text passed to --argjson"). The same applies to `vj` at line 223 when `verdict-derive.sh` prints nothing.
- **Effect:** `record-round` on a legacy file exits 2 (RCR-7 fails). `derive` aborts on any sprint with a legacy feedback file (RCD-3 fails).
- **Breaker fails open:** `SKILL.md:110` and `:131-135` only handle exit 10, so a round that errors out is silently not counted.

## Medium

**3. A new run trips the breaker at its first checkpoint from an earlier run's feedback history.**
`pr/head/.claude/scripts/run-checkpoint.sh:276-280, 303-311, 412-414`
- **Cause:** `recompute` counts every round in the active sprint's a2a directory. The only cutoff is `reset_at`, which only `/run-resume --reset-ice` writes (`halt-resume.md:81`).
- **The run-start breaker has no `reset_at`:** `SKILL.md:91-92` writes the `state-schemas.md:46` breaker verbatim, and that schema has none.
- **Reproduction (jq 1.7):**

content.text:
I found one real regression in the focus area and four low-severity issues. The generator, the regenerated `constraints.json`, the kernel hash, the CI workflow and the budget constants all check out.

**How I verified:** `pr/head` holds only the 68 touched files, so the scripts can't run there on their own. Upstream commit `40df53ed` (the feat commit for this PR) is byte-identical to `pr/head` for every file except two karpathy bats files that aren't in scope, so I ran everything against a full checkout of it and of its parent (the base). `/tmp` is mounted noexec, so those checkouts lived briefly under `$HOME`; I deleted them afterwards. Nothing under `/workspace/pr` was modified.

## Findings (by severity)

### 1. MEDIUM: the review and audit skills now prescribe a shell command their own grants refuse (existing test now fails)
- **Where:**
  - `pr/head/.claude/skills/reviewing-code/SKILL.md:69` and `:297`
  - `pr/head/.claude/skills/auditing-security/SKILL.md:67` and `:285`
  - The source text is in `pr/head/.claude/data/skill-includes/input_guardrails.md:3` and `pr/head/.claude/data/skill-includes/retrospective_postlude.md:1`.
- **What changed:** the rewritten shared blocks used to read `.loa.config.yaml`. They now tell the skill to run `.claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh knob guardrails.input.enabled false` and `... knob invisible_retrospective.enabled`.
- **Why it breaks:** both skills set `deny_raw_shell: true` (`reviewing-code/SKILL.md:39`, `auditing-security/SKILL.md:35`). Neither grants `Bash(.claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh knob *)`, in `allowed-tools` (line 6) or in `capabilities.execute_commands.allowed`.
- **Consequence:** under review and audit, the profile check either stalls or is refused. A refused check means "does not print true", so the guardrails and the retrospective step are silently skipped.
- **Evidence:** test CMP-188 in `tests/unit/adversarial-review-companion.bats` (line 4282) passes on base and fails on head:
  `reviewing-code: '.claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh knob guardrails.input.enabled false' is prescribed but no Bash grant admits it`
  The same failure is reported for the retrospective knob and for auditing-security. Upstream later fixed exactly this in `77455afb`.

### 2. LOW: negated assertions in the new bats file can't fail
- **Where:** `pr/head/tests/unit/lint-invariants.bats:59`, `:68`, `:69`, `:126`
- **Why:** bats does not fail a test on `! cmd` unless it is the test's last command. I confirmed this with bats 1.13 (`! true` followed by `echo` passes).
- **Which lines are dead:** LI-2 line 59 (heading absent from the live kernel), LI-3 lines 68–69, and LI-8 line 126, the "no agent_teams ERROR" check. That check is already admitted to be load-bearing by the comment at 127–128.
- **Which still work:** line 60 and line 95 are the last commands of their tests, so they count.
- **Impact:** other assertions in the same tests (the diff at 74–76, the PASS-message check at 125) happen to cover these cases today, so the damage is limited to coverage. Upstream later rewrote these as `run` plus a status check (LOW-8 in `77455afb`).

### 3. LOW: the lint's suggested fix doesn't work for a leftover heading with no marker
- **Where:** `pr/head/.claude/scripts/lint-invariants.sh:241-243` and `pr/head/.claude/scripts/generate-constraints.sh:169-172`
- **The mismatch:** the lint raises an ERROR when the class has no rows and *either* the marker or the `## Agent Teams` heading is present, and says "run generate-constraints.sh". `prune_optional_table`, though, does nothing whenever the start marker is missing.
- **Reproduced:** I left the heading and table header in the kernel with no marker block and ran the generator. It reported "Generation complete" and the heading was still there. The lint kept erroring with the same advice.

### 4. LOW: two retrospective docs give different fallbacks for the same knob
- **Where:** `pr/head/.claude/data/skill-includes/retrospective_postlude.md:1` (rendered into every SKILL.md that uses it) versus `pr/head/.claude/skills/continuous-learning/resources/retrospective-postlude.md:34`
- **The conflict:** the shared block calls `knob invisible_retrospective.enabled` with no fallback, so the fallback is empty. The resource says the effective value is `knob invisible_retrospective.enabled true`.
- **When it matters:** when profiles can't be resolved (`profiles.yaml` missing or unreadable, or yq/jq absent) and the key isn't set explicitly. The block then prints an empty string and the retrospective is skipped, while the resource says it runs.

### 5. LOW: the exit-code test no longer checks exit 0
- **Where:** `pr/head/.claude/scripts/test-lint-invariants.sh:257` and `:320`
- **What:** both "good fixture" checks, including the one labelled "exit 0 = all pass", now accept 0 or 1. Nothing in the suite asserts that the all-pass case returns 0 any more, so a lint that downgraded every PASS to WARN would go unnoticed.

## Checked and correct
- **constraints.json:** the five C-TEAM rows are gone and no other constraint references them.
- **Generator and validator:** `generate-constraints.sh` is idempotent on the head tree (no diff), and `validate-constraints.sh` reports 0 errors and 0 warnings.
- **Kernel:** the `@loa-managed` hash in `CLAUDE.loa.md` verifies, and the file is 9,189 B against the new 9,445 B cap.
- **Prompt budget:** the constants in `check-prompt-budget.sh`, the PB-10 header comment and the workflow agree. The over/under sentinel fixtures still give exit 1 and exit 0, and the workflow has no path filter, so it runs on every PR.
- **Keep-list:** the new K-07 pattern `^## Rules and arming$` matches `agent-teams-reference.md:32`.
- **Shared blocks:** `generate-skill-includes.sh --check` reports all blocks current.
- **Rationales:** IDR-3 finds the C-TEAM rationales word-for-word in the reference table.
- **Commands the run-mode docs rely on:** the `run-checkpoint.sh` subcommands (`mark`, `unmark`, `record-round`, `derive --json` with `.drift` and `.cache_state`) exist.
- **Tool-strip check:** the new pure-review check in `validate-skill-capabilities.sh` reads an explicit `false` correctly and accepts both the list and comma-string forms.
- **Failures are not new:** every other test failure I saw also fails on base. They come from this environment (jq 1.6, mawk, the yq build), not from the PR.

head/.claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh:624 — FR-6 fail-open regression: `_bdb_hd_same_line_exec` only flags a segment whose own tokens equal the target basename and whose command word is not a "safe reader", so a heredoc written to a plain file and executed in the same command via a safe reader is classified `nonexec` and its body dropped. Verified: `cat > notes <<EOF\necho pwn > .claude/settings.json\nEOF\ncat notes | sh` and `…\nsh -c "$(cat notes)"` exit 0 on head, exit 2 on base (the `cat` segment is a safe reader, the `sh` segment does not name the file, and a quoted `"$(cat notes)"` token never equals the basename). The header claim at :155 that a target named elsewhere is caught does not hold.
head/.claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh:310 — `_bdb_hd_exec_dest` treats only script extensions, rc files and hook/bin paths as executable, so files run implicitly by a later word in the same command pass as plain: `cat > Makefile <<EOF\nall:\n\tcp evil .claude/hooks/x.sh\nEOF\nmake` exits 0 on head (FR-SZ2 COPY was blocked on base). The same applies to package.json + `npm run`, justfile, Rakefile and similar. The "documented gap" at :175 only covers LATER commands, not the same one.
head/.claude/scripts/run-checkpoint.sh:378 — `derive` binds `--arg label` and uses `$label` in the jq program; `label` is a reserved keyword in jq 1.6 (`jq -n --arg label x '$label'` → "syntax error, unexpected label", verified on this host). `derive` exits 3 for every ledger with a sprint, and `write` swallows the error, so the run position is never derived on jq 1.6 hosts (Debian 12, Ubuntu 22.04). Rename the variable.
head/.claude/scripts/run-checkpoint.sh:226 — The `jq -e 'type == "object"' <<<"$pj" || pj='{}'` guard does not fire on empty input under jq 1.6 (`-e` with no output exits 0, verified), so a legacy feedback file with no trailer leaves `pj=""` and the later `--argjson p ""` aborts. `record-round` exits 2 and `derive` fails, and the skill only handles exit 10, so the breaker fails open. The same applies to `vj` at :223 when verdict-derive prints nothing.
head/.claude/scripts/run-checkpoint.sh:276 — Breaker recompute counts every feedback round in the sprint's a2a directory, and the only cutoff is `reset_at`, which the run-start breaker (state-schemas.md / run-mode SKILL.md) never writes. A fresh `/run` over a sprint with old CHANGES_REQUIRED rounds trips the breaker OPEN and turns the state HALTED at its first `write --phase IMPLEMENT`, yet `write` still returns 0.
head/.claude/skills/reviewing-code/SKILL.md:69 — The shared guardrails/retrospective blocks now tell the skill to run `.claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh knob …`, but the skill has `deny_raw_shell: true` and no `Bash(.claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh knob *)` grant in allowed-tools or capabilities. The check is refused, which reads as "not true", so input guardrails and the retrospective (:297) are silently skipped. This breaks the existing grant-coverage test (CMP-188).
head/.claude/skills/auditing-security/SKILL.md:67 — Same as above for auditing-security (deny_raw_shell, no grant for the profile-lib knob command); it also applies to the retrospective block at :285.
head/.claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh:233 — The cache fast path returns `.knobs[$k].value` from `.run/effective-config.json` whenever the id matches. The id is only path|mtime|size and can be recomputed, and the floor filter is not re-applied, so editing a `.run/` file (which implement-gate allows silently, unlike `.loa.config.yaml`) overrides explicit config such as `guardrails.danger_level.enforce: true` or `implement_gate.mode: deny`.
head/.claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh:77 — On GNU, `stat -Lc` exits non-zero when any one input (for example floor.yaml) is missing. The fallback `stat -Lf` then means "filesystem status" on GNU, so the cache id carries no file mtimes and a stale cache is served after the config changes (verified: switching to `loa.profile: full` still yielded standard until the cache was deleted). A missing floor file also silently disables the floor filter.
head/.claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh:61 — `LOA_PROFILE_CONFIG_FILE`, `LOA_PROFILES_FILE`, `LOA_PROFILE_FLOOR_FILE`, `LOA_PROFILE_ROOT` and `LOA_PROFILE_CACHE_FILE` are honoured in production, unlike `LOA_STATUS_CONFIG_FILE`, which is bats-gated a few lines above. For example, `LOA_PROFILE_FLOOR_FILE=/dev/null` disables the safety floor, and a config override redirects the guardrail and danger-level readers.
head/.claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh:46 — The root is resolved with `pwd -P`, but callers compute REPO_ROOT without resolving symlinks. In a symlinked `.claude/scripts` layout the library reads a non-existent config and returns profile defaults (for example `danger_level.enforce` false despite an explicit true), which regresses danger-level-enforcer's previous direct read.
head/.loa.config.yaml.example:21 — The docs say `lean` turns all profile knobs off and `full` all on, but the example (what a fresh install copies) explicitly sets 8 of the 9 profile keys, and explicit keys win, so `loa.profile` is effectively inert on a fresh install. This repeats the "inert control" problem the sprint claims to fix, and profile-lib.bats PL-4 locks it in.
head/.claude/data/profiles.yaml:42 — `standard: invisible_retrospective.enabled: true` silently flips the retrospective on for any config that does not set the key, including this repo's own `.loa.config.yaml`. The oracle records `empty_config_today: false`, and the header at :12-15 lists only the two guardrail keys as changed defaults.
head/.claude/hooks/compliance/implement-gate.sh:550 — `implement-active.json` counts only for 7200 s after `started_at`, and `mark` is written once at skill start. In `deny` mode, a direct `/implement` or `/bug` running longer than 2 h in a repo with a stale non-RUNNING cache has every App Zone write denied mid-task.
head/.claude/hooks/compliance/implement-gate.sh:510 — A sprint-plan-state.json whose `derived_at` is older than stale_hours now returns 1 immediately instead of falling through to simstim-state.json / state.json. A fresh simstim implementation run that the base allowed is now asked in the default mode, a regression the docs (hooks-reference.md:248 "legacy state files keep sanctioning as before") deny.
head/.claude/hooks/quality/karpathy-surgical-diff-check.sh:130 — The surgical-diff key is `.checkpoint.task`, the last CLOSED bead, not the current task, so each task's lines are filed under the previous bead and reviewing-code's SURGICAL check reads the wrong task. There is also no in-progress check: after a run ends, every later session keeps accumulating into the last bead's file, which contradicts the header (:10-14) and KS-2 ("no run in progress → session id").
head/tests/unit/karpathy-surgical-diff.bats:173 — `! grep -rqF "$secret" …` is not the last command, so bats never fails on it. KS-9's no-content-leak assertion is a no-op (verified: a hook that writes the payload into state and trajectory still passes).
head/tests/unit/karpathy-surgical-diff.bats:153 — The `[ -z "$output" ] && [ -z "$stderr" ]` checks sit mid-test inside an `&&` list, so a failure is ignored under bats' `set -e`. KS-8 cannot detect knob-off noise or state creation.
head/tests/unit/lint-invariants.bats:59 — Negated `! grep` assertions mid-test (:59, :68-69, :126) cannot fail under bats, so these checks are dead.
head/.claude/scripts/test-lint-invariants.sh:257 — The "exit 0 = all pass" check now accepts 0 or 1 (likewise :320), so nothing asserts that a clean fixture exits 0 any more.
head/.claude/scripts/lint-invariants.sh:241 — The lint errors when the `## Agent Teams` heading is present without rows and advises running generate-constraints.sh, but `prune_optional_table` (generate-constraints.sh:169) does nothing without the start marker, so the advice cannot fix a marker-less leftover heading.
head/.claude/data/skill-includes/retrospective_postlude.md:1 — `knob invisible_retrospective.enabled` is called with no fallback (empty), while continuous-learning/resources/retrospective-postlude.md:34 documents the fallback as `true`. When profiles cannot be resolved, the shared block skips the retrospective that the resource says runs.
head/.claude/skills/run-mode/resources/halt-resume.md:49 — The doc says resume reads "the file-derived position", but `derive --write` rewrites only sprint-plan-state.json and the breaker, while the steps below read `.run/state.json`; for `/run sprint-N`, `--write` is a no-op.
head/.claude/scripts/run-checkpoint.sh:463 — `.schema_version = (.schema_version // 2)` silently upgrades a v1 (field-less) file to 2, contradicting ":47 schema_version kept" and state-schemas.md:115; RCD-11's title says the opposite of what it asserts.
head/.claude/scripts/loa-status.sh:960 — The Profile line is printed with `echo -e`, which re-interprets `\e` / `\c` sequences in config override values after profile-lib stripped raw control characters (terminal escape injection, line truncation).
Verdict: CHANGES_REQUIRED

head/.claude/skills/reviewing-code/SKILL.md:69 — The shared guardrails/retrospective blocks now tell the skill to run `.claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh knob …`, but the skill has `deny_raw_shell: true` and no `Bash(.claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh knob *)` grant in allowed-tools or capabilities. head/.claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh:233 — The cache fast path returns `.knobs[$k].value` from `.run/effective-config.json` whenever the id matches. The id is only path|mtime|size and can be recomputed, and the floor filter is not re-applied, so editing a `.run/` file (which implement-gate allows silently, unlike `.loa.config.yaml`) overrides explicit config such as `guardrails.danger_level.enforce: true` or `implement_gate.mode: deny`.

The fallback `stat -Lf` then means "filesystem status" on GNU, so the cache id carries no file mtimes and a stale cache is served after the config changes (verified: switching to `loa.profile: full` still yielded standard until the cache was deleted). A missing floor file also silently disables the floor filter.
head/.claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh:61 — `LOA_PROFILE_CONFIG_FILE`, `LOA_PROFILES_FILE`, `LOA_PROFILE_FLOOR_FILE`, `LOA_PROFILE_ROOT` and `LOA_PROFILE_CACHE_FILE` are honoured in production, unlike `LOA_STATUS_CONFIG_FILE`, which is bats-gated a few lines above. For example, `LOA_PROFILE_FLOOR_FILE=/dev/null` disables the safety floor, and a config override redirects the guardrail and danger-level readers.
head/.claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh:46 — The root is resolved with `pwd -P`, but callers compute REPO_ROOT without resolving symlinks. In a symlinked `.claude/scripts` layout the library reads a non-existent config and returns profile defaults (for example `danger_level.enforce` false despite an explicit true), which regresses danger-level-enforcer's previous direct read.
head/.loa.config.yaml.example:21 — The docs say `lean` turns all profile knobs off and `full` all on, but the example (what a fresh install copies) explicitly sets 8 of the 9 profile keys, and explicit keys win, so `loa.profile` is effectively inert on a fresh install. This repeats the "inert control" problem the sprint claims to fix, and profile-lib.bats PL-4 locks it in.
head/.claude/data/profiles.yaml:42 — `standard: invisible_retrospective.enabled: true` silently flips the retrospective on for any config that does not set the key, including this repo's own `.loa.config.yaml`. The oracle records `empty_config_today: false`, and the header at :12-15 lists only the two guardrail keys as changed defaults.
head/.claude/hooks/compliance/implement-gate.sh:550 — `implement-active.json` counts only for 7200 s after `started_at`, and `mark` is written once at skill start. In `deny` mode, a direct `/implement` or `/bug` running longer than 2 h in a repo with a stale non-RUNNING cache has every App Zone write denied mid-task.
head/.claude/hooks/compliance/implement-gate.sh:510 — A sprint-plan-state.json whose `derived_at` is older than stale_hours now returns 1 immediately instead of falling through to simstim-state.json / state.json. A fresh simstim implementation run that the base allowed is now asked in the default mode, a regression the docs (hooks-reference.md:248 "legacy state files keep sanctioning as before") deny.
head/.claude/hooks/quality/karpathy-surgical-diff-check.sh:130 — The surgical-diff key is `.checkpoint.task`, the last CLOSED bead, not the current task, so each task's lines are filed under the previous bead and reviewing-code's SURGICAL check reads the wrong task. There is also no in-progress check: after a run ends, every later session keeps accumulating into the last bead's file, which contradicts the header (:10-14) and KS-2 ("no run in progress → session id").
head/tests/unit/karpathy-surgical-diff.bats:173 — `! grep -rqF "$secret" …` is not the last command, so bats never fails on it. KS-9's no-content-leak assertion is a no-op (verified: a hook that writes the payload into state and trajectory still passes).
head/tests/unit/karpathy-surgical-diff.bats:153 — The `[ -z "$output" ] && [ -z "$stderr" ]` checks sit mid-test inside an `&&` list, so a failure is ignored under bats' `set -e`. KS-8 cannot detect knob-off noise or state creation.
head/tests/unit/lint-invariants.bats:59 — Negated `! grep` assertions mid-test (:59, :68-69, :126) cannot fail under bats, so these checks are dead.
head/.claude/scripts/test-lint-invariants.sh:257 — The "exit 0 = all pass" check now accepts 0 or 1 (likewise :320), so nothing asserts that a clean fixture exits 0 any more.
head/.claude/scripts/lint-invariants.sh:241 — The lint errors when the `## Agent Teams` heading is present without rows and advises running generate-constraints.sh, but `prune_optional_table` (generate-constraints.sh:169) does nothing without the start marker, so the advice cannot fix a marker-less leftover heading.
head/.claude/data/skill-includes/retrospective_postlude.md:1 — `knob invisible_retrospective.enabled` is called with no fallback (empty), while continuous-learning/resources/retrospective-postlude.md:34 documents the fallback as `true`. When profiles cannot be resolved, the shared block skips the retrospective that the resource says runs.
head/.claude/skills/run-mode/resources/halt-resume.md:49 — The doc says resume reads "the file-derived position", but `derive --write` rewrites only sprint-plan-state.json and the breaker, while the steps below read `.run/state.json`; for `/run sprint-N`, `--write` is a no-op.
head/.claude/scripts/run-checkpoint.sh:463 — `.schema_version = (.schema_version // 2)` silently upgrades a v1 (field-less) file to 2, contradicting ":47 schema_version kept" and state-schemas.md:115; RCD-11's title says the opposite of what it asserts.
head/.claude/scripts/loa-status.sh:960 — The Profile line is printed with `echo -e`, which re-interprets `\e` / `\c` sequences in config override values after profile-lib stripped raw control characters (terminal escape injection, line truncation).
Verdict: CHANGES_REQUIRED

content.text:
I've written the review to `/workspace/review.md`: 25 findings and **Verdict: CHANGES_REQUIRED**. Nothing under `pr/` was changed.

**What blocks the merge:**

- **The new heredoc classifier opens a hole in the destructive-command fence.** If a command writes a heredoc to a plain file and then runs that file through a "safe reader" in the same command (`cat notes | sh`, `sh -c "$(cat notes)"`), the body is never scanned. A Makefile followed by `make` slips through the same way. I ran these against both versions: blocked on base, allowed on head.
- **`run-checkpoint.sh` fails on jq 1.6**, which Debian 12 and Ubuntu 22.04 still ship. One jq variable is named `$label`, a reserved word in 1.6, so `derive` fails to compile. Separately, a guard against empty input doesn't fire under 1.6, so old feedback files without a trailer abort `record-round` and the circuit breaker fails open. I reproduced both on this host's jq 1.6.
- **A fresh `/run` can halt at its first checkpoint.** The breaker counts feedback rounds left over from earlier runs, so it trips immediately on a sprint with old "changes required" rounds.
- **The review and audit skills now call a command they aren't allowed to run.** They're told to run `profile-lib.sh knob …`, but they forbid raw shell and don't grant that command. The call is refused, so input guardrails and the retrospective are silently skipped. An existing test (CMP-188) goes from passing to failing.
- **Profiles:**
  - Editing the cache file `.run/effective-config.json` overrides explicit safety settings.
  - The cache can serve stale values when an input file such as `floor.yaml` is missing.
  - Test-only environment variables work in production; one of them can switch off the safety floor.
  - `loa.profile` does almost nothing for a config copied from the example, because the example sets 8 of the 9 profile keys itself.
- **Implement gate:**
  - In `deny` mode, `/implement` or `/bug` sessions longer than two hours get every write refused (in a repo holding an old run-state file).
  - A stale run-state file now stops the check before it reaches a fresh simstim run, which base allowed.
- **Surgical-diff check:** it files each task's lines under the previous task.

The lower-severity findings are test assertions that can't fail (a `! grep` that isn't the test's last line is ignored by bats), docs that contradict the code, and an `echo -e` escape-injection issue in `/loa`.

Two of the reviewer agents I ran in parallel went outside the sandbox. They cloned the upstream `0xHoneyJar/loa` repository from GitHub and downloaded a jq 1.7.1 binary, to run tests the frozen `pr/` tree couldn't support. They found that upstream commit `40df53ed` matches `pr/head` byte-for-byte for the files they checked, and ran tests against it. Every finding cites lines in `pr/head`. I personally re-ran the fence bypasses, both jq 1.6 failures and the skill-grant mismatch; the rest come from those reviewers' runs and reading.

Some tests couldn't run here. The `pr/` snapshot holds only the 68 touched files, so fixtures and dependencies are missing.
